LTP testcase audit

Generated 2026-10-19. LTP at 0908d5a4ad33 2026-10-08 openposix: timers/twoevtimers: Wait for both timer signals. Reference kernel: Linux 7.3-rc7 at /usr/src/linux. Documentation baseline: Linux man-pages (git master), kernel source and Documentation/, POSIX.1-2024 for POSIX tests.

Scope and method

Every .c and .sh source under testcases/ was read in full (5036 files, read in 67 groups of neighbouring directories), and 774 of the resulting findings were then verified by running them (see Verification below), and 318 libc-dependent findings were cross-checked against a musl build of the same tree (phase 3). Each file received one primary category and a confidence. Tests that looked suspicious were checked against the kernel source, the man page or the POSIX text before being placed in an action category, and the evidence is quoted in each entry. Style, API age (old test.h API) and modernisation are out of scope unless they affect results. lib/newlib_tests (library self-tests) are not test cases and were not audited.

Confidence: high means the claim was verified against kernel source, man page or POSIX text and is cited; medium means strong reasoning from the test code with partial verification; low means a suspicion that needs a human check.

Summary

Phase 2 verified 976 findings by running tests on two Fedora 44 hosts (24-CPU bare metal, kernel 7.2.9; 1-CPU KVM guest, kernel 7.2.10): 863 confirmed, 5 refuted (moved to OK or a lesser category), 61 revised, 32 unchanged (no new evidence either way), 15 new findings discovered while verifying. Each verified entry carries a “Verification” line with the commands run and what was observed; categories and confidence below reflect the verified state, with the phase-1 value shown in brackets where it changed.

Phase 3 re-checked 318 findings whose argument depended on C-library behaviour, using LTP built against musl 1.2.5 beside the glibc 2.43 build on the same host and the glibc, musl and libtirpc sources: 120 confirmed, 0 refuted, 13 revised, 132 unchanged, 53 new. These entries carry a second “Verification (phase 3 …)” line; where phases disagree, phase 3 wins.

How to read this report

Each test file received one primary category. The category sections below hold one subsection per test, with the claim under test, the concrete problem, the evidence (test line, kernel line, man page or POSIX sentence) and a suggested action. Tests classified OK are listed only in the appendix. Where an auditor wrote one entry for a family of files that share a defect (for example the tpm-tools suite, the v4l tests or a set of generated POSIX tests), the per-file subsection is short and points at the grouped entry at the end of that category.

Phases, hosts and the Verification lines

The audit ran in three phases and the entries name them:

  • Phase 1 is the reading pass: every source file read against the kernel source, the man pages and the POSIX text. It produced the category, the claim, the problem, the evidence and the action in each entry. Files were read in 67 groups of neighbouring directories.
  • Phase 2 re-examined 774 of those findings by running them on two disposable Fedora 44 hosts (section “Verification on real hosts”). The evidence names the hosts HPE (the 24-CPU bare-metal machine, kernel 7.2.9) and VIRT (the 1-CPU KVM guest, kernel 7.2.10).
  • Phase 3 rebuilt the tree against musl beside the glibc build and compared the two, with the libc sources at hand (section “Cross-check against a second C library”).

A verified entry carries one Verification line per phase: the verdict (CONFIRMED, REVISED, REFUTED, UNCHANGED or NEW, defined in the two phase sections), the methods used, and the evidence with the commands run and what they printed. Method tags:

Tag Meaning
RUN the test was run as installed
READ the source was re-read, usually together with the kernel source or the man page
MUTATION a copy of the test was changed so that the behaviour it claims to check is wrong, rebuilt and run
BUILD something was compiled: the mutant, a fixed version, a probe, or the whole tree
REPEAT the run was repeated; the count is given
STRESS run under stress-ng load on every CPU plus I/O and memory workers
CONTAINER run inside a container or private namespace, or as a non-root user
VIRT also run on the 1-CPU guest
GIT LTP git history consulted for the intent of the code
MUSL run or built against the musl build
SRC the behaviour was located in the glibc, musl or libtirpc source and cited with file and line
BULK taken from the whole-suite runs under both libcs rather than from an individual run

Verification was done in numbered passes. When a file was examined by more than one pass, the evidence pieces are joined with || and each is prefixed with the pass that produced it and its verdict, for example [v03: CONFIRMED] or [m09: NEW]. Passes v00 to v21 belong to phase 2: v00 is the build and runtest cross-reference that checked every “never built or never run” claim, v01 to v21 are the per-finding passes on the two hosts. Passes m01 to m09 belong to phase 3: m01 to m07 are the per-finding passes under both libcs, m08 is the triage of every open_posix result that differs between the glibc and musl runs, and m09 is the triage of every syscalls runtest entry that differs.

Entries that phase 2 or 3 added (“Found in phase N verification”) show the verdict as, for example, NEW (WRONG, high) [category before this check: OK/high], and quote the commands and their output in “Ran” and “Observed” blocks. Commands named ltprun, ltprun-glibc, ltprun-musl, ltpstress, ltpstress-glibc, ltpstress-musl and ltprepeat are small wrappers installed on the hosts: they run one installed LTP binary from the glibc or the musl build with the LTP environment set, under stress-ng load, or N times with a tally, and print its output and exit status. Paths under /root/ltp-build, /root/build, /root/ltp-musl, /root/src and /opt/ltp* are the build trees, library sources and install prefixes on the bare-metal host.

In the appendix every file line carries [verified: V] with its phase-2 verdict and [musl: V] with its phase-3 verdict where it has one.

Suggested order of work, by value per unit of effort:

  1. Drop dead code. A large share of OBSOLETE entries are sources that are never built or never run (not in any runtest file, not in a Makefile, or impossible to compile against any supported kernel). Removing them is low risk and shrinks the tree noticeably.
  2. Fix tests that cannot fail. Most WRONG entries are verification bugs: the test runs, prints TPASS, and would do so even if the kernel were broken. These give false confidence and are usually one-line fixes once identified.
  3. Relax checks on undocumented or undefined behavior. UNDOC and UNDEF entries are candidates for false failures on correct kernels or other libcs. The fix is normally to accept every documented outcome, to set up the case so only one error condition applies, or to drop the subcase.
  4. De-flake. FRAGILE entries fail on correct systems because of sleeps, containers, filesystems, tunables or hardware. Fix with proper synchronisation or detection (TCONF).
  5. Then WEAK and DOCS. Low verification value and inaccurate descriptions; cheap to fix, low urgency.

Verification on real hosts (phase 2)

After the reading pass, 774 findings were re-examined by running things on two disposable Fedora 44 machines: a 24-CPU bare-metal host (kernel 7.2.9) and a 1-CPU KVM guest (kernel 7.2.10), both with LTP built from this tree and installed. The set covered every WRONG and FRAGILE entry, every medium- or low-confidence OBSOLETE, UNDOC, UNDEF and DOCS entry, and every low-confidence WEAK entry. High-confidence WEAK entries are value judgements and were not re-run.

Methods, by category:

  • WRONG, “check cannot fail”: mutation. A copy of the test was changed so that the behavior it claims to verify is wrong (syscall skipped, result replaced, flag removed, child made to fail) and rebuilt; if the test still reported PASS the finding is confirmed. Where phase 1 proposed a fix, the pass also applied it in several cases and showed that the mutant then fails.
  • WRONG, “wrong expectation”: run as-is on both kernels; a FAIL for the stated reason confirms.
  • FRAGILE: 5 plain and 5 stressed runs (stress-ng on every CPU plus io and vm) on the big host and 3 or more on the 1-CPU guest, plus the specific condition the finding names where it could be created: a container or private namespace, a non-root user, a tmpfs, overlayfs, ext2, vfat or noexec TMPDIR, a changed sysctl, a low rlimit, a CPU quota, a locale, a stepped clock, an RTC offset.
  • OBSOLETE “never built / never run”: a full build with a cross-reference of every installed binary and script against every runtest file, scenario file and calling script; a module-enabled build against kernel-devel for the kernel-module claims.
  • UNDOC, UNDEF, DOCS, WEAK: run once, LTP git history for the intent, and a fresh read of the man page or POSIX.1-2024 text.

Outcome for the 976 verification records (some findings were checked by two passes):

Verdict Count Meaning
CONFIRMED 863 finding right; confidence raised where the evidence allowed
REVISED 61 finding partly right: category, confidence or mechanism changed
REFUTED 5 finding wrong, moved to OK; listed in their own section
UNCHANGED 32 no new evidence either way (feature not present on these hosts, or race not reproduced)
NEW 15 problems found while verifying that phase 1 had not flagged

Confidence moved up for 312 findings (231 medium to high, 61 low to medium, 20 low to high) and down for 35, almost all FRAGILE races that did not reproduce in 16 to 900 runs although a delay mutant shows the mechanism is real. Every verified entry carries a Verification line with the commands and what was observed, and the phase-1 category or confidence in brackets where it changed.

What the refutations have in common: all five came from reasoning about library internals without running them (the SAFE_SHMCTL macro resets the id after IPC_RMID; strtok with the stringified delimiter ',' strips the quotes; sockfs does implement listxattr). Where phase 1 only read the test and the kernel, it held up.

What could not be verified here and keeps its phase-1 confidence: cgroup v1 controllers (Fedora 44 has no cpuset v1 and cpu/memory are v2), multi-node NUMA, Intel PT, HWP, a real TPM, a pre-6.9 or pre-6.0 kernel, and a few tests that would have needed a reboot or an unrecoverable sysctl.

Cross-check against a second C library (phase 3)

Phase 2 showed where the audit was weakest: all five refutations were wrong about what glibc or a library does, and about 170 findings still rested on an argument of the form “glibc does X here, POSIX does not require it”. To test those arguments instead of asserting them, LTP was built a second time from the same checkout against musl 1.2.5 (Fedora’s musl-clang, with the kernel UAPI headers, sys/queue.h and a libtirpc 1.3.8 built into the musl sysroot) beside the glibc 2.43 build on the 24-CPU host, and the glibc, musl and libtirpc sources were unpacked next to them.

Three kinds of data came out of it:

  • Build differences. Only 10 of 2863 LTP binaries and 12 of 1639 open_posix binaries do not build under musl. Each is a finding in itself: the cpuset tests need glibc’s fts.h, fmtmsg01 uses addseverity(), timer_create01/03 reach into glibc’s private _sigev_un._tid, pthread_rwlock_rdlock/2-1,2-2 use _NP rwlock kinds behind a guard that tests the compiler rather than the libc, the prioceiling tests never check _POSIX_THREAD_PRIO_PROTECT, and aio_h/4-1 hard-codes glibc’s lio_listio prototype.
  • Per-finding runs. Every libc-dependent finding (170 files, the per-finding passes m01 to m07) was run under both libcs, repeated where timing mattered, and the libc behaviour it cites was located in the glibc or musl source and quoted with file and line.
  • Whole-suite comparison. The complete open_posix conformance and functional suites were run under both libcs (1732 and 1720 results; 129 differ), and the whole syscalls runtest file was run under musl with every non-PASS re-run under glibc (1552 tests, 191 non-PASS under musl, 52 of them PASS under glibc). Every difference was triaged into “musl limitation or bug, test is right”, “artefact of the run” or “test fault that glibc hides” (passes m08 and m09, see “How to read this report”).

Outcome for the 318 files checked in phase 3:

Verdict Count Meaning
CONFIRMED 120 finding right; musl behaves differently or the libc source confirms the mechanism
REVISED 13 finding partly right: the mechanism, the suggested fix or the category changed
REFUTED 0 finding wrong
UNCHANGED 132 both libcs agree and the finding rests on the POSIX text alone, or the difference is a musl bug
NEW 53 tests rated OK that only pass because of glibc behaviour

Entries touched by phase 3 carry a second Verification (phase 3 …) line; where phases disagree, phase 3 wins because it had the sources.

What musl changed in the picture:

  • Undefined behaviour stopped being latent. Six pthread tests that pass on glibc crash with SIGSEGV on musl, which deliberately traps on joining or detaching a non-joinable thread (pthread_attr_setdetachstate/2-1, pthread_cancel/5-1, pthread_detach/1-1,4-1,4-2, pthread_join/6-2). pthread_setcanceltype/1-1 and pthread_mutex_init/1-2 hang or fail because musl disables cancellation while a mutex lock waits; pthread_rwlock_wrlock/3-1 deadlocks instead of returning EDEADLK. All were UNDEF already; they are now demonstrated rather than argued.
  • glibc’s error mapping hides wrong expectations. sem_unlink/4-1,5-1 pass only because glibc turns every invalid name into ENOENT and prefixes names with sem.; sem_open/5-1 returns success without testing anything on either libc; aio_read/10-1, aio_write/8-1,9-2 and aio_read/11-2 fail on musl because it reports EBADF synchronously and has no prioritized I/O, both allowed by POSIX; gethostname02, pathconf01, sysconf01, getpagesize01, shmt09 and sbrk01 encode glibc’s wrappers (musl’s sbrk refuses any non-zero increment by design).
  • Some suggested fixes were glibc-shaped too. The proposed fixes for sem_unlink/5-1 (require ENAMETOOLONG), mq_open/speculative/2-2 (assert EINVAL for a leading slash) and getaddrinfo_01 (one error code) would fail on musl; the entries now carry corrected actions.
  • The obsolescent XSI signal family is still shipped. sighold, sigignore, sigpause, sigrelse and sigset were removed from POSIX.1-2024, but musl exports them without deprecation and glibc with a deprecation warning only; the action for those 17 tests is softened from “drop” to “drop, or keep as Issue 7 legacy coverage”. sigpause/4-1 is the one test in the family that catches a real libc defect: musl hangs where it should return EINVAL.
  • Some phase-1 explanations were wrong even though the verdict held. sigwaitinfo/6-1 passes on glibc because glibc’s sigtimedwait wrapper rewrites SI_TKILL to SI_USER, not because raise() avoids tgkill; pthread_detach/4-2 reports UNTESTED on glibc because pthread_detach returns 0, not ESRCH “by luck”; the RPC broadcast failure comes from how both libcs’ getifaddrs report an address without brd, so “glibc” became “the C library” in those entries.
  • The whole-suite diff found patterns the per-item reading had missed. Six scheduling tests (sched_setparam/20-1,21-1,21-2, sched_setscheduler/15-2,22-1,22-2) leave their error path through pthread_exit((void *)-1) from the main thread, so the process exits 0 and the suite counts a PASS; none of the 38 sched_*/fork tests that use process scheduling checks _POSIX_PRIORITY_SCHEDULING or sysconf(_SC_PRIORITY_SCHEDULING) before relying on it, so on a libc that declines the option (musl returns ENOSYS by design) they report UNRESOLVED or FAIL instead of UNSUPPORTED; six pthread_attr_*stack* tests read the stack of a fresh attribute, which POSIX leaves unspecified (glibc returns 0, musl EINVAL); three sched_setparam/25-* tests #error when _POSIX_SPORADIC_SERVER is undefined although POSIX allows that; aio_h/4-1 was changed in 2020 from the POSIX lio_listio prototype to glibc’s; and sigismember/5-1 and pthread_attr_setschedpolicy/4-1 require an EINVAL that POSIX only says “may” happen.
  • The syscalls runtest file under musl is covered by pass m09; 139 entries fail under both libcs in this environment for reasons phase 2 already recorded (single NUMA node, no kernel modules, swap on btrfs, kernel 7.2 drift) and were not re-examined.
  • musl bugs found on the way (not findings against the tests, recorded in the evidence): aio_cancel deadlocks on an in-progress request, sigpause ignores an invalid signal, lio_listio stops at the first failed submit, pthread_cond_broadcast wakes strictly in wait order regardless of priority, and sysconf(_SC_THREAD_PRIO_INHERIT) is hard-coded to -1.

Limits of this cross-check: musl is a second data point, not an oracle. Where both libcs agree the finding still rests on the POSIX or man-page text and its confidence was left alone; where musl disagrees because it is non-conformant, the finding was not credited for it. The comparison covers one architecture (x86_64) and one musl version.

Recurring patterns

The same handful of root causes explain most of the findings. They are worth knowing because they suggest tree-wide checks rather than one-off fixes.

Verification that cannot fail. Wrapper scripts that end with exit 0 or whose last command is rm -rf or tst_resm TINFO (test_controllers.sh, the cpuctl suite, sched_stress.sh, realtime run.sh, fs_racer.sh, smt_smp_affinity.sh); parents that check WEXITSTATUS() without WIFEXITED() so a child killed by a signal counts as PASS (open_posix sigaction 17-, 22-, 25-, raise/1-2, mq_notify 2-1 and 9-1); comparisons of a value with itself (the float_ suite, dup07, dup202, getpagesize01, mv_tests backup check); (flags & 0) != 0 style checks (socket02, socketpair02, pipe2_01); results computed and never asserted (mq_notify01, pth_str03, pi_perf, openposix pthread_create/s-c1); inverted errno logic (aio_read/9-1, aio_write/7-1, mmap/27-1); copy-paste leftovers (acct02 reads stime for utime, pthread_atfork/1-1 checks the parent twice, pthread_mutex_setprioceiling/1-1 never calls setprioceiling, nftw test29A/30A call the ENOTDIR helper). A grep for exit 0 at the end of runner scripts and for WEXITSTATUS without WIFEXITED would find more of these.

Regressions introduced by mechanical conversions. Several WRONG entries were correct in the old API and lost their check during the new-API conversion or a mass edit: mmap03 dropped its memcmp (5c778f6cd65d), fchmod04 dropped seteuid(nobody) (7ede1cd15414), rename13 now renames a path onto itself (f93f55eeb32f), recvmsg01 moved SCM_RIGHTS cases to PF_INET where TCP ignores them, munmap03 passes the address of a pointer variable (0c7346cb0974), fcntl33 lost the assignment that enables its overlayfs exception, migrate_pages03 runs the migration as nobody (53eac722fd37), the IPv6 multicast query tests send queries from a non-link-local address the kernel drops (ef227aca9ef1), if-addr-addlarge deletes each address right after adding it (f925eece9747). In the POSIX suite, commit d3df7e05e9f7 (“Replace SIGPOLL with SIGUSR2”) hand-edited generated sigaction files, turned nine -2.c SIGALRM tests into byte-identical copies of the -18.c SIGUSR2 tests, and so removed SIGALRM coverage from those families. Compiler optimisation is a related trap: work loops with no side effects compile to nothing at -O2 (realtime tc-2 and periodic_cpu_load, open_posix sched_setparam/2-1, 2-2, pthread_exit/6-2), so timing and CPU-accounting checks pass trivially.

Kernel drift. Tests whose premise the kernel has since removed or changed: /proc/schedstat version 17 renamed the domain line (6.14), so every cpuset_sched_domains case fails; the pipe user-pages soft limit is skipped for root (pipe15 passes without reaching the regression); setsockopt08 (CVE-2021-22555) is rejected before the vulnerable path since 6.9; set_mempolicy05’s compat heuristic is invalid since the compat path was removed in 5.15; memcg charge moving was removed in 6.13; DCCP in 6.16 and UDP-Lite in 7.1; sys_sysctl in 5.5; the powerpc endian switch in 6.12; mandatory locking in 5.15 (fcntl14, fcntl16, ftruncate04); tracing_enabled; the Blackfin register table in ptrace04; statmount flag 1 and landlock flag 1 gained meanings in 7.0; v4l2 returns ENOTTY not EINVAL since 3.1. The tbio, tpci-adjacent, v4l and usb kernel modules cannot compile against any supported kernel and the build silently ignores that.

Code that is never built or never run. About a hundred rpc/rpc-tirpc variant clients (*_mt, *_stress, *_complex, *_dataint, *_limits, *_performance, *_scalability), open_posix stress/threads (no Makefile, never had one), v4l/user_space and usb, memtoy, mmc_security, the sched_tc0..3 load generators, async_handler_tsc, gtod_infinite, setgroups04, mmap-corruption01, shmat1, nfsv4/acl/acl1.c, ltpSockets, fs_racer_dir_test, cpuhotplug01 (commented out), cmdlib.sh/net_cmdlib.sh. Separately, over a hundred open_posix N-M.sh scripts (plus their build-time <func>_N-M.sh copies) only echo “Tested implicitly via assertion N” and exit 0, which the runner records as PASS.

Undocumented error precedence. Many errno tests set up two error conditions at once and pass only because of the order the kernel happens to check them: EROFS cases run as nobody on a root-owned file (chown04, fchmod06, fchown04, fchownat03, lchown02, linkat02, utimes01 is the documented exception), EINVAL-before-EBADF or -EFAULT with closed or NULL arguments (dup3_02, io_cancel01/02, mq_notify02, prctl02, name_to_handle_at02, accept01), F_GETLK probes that overlap several locks (fcntl11/19/20/21), the max_map_count off-by-one. The fix is to make each case trigger exactly one documented error.

POSIX-undefined behavior required by the conformance suite. POSIX.1-2008 and 2024 removed many “shall fail” errors that the 2002-era tests still demand: pthread_join/detach/cancel on an already joined or detached thread, re-initialising or destroying a locked rwlock or mutex, spinlock EBUSY and EDEADLK, invalid timer ids, uninitialised attribute objects, pthread_once with automatic storage. Tests also count a POSIX-permitted spurious wakeup as FAIL (pthread_cond_wait/1-1, pthread_cond_timedwait/1-1, 2-2), require “may fail” errors (getgroups01, fpathconf01, sigaddset/4-1, aio EBADF synchronously) and require a single waiter for EPOLLEXCLUSIVE. These pass on glibc and Linux today; the question for maintainers is whether to keep them as Linux behavior tests (then document that) or drop them from a conformance suite.

Environment assumptions. sleep()-based handshakes (flock07, nanosleep02, kill02, semop05, the open_posix mq_, cond_ and cancel tests), privileges and containers (bind02 ignores ip_unprivileged_port_start, memfd_create01 fails with memfd_noexec set, mlock/12-1 as a normal user, 17 mq tests create queues above msg_max as non-root, ptrace11 under Yama, sched_getscheduler/7-1 on pid 1), filesystems (open12 on vfat, ustat01/02 on a btrfs root, hugemmap11 O_DIRECT on tmpfs, fallocate03, name_to_handle_at on overlayfs, vma05 on distros with /lib64), hardware and latency thresholds (the realtime suite, dctcp01, sctp01, timerfd01, epoll_wait04, getrusage04, cpufreq_boost, irqbalance01), tunables (sysfs tests, membarrier01 under nohz_full, overcommit_memory, min_free_kbytes).

Side effects worth fixing regardless of category. cpuhotplug07 runs make mrproper in /usr/src/linux by default; block_dev tc07 taints the kernel with a WARN on every run and disables later taint checks; tpci unbinds live PCI drivers; madvise01 uses MADV_HWPOISON as a smoke test and poisons host pages; kvm_pagefault01 reloads kvm with npt/ept off and never restores it; tcp_cc_lib.sh never restores tcp_congestion_control; mmap/24-1 lowers max_map_count and restores it only on failure; tirpc_svc_tp_create registers a bogus RPC program and never unregisters it; pthread_atfork/3-3 reaches about 1.9 GB RSS; the pthread_mutex_lock s-c tests exhaust thread and PID limits; the tpm-tools suite is destructive and order-dependent; twopsetclock moves the wall clock.

Man pages that disagree with the kernel. In these cases the tests follow the kernel and were left OK, but the man-pages project should be told: get_mempolicy with MPOL_F_ADDR and a NULL address returns EFAULT (man says EINVAL); init_module with an unsigned module under enforcement returns EKEYREJECTED (man says ENOKEY); getsockopt with a wrong level returns EOPNOTSUPP (not listed); fsconfig with fd < 0 returns EINVAL (man says EBADF); Q_GETNEXTQUOTA with no next id returns ENOENT (man says ESRCH); unshare can return EMFILE (not listed); epoll_ctl can return EFAULT (not listed).

Patterns that only showed up when running

  • A child killed by its signal counts as PASS. Many open_posix tests check WEXITSTATUS() without WIFEXITED(); when the child dies of the very signal under test the status reads 0 and the test passes. Mutation showed this for the whole sigaction 17-* and 22-* families and several sigqueue/sigpause tests, and it also hides signals that are ignored by default (SIGCHLD, SIGURG, SIGCONT).
  • The workload is optimized away. In periodic_cpu_load, tc-2 and sched_setparam/2-1, the installed binary’s busy loop compiles to a bare ret or a single add, so timing-based verdicts measure nothing.
  • Hard-coded “nonexistent” pid 999999. Both hosts set pid_max to 4194304 and the big host’s pid counter crossed 999999 on its own during the session; inside a pid namespace where that pid is alive the sigqueue and kill tests fail.
  • Non-root runs report FAIL, not UNRESOLVED. Sixteen mq_receive/mq_timedreceive tests, the priority tests and several others misreport a missing privilege as a conformance failure.
  • Side effects seen live: mmap/24-1 lowers vm.max_map_count on its normal pass path; runpwtests03 leaves every CPU on the userspace governor; tcp_cc_lib leaves dctcp as the congestion control; gethostid01 creates /etc/hostid; rpc_test.sh cannot kill servers whose name exceeds 15 characters; tirpc_svc_tp_create leaves an RPC program registered.
  • Vacuous per-filesystem coverage. open12 lacks .mount_device, so all ten “testing on ” iterations run on the same TMPDIR; adding it makes vfat fail and exfat break, as phase 1 predicted.

Caveats

The classification was produced by 67 model-driven reading passes over every source file, with kernel source, man pages and POSIX consulted for anything flagged, followed by 22 verification passes that ran the flagged tests, mutated copies of them and repeated runs under load on two Fedora 44 hosts (kernels 7.2.9 and 7.2.10), and 9 cross-check passes against a musl build of the same tree with the glibc, musl and libtirpc sources at hand. Findings that were in neither set (most OK entries and high-confidence WEAK entries) rest on reading alone, except that every open_posix test and every syscalls runtest entry was at least run once under both libcs and any difference triaged. Entries whose Verification line says UNCHANGED kept their phase-1 confidence because the hosts could not exercise them. Negative results for races (“not reproduced in N runs”) do not prove absence; the entry says whether a delay mutant showed the mechanism. Claims about libc or libtirpc internals in entries without a phase-3 line were made without the library source; entries with one cite the file and line. The musl comparison covers one version (1.2.5) on x86_64. POSIX judgements use the 2024 edition; where an older edition still listed an error the entry says so. Numbers in the summary tables count primary categories only and reflect the verified state; secondary tags appear in brackets in the appendix.

WRONG: Incorrect expectation or ineffective check

The test asserts something the kernel source, man page or POSIX contradicts, or its verification is broken so it can pass without exercising the claimed behavior (wrong variable checked, unreachable failure path, child failure not propagated, result ignored). Results from these tests are misleading in one direction or the other. Action: fix the check, or drop the test or subcase if it cannot be fixed.

351 testcases. Sorted by path; confidence shown in each entry.

testcases/kernel/containers/utsname/utsname04.c (runtest: containers/utsname04_clone, utsname04_unshare)

  • Category: WRONG
  • Confidence: high
  • Claim under test: An unprivileged process gets EPERM from clone()/unshare() with CLONE_NEWUTS.
  • Problem: The errno check is TST_EXP_PASS(errno == EPERM). TST_EXP_PASS expands to TEST(SCALL), and TEST() does errno = 0; before evaluating SCALL, so the expression is always 0 == EPERM -> 0, which TST_EXP_PASS reports as TPASS regardless of the real errno. (Had errno survived, the logic would also be inverted: a true comparison returns 1, which TST_EXP_PASS reports as “invalid retval”.) Only “the call failed” is really verified; the errno is never checked. In the clone mode tst_res() calls also run between the failure and the check.
  • Evidence: utsname04.c:42, 46; include/tst_test_macros.h:43-48 (TEST sets errno = 0) and 279-299 (TST_EXP_PASS_SILENT_ treats non-zero as failure). clone(2)/unshare(2) document EPERM for CLONE_NEWUTS without CAP_SYS_ADMIN.
  • Suggested action: Use TST_EXP_FAIL(unshare(CLONE_NEWUTS), EPERM) and, for clone, save errno right after tst_clone() and check it with TST_EXP_EQ_LI(saved_errno, EPERM).
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN,MUTATION. HPE as-is: clone/unshare modes TPASS ‘errno == EPERM passed’. Mutated work copy so the call fails with EINVAL (clone flags CLONE_NEWUTS|CLONE_THREAD; unshare(-1)): both modes still ‘TPASS: errno == EPERM passed’ (passed 2 failed 0) -> errno check is vacuous (TEST() zeroes errno before evaluating errno == EPERM)

testcases/kernel/controllers/cpuctl/run_cpuctl_latency_test.sh (runtest: controllers/controllers via test_controllers.sh)

  • Category: WRONG (secondary: OBSOLETE, FRAGILE)
  • Confidence: high
  • Claim under test: wakeup latency of a sleeping task stays below 2x the scheduler wakeup granularity with 100 CPU hogs, without (test 1) and with (test 2) cpu cgroups.
  • Problem: the verdict never reaches the harness. cpuctl_latency_check_task exits 1 on FAIL, but the script only echoes “TBROK …” and ends with cd $PWD, so it always exits 0. The parent test_controllers.sh also always ends with exit 0. The “sources compiled” check [ ! -f $cpuctl_latency_test ] uses undefined variables, so it collapses to [ ! -f ] and never fires. The threshold comes from /proc/sys/kernel/sched_wakeup_granularity_ns, which moved to debugfs in 5.13 and no longer exists under EEVDF. So the code always uses the (log2(ncpus)+1)5ms2 fallback, which the kernel does not promise for 100 runnable hogs at the same nice level. Test 2 depends on parameters.sh mounting a v1 hierarchy with only cpu. That fails with EBUSY on any host where cpu is co-mounted with cpuacct (kernel/cgroup/cgroup-v1.c:1214-1218 skips the mismatched root, then rebind_subsystems refuses a controller that is already bound). On v2 hosts the whole suite TCONFs in test_controllers.sh.
  • Evidence: run_cpuctl_latency_test.sh:98-99, :129, final wait $check_task / cd $PWD block; test_controllers.sh:101 exit 0; no sched_wakeup_granularity sysctl in /usr/src/linux/kernel/sched/.
  • Suggested action: drop. If kept, propagate the check task’s exit status and rewrite it on the new shell API with a cgroup v2 path (tst_cgctl).
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN,MUTATION. HPE: test 1 as-is PASS (max 3447us), script rc 0. Copy with allowed_latency=0: ‘FAIL The Latency test 1 failed’, ‘Task exited abnormally with return value: 1’, ‘TBROK Test could’nt execute…’ yet SCRIPT_RC=0. Test 2 (unshare -m): ‘ERROR: Could not mount cgroup filesystem on /dev/cpuctl’ (cpu bound to v2). Via test_controllers.sh: TCONF on any cgroup2 host

testcases/kernel/controllers/cpuctl_fj/run_cpuctl_test_fj.sh (runtest: controllers/controllers via test_controllers.sh)

  • Category: WRONG (secondary: FRAGILE, OBSOLETE)
  • Confidence: high
  • Claim under test: 22 cases on v1 cpu.shares parsing and clamping, root restrictions, attach rules, and share-based CPU distribution.
  • Problem: (1) case5 (“attach realtime process”) writes PID 3 to tasks and requires EINVAL. That assumes PID 3 is an RT kthread (migration/0 on 2.6 kernels) and that CONFIG_RT_GROUP_SCHED is active. On current kernels PID 3 is the SCHED_NORMAL pool_workqueue_release kthread (kernel/workqueue.c:8253, the first kthread created in workqueue_init). It has no PF_NO_SETAFFINITY, so cgroup_procs_write_start (kernel/cgroup/cgroup.c:3150) accepts it and case5 FAILs on a correct kernel. RT tasks are only refused when rt_group_sched_enabled() (kernel/sched/core.c:9640-9650). (2) do_test prints TFAIL when cleanup fails and then TPASS for the same case (no continue). (3) Each case ends with wait $pid, and SIGUSR1 is sent right after spawning cpuctl_fj_cpu-hog. If the signal arrives before sigaction(), the default action kills the hog and wait returns 138, so the case fails. (4) case19-22 judge one top -bn1 sample (line 8, column 9) against windows such as 96-103% or 44-56% on a shared CPU0, and case21/22 need all 10 samples in range. That depends on load, the top version and .toprc. (5) If the v1 -o cpu mount fails (cpu co-mounted with cpuacct), all 22 cases report TFAIL instead of TCONF. The script’s exit status never reflects TFAIL, and the parent exits 0. The other EINVAL/clamp expectations (cases 6-17) match kernel/sched/fair.c:15720-15723 and kstrtoull parsing.
  • Evidence: run_cpuctl_test_fj.sh:230-249, 284-292, 99, 600, 641, 674, 697-707, 51-55.
  • Suggested action: drop case5 (or create an RT task, check CONFIG_RT_GROUP_SCHED and attach it). Fix the TPASS-after-TFAIL bug and TCONF on mount failure. Better: drop the suite in favor of cgroup v2 cpu.weight tests.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN,READ. HPE: PID 3 = pool_workqueue_release, SCHED_OTHER, flags 0x208040 (no PF_NO_SETAFFINITY); cpuctl_fj_simple_echo 3 > /cgroup.procs -> rc 0 (case5 needs 22) and PID 3 moved. Script as-is (unshare -m): 22x ‘failed to mount cpu subsystem’ + 22x ‘caseN FAIL’ (no TCONF), script rc 0. Early SIGUSR1 kills cpuctl_fj_cpu-hog (rc 138) 1/10 when sent at once

testcases/kernel/controllers/cpuset/cpuset_hotplug_test/cpuset_hotplug_test.sh (runtest: controllers/cpuset_hotplug)

  • Category: WRONG (secondary: FRAGILE, DOCS)
  • Confidence: medium
  • Claim under test: offlining or onlining CPU1 updates root and child cpuset.cpus, and the affinity of tasks in the cpuset follows.
  • Problem: in the root cases (1-2) and the “EMPTY” general case, the “task cpus” value is read from /sys/devices/system/cpu/present instead of the task’s Cpus_allowed_list. The task’s affinity is never checked, and the comparison against cpus_all (0..online_count-1) is unrelated to cpusets. It also fails falsely whenever present != online, for example with nosmt or maxcpus=, where online can be a contiguous 0-N (so ncpus_check passes) while present is larger. Hotplugging CPU1 is assumed to be possible: only Hyper-V is excluded, so a missing or refused cpu1/online gives TFAIL instead of TCONF. sleep 1 waits for asynchronous task migration out of an emptied cpuset (cpuset_migrate_tasks_workfn, kernel/cgroup/cpuset-v1.c:270-321). This is acknowledged in the code with an issue link. TST_TOTAL=13 but only 6 cases run.
  • Evidence: cpuset_hotplug_test.sh:96, :188, :26; cpuset_funcs.sh:130-135, 246-259.
  • Suggested action: read /proc/$tst_pid/status Cpus_allowed_list in all cases and compare it with the online mask. TCONF if cpu1/online is missing or not writable. Fix TST_TOTAL.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): UNCHANGED via RUN,READ. Cannot exercise: Fedora 44 kernels have CONFIG_CPUSETS_V1 unset, /proc/cgroups has no cpuset line -> HPE ‘cpuset_hotplug 1 TCONF: Cpuset is not supported’ (same on VIRT). Re-read confirms task_cpus read from /sys/devices/system/cpu/present (:96, :188), TST_TOTAL=13 with 6 cases, no TCONF for unwritable cpu1/online

testcases/kernel/controllers/cpuset/cpuset_lib/cpuinfo.c (runtest: helper library for controllers/cpuset_sched_domains)

  • Category: WRONG
  • Confidence: high
  • Claim under test: getcpuinfo()/get_sched_domains() reads each CPU’s sched-domain span from /proc/schedstat so cpuset_sched_domains_check can compare it with the expected partition.
  • Problem: The parser does sscanf(buf, "%s %s", str1, str2) and feeds the second token of every domainN line to bitmask_parsehex(). Since schedstat version 17 (kernel commit 011b3a14dc66 “sched/stats: Print domain name in /proc/schedstat”, v6.14) the line is domainN <name> <cpumask> ..., so str2 is “SMT”/“MC”/“PKG”/“NUMA”. strtoul() reads no hex digits, bitmask_parsehex() returns error, get_sched_domains() returns -1, and getcpuinfo() fails. Every caller therefore fails on 6.14+ kernels. The format is documented and versioned (“version N” header line), so the parser should check the version or skip the name field.
  • Evidence: cpuinfo.c:222 (sscanf “%s %s”), cpuinfo.c:239 (bitmask_parsehex(str2)), cpuinfo.c:279; libbitmask.c:241-246 (nchars_read < 1 -> err); /usr/src/linux/kernel/sched/stats.c:107 (SCHEDSTAT_VERSION 17) and :139 seq_printf(seq, "domain%d %s %*pb", dcount++, sd->name, ...); Documentation/scheduler/sched-stats.rst:8-9 “The domain field prints the name of the corresponding sched domain from this version onwards” and :91 domain<N> <name> <cpumask> ....
  • Suggested action: Read the “version” line; for version >= 17 parse the third token (sscanf(buf, "%s %*s %s", ...)), else the second.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN,MUTATION,BUILD. HPE /proc/schedstat ‘version 17’, lines ‘domain0 SMT 001001 …’. Original cpuset_sched_domains_check: ‘get sched domain’s info for each cpu failed’ -> ‘TFAIL: getcpuinfo failed’. Rebuilt with cpuinfo.c parsing the 3rd token for domain lines: getcpuinfo succeeds and the check proceeds to partition_domains (fails there only because cpuset v1 is not built in)

testcases/kernel/controllers/cpuset/cpuset_load_balance_test/cpuset_sched_domains_check.c (runtest: helper run by controllers/cpuset_sched_domains)

  • Category: WRONG (secondary: FRAGILE)
  • Confidence: high
  • Claim under test: The sched domain span of every CPU matches the partition that cpuset sched_load_balance settings should produce.
  • Problem: It calls getcpuinfo() (cpuset_lib/cpuinfo.c) and reports TFAIL when that fails. On kernels >= 6.14 getcpuinfo() always fails because of the schedstat v17 domain-name field (see cpuinfo.c entry), so the check always reports “getcpuinfo failed” without testing anything. Secondary: /proc/schedstat exists only with CONFIG_SCHEDSTATS (kernel/sched/build_utility.c:73), and a missing file gives TFAIL instead of TCONF. The expected partition also ignores CPUs removed from load balancing by isolcpus=domain / nohz_full (housekeeping HK_TYPE_DOMAIN), so such systems mismatch.
  • Evidence: cpuset_sched_domains_check.c:66-67; cpuinfo.c:217-218 (fopen fail -> -1); kernel/sched/stats.c:139.
  • Suggested action: Fix the parser in cpuinfo.c. Return TCONF when /proc/schedstat is missing. Exclude non-housekeeping CPUs from the expected domains, or TCONF when isolcpus is set.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN,MUTATION,BUILD. HPE (kernel 7.2.9, schedstat v17): ltprun cpuset_sched_domains_check -> ‘cpuset_sched_domains_check.c:67: getcpuinfo failed’ RC=1 before any domain comparison; same binary with fixed cpuinfo.c parser gets past getcpuinfo (fails later at :72 partition domains only because CPUSETS_V1=n)

testcases/kernel/controllers/cpuset/cpuset_load_balance_test/cpuset_sched_domains_test.sh (runtest: controllers/cpuset_sched_domains)

  • Category: WRONG (secondary: FRAGILE)
  • Confidence: high
  • Claim under test: cpuset sched_load_balance / cpus / CPU hotplug combinations partition the scheduler domains correctly (19 cases).
  • Problem: Each case decides pass/fail only through the exit status of cpuset_sched_domains_check. That helper fails unconditionally on 6.14+ because of the schedstat domain-name field, so all 19 cases TFAIL on current kernels whatever the partitioning is. Secondary: it waits for domain rebuild with a fixed sleep 1 before checking, and does not handle isolcpus/nohz_full or !CONFIG_SCHEDSTATS.
  • Evidence: cpuset_sched_domains_test.sh:77-78, 120-121, 196-197 (sleep 1 + cpuset_sched_domains_check); cpuinfo.c:222/239; kernel/sched/stats.c:139.
  • Suggested action: Fix cpuinfo.c parsing (see above), then add a TCONF for missing /proc/schedstat and isolated CPUs.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN,MUTATION. HPE/VIRT as-is: ‘cpuset_sched_domains 1 TCONF: Cpuset is not supported’ (CONFIG_CPUSETS_V1 unset, 1 node). Each case’s verdict = exit status of cpuset_sched_domains_check, which was shown to TFAIL ‘getcpuinfo failed’ on the schedstat v17 format here, so on any >=6.14 host with cpuset v1 every case fails regardless of partitioning

testcases/kernel/controllers/freezer/fork_freeze.sh (runtest: via test_controllers.sh -> run_freezer.sh)

  • Category: WRONG
  • Confidence: high
  • Claim under test: freezing a cgroup while a forkbomb (timed_forkbomb) runs inside it.
  • Problem: timed_forkbomb is started in the background by a non-interactive bash, so its stdin is /dev/null (POSIX async-list rule, verified). The echo go >> /proc/$pid/fd/0 on line 45 writes to /dev/null. timed_forkbomb.c:58 while (scanf("%as", &word) < 1) {} then spins forever on EOF (-1). Even with real input it would spin, because with LTP’s -std=gnu99 glibc uses the C99 scanf, where “%a” is a float conversion, so “go” returns 0 (verified by compiling a test). No fork ever happens; the test freezes and thaws one busy-looping task. Line 29 also sources ${CGROUPS_TESTROOT}/libltp, which is not in INSTALL_TARGETS.
  • Evidence: fork_freeze.sh:38-55; timed_forkbomb.c:56-61; include/mk/config.mk:67 (-std=gnu99); freezer/Makefile INSTALL_TARGETS.
  • Suggested action: start the helper with a pipe or FIFO as stdin and use %ms (or just a pipe/signal handshake) in timed_forkbomb.c, or drop it in favour of the cgroup_fj freezer stress tests.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN,READ. HPE (v1 freezer): fork_freeze.sh RC 0 (‘line 29: …/libltp: No such file or directory’); during the run ps shows exactly 1 timed_forkbomb, state R ~48% CPU, /proc/PID/fd/0 -> /dev/null -> the ‘echo go’ goes to /dev/null, the helper spins in scanf and never forks; the test freezes/thaws one busy loop and passes
  • Verification (phase 3, glibc vs musl build and libc sources): CONFIRMED via MUSL,RUN,SRC. HPE glibc: fork_freeze.sh RC=0, 1 timed_forkbomb state R 49% CPU, fd0->/dev/null; musl: RC=0, 1 timed_forkbomb (ld-musl) R 42%, fd0->/dev/null. Probe sscanf(“go”,“%as”)=0, sscanf(““)=-1 under both (glibc binary imports __isoc99_scanf; musl vfscanf.c:301 ‘a’ is a float conv) -> helper spins in scanf under either libc, never forks

testcases/kernel/controllers/freezer/freeze_move_thaw.sh (runtest: via test_controllers.sh -> run_freezer.sh)

  • Category: WRONG
  • Confidence: high
  • Claim under test: moving a task out of a FROZEN cgroup into a THAWED cgroup fails, and the task stays frozen in the original group.
  • Problem: The kernel has allowed migrating frozen tasks for a long time. freezer_attach() thaws a task that moves into a non-freezing cgroup, and the v1 freezer has no can_attach. The write to child2/tasks therefore succeeds, which sets result=1 (line 57). The task is then thawed and in child2, so assert_sample_proc_is_frozen at line 71 fails. The test always fails on current kernels. run_freezer.sh stops at the first failure, so this also stops freeze_cancel, freeze_self_thaw, stop_* and fork_freeze from running. The script’s own comments (lines 24-28, 63-94) expected that the semantics might go this way and say how to flip the asserts.
  • Evidence: freeze_move_thaw.sh:56-73; kernel/cgroup/legacy_freezer.c:144-185 (“Tasks can be migrated into a different freezer anytime regardless of its current state … !(freezer->state & CGROUP_FREEZING) -> __thaw_task(task)“).
  • Suggested action: change to the documented semantics: the move succeeds, the task is in child2 and not frozen. Drop the stale comments.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN. HPE (v1 freezer, 7.2.9): ‘freeze_move_thaw.sh 1 TFAIL : Expected task 1062575 to be frozen (unexpected task state: “S”)’ RC 1 -> the move into the THAWED cgroup succeeded and thawed the task, as kernel/cgroup/legacy_freezer.c freezer_attach() documents; run_freezer.sh stops here, so later scripts never run

testcases/kernel/controllers/freezer/freeze_self_thaw.sh (runtest: via test_controllers.sh -> run_freezer.sh)

  • Category: WRONG
  • Confidence: high
  • Claim under test: a task in a cgroup freezes its own cgroup by writing FROZEN, and the test then thaws it.
  • Problem: In sleep_freeze_self_sleep() (line 40) the background subshell does export sample_proc=$!. Inside an async subshell $! is not the subshell’s own PID: it is empty here, because no earlier background job exists (checked: ( echo $! ) & prints empty). add_sample_proc_to_cgroup therefore reports a TFAIL and writes an empty string to tasks (EINVAL). The subshell never joins the cgroup, so it freezes an empty cgroup and keeps running. In the parent, sample_proc is the subshell PID, which is in state S, so assert_sample_proc_is_frozen (line 66) fails. Self-freezing is never exercised. Today this is hidden only because run_freezer.sh stops at freeze_move_thaw.sh first.
  • Evidence: freeze_self_thaw.sh:38-49,64-66; libcgroup_freezer add_sample_proc_to_named_cgroup / assert_task_is_frozen.
  • Suggested action: use $BASHPID (or sh -c 'echo $$ > tasks; ...') inside the subshell.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN,READ. HPE: ‘TFAIL : Expected pid does not exist’, ‘echo: write error: Invalid argument’, ‘TFAIL : Failed to add sample process to cgroup’, ‘TINFO : freezing itself’ (empty pid), ‘TFAIL : Expected task N to be frozen (unexpected task state: “S”)’ RC 1. bash -c ‘( echo $! ) & wait’ prints empty

testcases/kernel/controllers/freezer/freeze_write_freezing.sh (runtest: via test_controllers.sh -> run_freezer.sh)

  • Category: WRONG
  • Confidence: high
  • Claim under test: writing “FREEZING” to a FROZEN cgroup fails with EIO and the state stays FROZEN.
  • Problem: It has the same broken > freezer.state 2>&1 | grep 'Input/output error$' construct (line 44) as write_freezing.sh. grep never matches, the ERR trap breaks out before the line-46 assert, and the script exits 0. The kernel returns EINVAL, not EIO.
  • Evidence: freeze_write_freezing.sh:44-47,60; kernel/cgroup/legacy_freezer.c:410-428.
  • Suggested action: the same fix as write_freezing.sh.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN,MUTATION,VIRT. HPE as-is RC 0. Mutated copy writing THAWED instead of FREEZING to the FROZEN cgroup (state really changes) still RC 0 on HPE and VIRT -> the ‘state stays FROZEN’ assert is never reached. Direct check: FREEZING written to a FROZEN v1 freezer -> ‘write error: Invalid argument’, state FROZEN (EINVAL, not EIO)

testcases/kernel/controllers/freezer/run_freezer.sh (runtest: via test_controllers.sh)

  • Category: WRONG (phase 1: WEAK)
  • Confidence: high (phase 1: medium)
  • Claim under test: driver that runs all v1 freezer scripts.
  • Problem: main() breaks out of the loop at the first failing script (line 118). Because freeze_move_thaw.sh always fails, the later five scripts never run. If the trial mount in test_prereqs fails, TEST_SCRIPTS stays empty and the driver exits 0 having run nothing. Its exit status is ignored anyway by test_controllers.sh, which always exits 0.
  • Evidence: run_freezer.sh:97-99,108-122; test_controllers.sh:101.
  • Suggested action: run all scripts and aggregate the results; TCONF when the freezer cannot be mounted; fix the always-failing scripts.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): NEW via RUN,VIRT,GIT. HPE and VIRT, freezer hierarchy free (waited until /proc/cgroups showed none): run_freezer.sh prints ‘Variable TST_TOTAL is set to 0, must be greater than zero’, RC 1, runs no script. test_setup sets TST_TOTAL=#TEST_SCRIPTS (still 0) before tst_resm; ltpapicmd.c:285 exits 1 on TST_TOTAL<=0 (since 2012 or earlier). Freezer suite never runs via test_controllers.sh, which ignores the rc
  • Verification conclusion: test_setup() exports TST_TOTAL=${#TEST_SCRIPTS[@]} (still 0, because the list is only filled in test_prereqs) and then calls tst_resm. ltpapicmd.c:285-289 exits 1 when TST_TOTAL <= 0, so test_setup && test_prereqs && main stops before any freezer script runs. test_controllers.sh ignores the rc. So the freezer suite never runs from runtest at all; this also means the freeze_move_thaw “stops the chain” effect in the phase-1 entries never actually happens. Fix: set TST_TOTAL=1 before the first tst_resm (or port the suite), or drop it.

testcases/kernel/controllers/freezer/timed_forkbomb.c (helper for fork_freeze.sh)

  • Category: WRONG
  • Confidence: high
  • Claim under test: helper that waits for a word on stdin, then fork-bombs for N seconds.
  • Problem: while (scanf("%as", &word) < 1) never terminates. Under -std=gnu99, “%a” is the C99 float conversion (returns 0 on “go” and leaves the input unconsumed), and on EOF it returns -1. It also passes char** to a float conversion (UB). See fork_freeze.sh.
  • Evidence: timed_forkbomb.c:56-61.
  • Suggested action: use %ms, or a simple read() on a pipe/FIFO; treat EOF as “go” or as an error.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN,BUILD. Local: scanf(“%as”) built with -std=gnu99 (and default gnu17): ‘echo go |’ -> ret=0 three times (input not consumed), ‘ ret=-1; so ’while (scanf(…) < 1)’ never ends. HPE: the helper started by fork_freeze.sh stays a single R-state process for the whole test (no fork)

testcases/kernel/controllers/freezer/write_freezing.sh (runtest: controllers/controllers -> test_controllers.sh -> run_freezer.sh)

  • Category: WRONG
  • Confidence: high
  • Claim under test: writing “FREEZING” to freezer.state of a THAWED cgroup fails with EIO and leaves the state THAWED.
  • Problem: Line 42 is "${CG_FILE_WRITE}" "FREEZING" > freezer.state 2>&1 | grep -E 'Input/output error$'. Redirections apply left to right, so stderr is also pointed at freezer.state; /bin/echo’s error message never reaches the pipe, grep always exits 1, and the trap 'break' ERR leaves the loop before the state assert on line 44. result stays “” (UNFINISHED), so exit $result becomes plain exit, which returns the status of cleanup_freezer || /bin/true (0). The test passes without checking anything. The expected error is also wrong: the kernel returns EINVAL, not EIO, for any string other than THAWED/FROZEN. Reproduced the redirect/ERR-trap behaviour with a /dev/full stand-in.
  • Evidence: write_freezing.sh:42-46,58; kernel/cgroup/legacy_freezer.c freezer_write() lines 410-428 (else return -EINVAL;).
  • Suggested action: capture stderr properly (/bin/echo FREEZING 2>&1 >freezer.state | grep -q 'Invalid argument'), expect EINVAL, and make a failed match a real TFAIL. Or port it to a new-API C test.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN,MUTATION. HPE as-is RC 0. Mutated copy writing FROZEN instead of FREEZING (state really changes to FROZEN) still RC 0 -> the THAWED assert is never reached. Direct check on a v1 freezer: ‘/bin/echo FREEZING > freezer.state’ -> ‘write error: Invalid argument’, state stays THAWED (EINVAL, not EIO)

testcases/kernel/controllers/memcg/regression/memcg_regression_test.sh (runtest: controllers/memcg_regression)

  • Category: WRONG (secondary: WEAK)
  • Confidence: high

HPE+VIRT (Fedora 44, ntfs-3g mkfs.ntfs present): zram01 ‘line 82: mkfs.ntfs3: command not found’ -> ‘TFAIL: Failed to make ntfs3 on /dev/zram9’ + TBROK. tst_supported_fs lists ntfs3 since 7dc8e9a515ce (2026-04, maps ntfs3->mkfs.ntfs internally) but zram_makefs runs mkfs.$fs literally
  • Verification conclusion: Since the library started reporting kernel ntfs3 as a separate filesystem, zram01 fails on any system with ntfs3 and mkfs.ntfs. zram_makefs() calls mkfs.$fs directly, and mkfs.ntfs3 does not exist. Proposed: map ntfs3 to mkfs.ntfs in zram_makefs (or use tst_mkfs), or skip ntfs3 in initialize_vars.

Mutation: the 1-byte -w write_buffer() gets fd -1 (EBADF on every write) -> gf01 still ‘TPASS: Test passed’ rc=0 over its 20s run: failed non-ENOSPC writes in -w mode are never errors. cleanup() OOB unlink not checked (no ASAN/valgrind on hosts)

  • Evidence: fsx-linux.c:222-228 (memcpy then memory_compare of the same bytes); grep op_max_size shows only lines 40,48,326,327,371 (declaration/parse/help, no use); op_file_position() calls at 132,164,188,209,247 use file_size/file_max_size only.
  • Suggested action: in op_map_read compare addr to file_buff + pos.offset without the memcpy; clamp pos.size to op_max_size in op_file_position(); fix the option help strings. Otherwise drop fsx05..fsx10 as duplicates.

Mutation: pwrite ‘Z’ into the file at the map-read offset (model untouched) right before mmap -> ‘TPASS: All file operations succeed’ (-N 2000); same plus memcpy removed -> TFAIL. fsx-linux -N 2000 -o 1024 -D: 1571/1601 ops had size>1024, max 255783 -> -o ignored

testcases/kernel/fs/ftest/ftest05.c (runtest: fs/ftest05)

  • Category: WRONG (secondary: WEAK)

Old-lib tst_exit() exits with T_exitval, which is 0 when no failure was reported, so the parent counts the child as passed and that child silently stops testing. On a correct kernel a below-EOF read always returns csize, so this branch exists only to catch a bug, and it hides it. The sibling ftest01.c (of which this is a copy) uses tst_brkm(TFAIL, ...) at the same spot. Apart from this the test duplicates ftest01: it only replaces lseek with lseek64, and with max_size = 1 MiB no offset ever needs 64 bits.
  • Evidence: ftest05.c:350-354 (if (xfr != csize) { /* tst_resm commented */ tst_exit(); }); ftest01.c:356-361 (tst_brkm(TFAIL)); lib/tst_res.c:414-427 (tst_exit -> exit(T_exitval & ~TINFO)); ftest05.c:149 (max_size = K_1 * K_1).
  • Suggested action: Replace the bare tst_exit() with tst_brkm(TFAIL, NULL, “xfr=%d != %d, zero read”, …) as in ftest01. Consider dropping ftest05 as a duplicate of ftest01, or making it use offsets above 2 GiB so lseek64 actually matters.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN,MUTATION. HPE: ftest05 TPASS as-is. Mutation: in the ‘below EOF, not seen yet’ branch force xfr = csize - 1 (short read) -> every child hits the bare tst_exit() with T_exitval 0 and the run still reports ‘TPASS: Test passed.’ rc=0 -> a short read below EOF is silently ignored

testcases/kernel/fs/openfile/openfile.c (runtest: fs/openfile01)

  • Category: WRONG (secondary: WEAK)
  • Confidence: high
  • Claim under test: “Create files and open simultaneously”: N threads each fopen() the same file M times concurrently.
  • Problem: No failure can produce a FAIL result. (1) If a thread’s fopen() fails it only calls perror and pthread_exit() (lines 218-226). It never increments c.thr_sleeping, so main blocks forever in pthread_cond_wait at lines 161-162: a hang or timeout instead of TFAIL. (2) main never joins the threads. It prints TPASS “Threads are done reading” (line 185) right after the broadcast, while the threads have not yet closed their files, and then _exit(0), so thread errors after wakeup are invisible. (3) Every TFAIL path in main calls cleanup(), which only does tst_rmdir() and returns (lines 64-68), so execution continues (e.g. with fd == NULL) and still reaches TPASS and _exit(0). The exit status is therefore always 0. In the end the test checks only that fopen(“rw”) works 10x10 times, and reports even that wrongly.
  • Evidence: openfile.c:64-68, 128-131, 161-168, 185-190, 218-226.
  • Suggested action: Convert to the new API. Have threads return status, join them in main and TFAIL on any open failure, increment the counter (or use a barrier) even on error, and use tst_brk instead of falling through. Alternatively drop it: the open() limit/concurrency coverage exists in syscalls/open*, and fs_fill/stress tests cover the rest.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN,MUTATION. HPE: openfile -f10 -t10 with stdout to a file: rc=0 and 0 bytes of output (TPASS line lost, _exit(0) skips stdio flush). Mutation thread 0 fopen fails -> 10x ‘FAIL - Couldn’t open file’ then hang until timeout rc=124. Mutation TFAIL+cleanup() before TPASS in main -> rc=0, 0 bytes output: failures in main cannot fail the test

testcases/kernel/fs/racer/fs_racer_file_link.sh (runtest: via fs/fs_racer)

testcases/kernel/hotplug/cpu_hotplug/functional/cpuhotplug07.sh (runtest: cpuhotplug/cpuhotplug07)

  • Category: WRONG (secondary: FRAGILE, WEAK)
  • Confidence: high (phase 1: medium)
  • Claim under test: offlining a CPU while a kernel compile is running migrates the compile process off that CPU.
  • Problem: KCOMPILE_LOOP_PID is the cpuhotplug_do_kcompile_loop wrapper shell, which spends its time blocked in wait() for make; the make/cc children were forked before set_affinity and keep their original mask, so the compile load is never pinned to the CPU being offlined. For a sleeping task, sched_setaffinity does not move it (affine_move_task only acts on running/queued tasks), and CPU offline only pushes runnable tasks, so ps -o psr (task_cpu) of the sleeping shell just reports its last CPU: the check passes trivially when that CPU was not CPU_TO_TEST, and can falsely TFAIL when it was. Environment: the loop runs make mrproper in the -d dir (default runtest arg /usr/src/linux), destroying the user’s kernel config/build tree; bzImage target exists only on x86/arm/s390/m68k/parisc, so on arm64/ppc64 there is no compile load; cleanup kills only the shell with SIGKILL, leaving the running make tree orphaned.
  • Evidence: cpuhotplug07.sh:88-113; tools/cpuhotplug_do_kcompile_loop:17-20; include/cpuhotplug_hotplug.sh:52-58; /usr/src/linux/kernel/sched/core.c affine_move_task() (~2969: only task_on_cpu/TASK_WAKING/task_on_rq_queued paths migrate); runtest/cpuhotplug:9 -d /usr/src/linux.
  • Suggested action: pin the actual workload (taskset the whole process group / start make under taskset) and verify via /proc//status Cpus_allowed or a CPU-bound child’s psr; do not run mrproper in a user tree (copy sources to tmpdir or use a synthetic CPU load); kill the process group in cleanup. Otherwise drop (cpuhotplug04/05 cover offline/online stress).
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN,READ. HPE, safe variant with -d pointing to a fake tree whose Makefile has no-op mrproper/defconfig and a CPU-spinning bzImage: ‘TPASS: turned off CPU 1, process migrated to CPU 15’ (-l 3), yet after the test the spinning make child was still running, orphaned, with Cpus_allowed_list 0-23: the load was never pinned, only the wrapper shell. Default -d /usr/src/linux runs ‘make mrproper’ there

A compare mismatch in Test 6 does not set failflag, so TPASS is printed after the TFAIL. pos is never advanced, so all N requests hit offset 0 (claimed “given number of requests” exercise is one block). Also: io_getevents returning a negative error causes an infinite loop; iocbs = malloc(sizeof(int) * nr) under-allocates a pointer array (overflow with -n 1 on 64-bit); TC[] ftruncate cases are dead code; libaio does not set errno so the TEST_ERRNO printed is meaningless.

  • Suggested action: check event.res == bufsize after each getevents, clear dstbuf before each read in Test 6 and set failflag on mismatch, advance pos; or drop aio01 as covered by aio02 and testcases/kernel/syscalls/io_submit, io_getevents and ltp-aiodio/aio-stress.
