testcases/kernel/tracing/ftrace_test/ftrace_stress/ftrace_trace_pipe.sh (runtest: worker of tracing/ftrace-stress-test)

  • Category: WRONG
  • Confidence: high (phase 1: medium)
  • Claim under test: repeatedly open trace_pipe, read it for 200 ms, interrupt the reader, repeat.
  • Problem: In a non-interactive shell, asynchronous commands inherit SIGINT as ignored (POSIX sh “Asynchronous Lists”; same in bash and dash without job control). kill -INT $this_pid therefore does nothing to the background cat trace_pipe, which keeps blocking or reading, and wait $this_pid blocks until the driver sends SIGUSR1 at the end. trace_pipe is opened once per run instead of up to 20 times per round.
  • Evidence: ftrace_trace_pipe.sh lines 25-40 (after the license banner); POSIX XCU 2.9.3.1 “If job control is disabled … the commands in the list shall inherit from the shell a signal action of ignored (SIG_IGN) for the SIGINT and SIGQUIT signals.”
  • Suggested action: use kill -TERM (or -KILL) for the reader.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN. HPE standalone 12 s (sh -x): 1 ‘cat trace_pipe’ started, 1 ‘kill -INT’ issued, then wait blocks for the rest; cat’s SigIgn 0x7 (INT ignored; HUP from nohup). In the real driver (20 s run) only 1 distinct cat trace_pipe PID over 60 samples. Local: background job of ‘sh -c’ has SigIgn 0x6 and survives kill -INT

testcases/kernel/tracing/ftrace_test/ftrace_stress_test.sh (runtest: tracing/ftrace-stress-test)

  • Category: WRONG (secondary: WEAK)
  • Confidence: high
  • Claim under test: concurrent stress of ftrace control files finds no bugs.

Their tst_resm TFAIL calls (ftrace_set_ftrace_filter.sh, ftrace_trace_options.sh, ftrace_set_ftrace_pid.sh TBROK) only update LTP_RET_VAL in their own process, and the driver kills them with SIGKILL without collecting status. The driver itself only emits TINFO, and old-API tst_exit masks TINFO, so the test exits 0 (PASS) unless the machine crashes, and it tells the user to “Run dmesg to double-check for bugs”. It also never checks taint. Several workers are broken as well (see ftrace_set_event.sh, ftrace_set_ftrace_pid.sh, ftrace_trace.sh, ftrace_trace_pipe.sh, ftrace_tracing_enabled.sh), so the actual stress is much smaller than claimed.
  • Evidence: ftrace_stress_test.sh:61-76, 78-104, 118-120; testcases/lib/test.sh:46-52 (per-process LTP_RET_VAL), :120-124 (exit masks TINFO).
  • Suggested action: port to the new shell API, have the driver check kernel taint/dmesg after the run and propagate worker failures (e.g. via a results file), or drop the unchecked parts.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN,MUTATION. HPE: as-is (30s) exits 0 with only TINFO plus dozens of worker ‘write error: Device or resource busy’ lines; mutated ftrace_trace_options.sh worker to emit ‘tst_resm TFAIL MUTATION’ -> TFAIL printed but driver rc=0, only TINFO Finished -> worker failures never propagate

testcases/misc/crash/crash01.c (runtest: crashme/crash01)

  • Category: WRONG (secondary: WEAK)
  • Confidence: high
  • Claim under test: “Test OS robustness by creating a string of random bytes and then jump to it”: random instructions are executed and the faults they raise are caught by signal handlers.
  • Problem: The random bytes are put in a malloc() buffer (bad_malloc(), compute_block_badboy()) and then called through a function pointer. The only mprotect(PROT_EXEC) is under #ifdef pyr (Pyramid hardware), so on every current Linux arch with NX (x86_64, arm64, ppc64, s390x…) the heap is not executable. Every (*badboy)() faults with SIGSEGV on instruction fetch at the first byte. No random instruction ever runs, so the test exercises only “SIGSEGV + longjmp” ntries times. The result is TPASS (“we’re still here”) unconditionally, and the child’s exit status is only printed, never checked.
  • Evidence: crash01.c:344-354 (mprotect only #ifdef pyr), :502-506 (call into heap), :193 (unconditional TPASS); arch/x86/include/asm/elf.h:261-285 (x86_64 with NX: READ_IMPLIES_EXEC never set, “exec-none” for heap mappings).
  • Suggested action: Put the random code in an mmap(PROT_READ|PROT_WRITE|PROT_EXEC) area, or mprotect() the buffer to PROT_EXEC (and flush the icache with builtin_clear_cache on non-x86 instead of the ppc-only asm). Otherwise drop it: it duplicates nothing useful as it stands.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN,MUTATION. HPE: crash01 -v 5 -n 50 -s 1 as-is: 50/50 ‘Got signal 11’ (fetch from NX heap), TPASS; mutated bad_malloc() to mmap PROT_EXEC: same seed gives 42x SIGSEGV + 8x SIGILL -> as-is no random byte is ever executed, TPASS is unconditional

testcases/misc/math/float/exp_log/genldexp.c (helper for math/float_exp_log)

For a double holding an integer <= 20000 the low 32 bits of the IEEE-754 encoding are zero. On little-endian, every int written to ildexp_inp.ref is therefore 0, so ldexp(x, 0) == x for all 20000 points and the exponent path is never exercised. On big-endian the exponents become huge values from the double’s high word. The test still passes because create_Result_file() reads back the same garbage.
  • Evidence: exp_log/genldexp.c create_Data_file(): double tabDD[20000], tabDI[20000], tabDI[i] = nbVal - i;, write(fpi, &tabDI[i], sizeof(int));.
  • Suggested action: Declare tabDI as int.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via BUILD,RUN. local x86_64 build of genldexp.c, ./genldexp 1: od -td4 ildexp_inp.ref | sort -u -> single value 0 for all 20000 exponents (doubles’ low word), so ldexp(x,0)==x is all that float_exp_log checks for ldexp

testcases/misc/math/nextafter/nextafter01.c (runtest: math/nextafter01)

  • Category: WRONG (secondary: WEAK, DOCS)
  • Confidence: high
  • Claim under test: nextafter(1.0, 1.1) returns the next double above 1.0, nextafter(1.0, 0.9) returns the next double below 1.0, and nextafter(1.0, 1.0) returns 1.0.

So check != 1.0 is false and block 2 passes for any return value. Block 1 passes when check == answer or (float)check == 1.0. A broken nextafter() that returns 1.0 unchanged gives check == 1.0 == answer and passes too. Only block 3 (x == y) really checks anything. The header names the test “scalb”.

testcases/network/dhcp/dhcp_lib.sh (runtest: net.tcp_cmds/dhcpd, dnsmasq; net.ipv6/dhcpd6, dnsmasq6)

  • Category: WRONG (secondary: FRAGILE)
  • Confidence: high (phase 1: medium)
  • Claim under test: the DHCP server starts on ltp_veth0, and dhclient on ltp_veth1 gets the single configured address.
  • Problem: The “did the server start” check after sleep 1 is if [ "$(pgrep '$dhcp_name')" ]; then ... tst_brk TBROK "Failed to start". It has two bugs. The single quotes make pgrep look for the literal string $dhcp_name, so it never matches. The logic is also inverted: it breaks when the process IS found. So the check is dead code and a server that fails to start goes unnoticed. The test then reports TFAIL “not configured by DHCP” instead of TBROK. Readiness also depends only on sleep 1. dhclient retries, which hides most of that, so impact is small. The final address/prefix assertion itself is sound.
  • Evidence: dhcp_lib.sh:128-133.
  • Suggested action: Replace with pgrep -x "$dhcp_name" >/dev/null || { print_dhcp_log; tst_brk TBROK "Failed to start $dhcp_name"; }, and wait for the process or listening socket instead of using sleep 1.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via READ,GIT,RUN. test cannot run here (dhcpd/dnsmasq/dhclient absent on both Fedora hosts -> TCONF via TST_NEEDS_CMDS); replayed the check in sh: with a process named fakedhcpd running and after it exited, [ “(pgrep′dhcp_name’)” ] is false both times (literal regex ‘$dhcp_name’ can never match) -> dead check; introduced in 0095b0b70c8d (2014)

testcases/network/lib6/asapi_01.c (runtest: net.ipv6_lib/asapi_01)

  • Category: WRONG (secondary: FRAGILE)
  • Confidence: high
  • Claim under test: RFC 3542 sec. 3.1 IPV6_CHECKSUM: with the option set, the kernel computes the checksum and stores it at the given offset of raw IPv6 packets.
  • Problem: The receive-side checksum verification is a no-op. Line 324-325 computes the pseudo-header plus packet sum into cs and then never uses it. Line 326 tests if (!csum(0, rpbuf, xlen)), which is the checksum of the payload alone, without the pseudo-header. For these 0xA5-filled payloads that value is non-zero whether the kernel wrote a correct checksum, a wrong one, or none. Every positive case therefore reports TPASS after only the data-corruption check. Two smaller problems: in the setsockopt path, a failure is reported as TPASS (line 270) before the errno check at line 275, so a wrong errno for the odd-offset case is never detected. The subtests 2.3/2.4 (IN6_ARE_ADDR_EQUAL, getprotobyname) depend on /etc/protocols containing the RFC names, which is not always true in minimal containers.
  • Evidence: asapi_01.c:323-331, 263-279; kernel net/ipv6/raw.c:536-537 (EINVAL when offset >= total_len - 1) and :1015-1016 (odd offset -> EINVAL), so the expected errnos are right but the success check is broken.
  • Suggested action: Replace line 326 with if (cs != 0) (the checksum over pseudo-header plus packet must fold to 0, or 0xffff depending on the csum() convention). Check TEST_ERRNO == EINVAL before reporting TPASS for the setsockopt failure case. Consider porting to the new API.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN,MUTATION. HPE: as-is 17 TPASS; instrumented: correct packets give full pseudo-hdr cs=0x0 but payload-only csum 0xb600/0xcf00/0x8508 (what line 326 tests); mutated to XOR the 2 checksum bytes after recv (wrong checksum): full cs=0x99d5.. yet all IPV6_CHECKSUM cases TPASS -> check vacuous, ‘cs != 0’ fix validated

testcases/network/lib6/getaddrinfo_01.c (runtest: net.ipv6_lib/getaddrinfo_01)

  • Category: WRONG (secondary: WEAK)
  • Confidence: high
  • Claim under test: getaddrinfo() rejects inconsistent socktype/protocol hints (SOCK_STREAM + IPPROTO_UDP).
  • Problem: The subcase calls check_addrinfo(0, "SOCK_STREAM/IPPROTO_UDP", NULL, 0, NULL, 0, SOCK_STREAM, IPPROTO_UDP, NULL), i.e. node == NULL and service == NULL. getaddrinfo() returns EAI_NONAME for that before it looks at the hints, so the “failed as expected” TPASS never tests the socktype/protocol consistency check. A glibc that accepted SOCK_STREAM/IPPROTO_UDP would still pass. Separately, check_addrinfo_badflags() after “0+service” treats EAI_BADFLAGS as TPASS even though that call (flags 0) is expected to succeed. This is a weak, permissive check.
  • Evidence: getaddrinfo_01.c:254-258, 239-241; getaddrinfo(3) ERRORS: “EAI_NONAME The node or service is not known; or both node and service are NULL”; “EAI_SOCKTYPE … if hints.ai_socktype and hints.ai_protocol are inconsistent (e.g., SOCK_DGRAM and IPPROTO_TCP)”. glibc getaddrinfo() checks name == NULL && service == NULL first.
  • Suggested action: Pass a node (e.g. hostname or “127.0.0.1”) and/or a numeric service, and expect EAI_SOCKTYPE or EAI_SERVICE (TST_EXP with an accepted set). Drop the badflags acceptance for the flags==0 call.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN,MUTATION. HPE: as-is passed 22; mutated the subcase to consistent hints SOCK_DGRAM/IPPROTO_UDP (still node=NULL service=NULL): getaddrinfo ret=-2 EAI_NONAME ‘Name or service not known’ and ‘SOCK_STREAM/IPPROTO_UDP: failed as expected’ TPASS for IPv4 and IPv6 -> subcase never tests socktype/protocol consistency
  • Verification (phase 3, glibc vs musl build and libc sources): CONFIRMED via MUSL,RUN,SRC. HPE glibc 22 TPASS, musl 22 TPASS. NULL/NULL short-circuits in both: glibc nss/getaddrinfo.c:2301, musl network/getaddrinfo.c:22 -> EAI_NONAME. Probe node=127.0.0.1 SOCK_STREAM/IPPROTO_UDP: glibc -7 EAI_SOCKTYPE, musl -8 EAI_SERVICE (lookup_serv.c:20-27); a fixed test must accept both

testcases/network/multicast/mc_member/mc_member.sh (runtest: net.multicast/mc_member)

  • Category: WRONG (secondary: FRAGILE)

testcases/network/multicast/mc_opts/mc_opts.sh (runtest: net.multicast/mc_opts)

TTL is -t. The ping -I 3.3.3.3 check passes only because bind() to a non-local address fails, and it would hang or behave differently with net.ipv4.ip_nonlocal_bind=1. The helper mc_verify_opts_error does not generate any error (see below). The whole sequence is repeated 10 times with no variation.

  • Suggested action: Drop the ping -T line, or replace it with a setsockopt(IP_MULTICAST_TTL, 256) check expecting EINVAL (net/ipv4/ip_sockglue.c: val > 255 -> EINVAL). Drop the 10x loop. Move the checks into a single C test.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN,VIRT. VIRT: mc_opts.sh TPASS ‘Test Successful’; ‘ping -T 777 224.0.0.1’ -> ‘ping: invalid timestamp type: 777’ rc=2 (iputils CLI parse error, -T is timestamp, not TTL) -> the ‘out of range’ check never reaches the kernel; 10x loop repeats identical steps

testcases/network/nfs/nfs_stress/nfs02.sh (runtest: net.nfs/nfs02_*)

  • Category: WRONG
  • Confidence: high

  • Problem: test3 runs ROD chmod a-wx ascii.sm; ROD ls -l ascii.sm | grep -q "r--"; ROD chmod a+w ascii.sm. The second line is a pipeline. ROD only wraps ls (in a subshell), and the exit status of grep is never checked (no ||, no set -e). Also “r–” matches the original -rw-r--r-- mode as well. So a server or client that dropped the chmod would still get “test3 passed”. Only a chmod error can fail it.
  • Evidence: nfs02.sh:40-47.
  • Suggested action: Use EXPECT_PASS "[ \"\$(stat -c %A ascii.sm)\" = '-r--r--r--' ]" (or compare stat -c %a to 444). Optionally verify on rhost as well.

VIRT (nfs-server started, -v 4.2 -t tcp): as-is passed 12; mutated ‘ROD chmod a-wx ascii.sm’ to ‘true’: ‘TPASS: test3 passed’ in all 3 iterations, passed 12 failed 0 rc=0 -> permission check vacuous (grep r– matches -rw-r–r–, grep status unchecked)

testcases/network/nfs/nfs_stress/nfs03.sh (runtest: net.nfs/nfs03_*)

  • Category: WRONG (secondary: WEAK)
  • Confidence: high
  • Claim under test: multiple processes creating and deleting files on NFS concurrently succeed.
  • Problem: touch_files and rm_files (each with ROD per file) run as & background subshells. In the shell API, tst_res/tst_brk counters are shell variables (testcases/lib/tst_test.sh:104-127), so a ROD failure inside the subshell only exits that subshell. Worse, it runs the cleanup (unmount/unexport) from the subshell. The parent’s wait $pid1 / wait $pid3 ignore the exit status, and tst_res TPASS "test done" is unconditional. Only the foreground rm_files in dir2 can fail the test, and rm -f effectively never fails. The final state of the directories is not verified either.
  • Evidence: nfs03.sh:46-78; tst_test.sh:104-127.
  • Suggested action: Check wait $pid || tst_res TFAIL ... for every background job, and use plain commands in the subshells (exit non-zero instead of ROD). Verify file counts after creation and that the directories are empty after removal.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN,MUTATION,VIRT. VIRT -v 4.2 -t tcp: as-is TPASS x3; mutA (background touch_files creates nothing): ‘TPASS: test done’ x3 rc=0 -> creation never verified; mutB (ROD touch fails in bg subshell): subshell runs cleanup (22 umount retries while parent busy), parent’s rm then TBROKs, rc=6 -> failure only surfaces indirectly via the cleanup side effect

testcases/network/rpc/rpc-tirpc/tests_pack/rpc_suite/tirpc/tirpc_bottomlevel_clnt_vc_create/tirpc_clnt_vc_create.c (runtest: net.tirpc_tests tirpc_clnt_vc_create)

  • Category: WRONG
  • Confidence: high (phase 1: medium)
  • Claim under test: clnt_vc_create() creates a connection-oriented (TCP) client handle.
  • Problem: The fd handed to clnt_vc_create() is created with bound_socket(AF_INET, SOCK_DGRAM), although the address is resolved via getnetconfigent(“tcp”) and the server tirpc_svc_5 listens on a SOCK_STREAM socket. clnt_vc_create() connect()s the fd if it is not connected yet; connect() on a UDP socket always succeeds without any peer, so the handle is created but no TCP connection to the server is ever made. The test therefore passes even if the TCP service is down and does not exercise the vc path. The bug was introduced in 7583b965e18a (“rpc-tirpc: the bottom-level fixes”), which switched the netconfig to tcp but used SOCK_DGRAM (likely copy-paste from tirpc_clnt_dg_create.c).
  • Evidence: tirpc_clnt_vc_create.c “sock = bound_socket(AF_INET, SOCK_DGRAM);” followed by clnt_vc_create(sock, &svcaddr, …); tirpc_svc_5.c server_defs “tcp … SOCK_STREAM”.

  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN,MUTATION,BUILD. HPE as-is TPASS. Mutation: after rpcb_getaddr set svcaddr port to 9 (closed): with the test’s SOCK_DGRAM fd -> still TPASS; same mutation with SOCK_STREAM -> TFAIL (connect refused). So no TCP connection to tirpc_svc_5 is ever made. VIRT as-is 3/3 TPASS. The rpc-tirpc suite builds and installs completely and was run through rpc_test.sh with rpcbind running.

testcases/network/stress/multicast/grp-operation/mcast-lib.sh (helper; affects runtest net_stress.multicast/mcast4-group-same-group, mcast6-group-same-group, mcast4-group-source-filter, mcast6-group-source-filter)

  • Problem: The loop collects the PIDs and then does for pid in $pids; do wait $pid; done without looking at the exit status, and then prints tst_res TPASS "test is finished successfully" unconditionally. ns-mcast_join exits with EXIT_FAILURE via fatal_error() when MCAST_JOIN_GROUP, MCAST_MSFILTER or MCAST_LEAVE_GROUP fails (ns-mcast_join.c:463-478), so a kernel that rejects the joins, filters or leaves still gets TPASS. The only thing that can fail the test is a hang or a kernel crash.
  • Evidence: mcast-lib.sh:131-146; ns-tools/ns-mcast_join.c:463-478, 518.
  • Suggested action: collect the status, e.g. for pid in $pids; do wait $pid || ret=1; done, and report TFAIL when any ns-mcast_join failed (TPASS only when all succeeded).
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN,MUTATION. HPE: same-group/source-filter TPASS as-is (v4 and -6). Mutated lib copy (PATH first) sets igmp_max_memberships=0 so the kernel rejects every join: mcast-group-same-group.sh and mcast-group-source-filter.sh print 20x ‘setsockopt(): Failed to join a group: No buffer space available’ and still ‘TPASS: test is finished successfully’.

testcases/network/stress/ns-tools/ns-icmp_redirector.c (helper; used by runtest net_stress.route/route4-redirect, route6-redirect via route-redirect.sh)

  • Category: WRONG (secondary: UNDEF)

The redirector runs daemonised (-b), so if it crashes or misbehaves nobody notices, and route6-redirect still prints TPASS, because route-redirect.sh only checks that ns-udpsender could send. (2) In return_neigh_adv() the “DAD NS: do nothing” early return sits inside if (debug) { ... }, so in normal runs the tool answers DAD Neighbor Solicitations with a Neighbor Advertisement, which makes any address that lhost configures during the test fail DAD.

  • Suggested action: allocate sizeof(struct ip6_gateway_info) (or use a static struct, as there is only one); move the return out of the debug block. Better, have route-redirect.sh verify that a redirect was actually applied (e.g. ip route get $DST_HOST shows the redirected gateway, or the IcmpInRedirects / Icmp6InRedirects counters grew).
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN,MUTATION,BUILD. gcc -O2 -Wall: ‘allocation of insufficient size 16 for type struct ip6_gateway_info with size 40’. HPE route-redirect.sh -6 with a logging-instrumented redirector: ‘gw_p usable=24 bytes, copying 40 bytes’, next call usable=0 (heap header smashed), only 1 Icmp6InRedirects (as-is: 10), still TPASS. DAD-NS branch never hit in this test.

testcases/network/stress/ns-tools/ns-mcast_receiver.c (helper for runtest: net_stress.multicast mcast4/6-pktfld01/02)

  • Category: WRONG
  • Confidence: medium

  • Problem: msgbuf_size is size_t (8 bytes) but is filled by getsockopt(SO_RCVBUF) with optlen = sizeof(size_t). The kernel clamps len to sizeof(int) and copies only 4 bytes, so the upper 32 bits of msgbuf_size are uninitialized stack data; malloc(msgbuf_size + 1) can then fail (or allocate a huge buffer) and the receiver exits. Since mcast-pktfld* start it with -b (daemonized), its exit is never seen and the test passes with no receive-side load. Also SO_REUSEADDR is set after bind() (no effect).

  • Suggested action: use int for the getsockopt result (then cast), or zero-init msgbuf_size; move SO_REUSEADDR before bind().
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN,MUTATION. HPE instrumented receiver: getsockopt(SO_RCVBUF) returns optlen=4, msgbuf_size=212992 (upper half happened to be 0). Mutation pre-filling msgbuf_size=0x5a5a5a5a00000000 (stale stack): logged 0x5a5a5a5a00034000, receiver gone in 22/22 samples, mcast-pktfld01 still TPASS. Latent: harmless only while the stack slot is 0.

testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/definitions/errno_h/3-2.c (openposix: conformance/definitions/errno_h/3-2)

  • Category: WRONG
  • Confidence: high
  • Claim under test: errno symbolic constants have unique values (except permitted aliases).
  • Problem: The failure condition is tst->value == sym[i].value && tst->duplicate != sym[i].value && strcmp(names). For every entry except EAGAIN/EWOULDBLOCK, duplicate equals value, so whenever tst->value == sym[i].value holds, tst->duplicate != sym[i].value is false. The check can therefore never report a duplicate (e.g. EIO==EINVAL would pass). The test passes unconditionally.
  • Evidence: 3-2.c table (third field = own value) and the if() in test_main.
  • Suggested action: rewrite as: fail if values equal and names differ, unless the pair is an allowed alias (EAGAIN/EWOULDBLOCK, ENOTSUP/EOPNOTSUPP, which POSIX explicitly lets coincide). Note on Linux ENOTSUP==EOPNOTSUPP, so the allow-list must include that pair.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN,MUTATION. HPE: errno_h_3-2.run-test rc=0 (PASS) although ENOTSUP==EOPNOTSUPP==95 on Linux and the table marks neither as an alias (dup field = own value). Mutation: table entry EINVAL changed to {EIO, “EINVAL”, EIO} (simulated EINVAL==EIO) -> 3-2mut rc=0 PASS. Duplicate check cannot fire.

Guard dropped only -> UNRESOLVED ‘Could not fail queuing 1024 request’. Never tests EAGAIN on glibc
  • Verification (phase 3, glibc vs musl build and libc sources): UNCHANGED via MUSL,RUN,SRC. HPE glibc: rc=4 UNSUPPORTED; musl: rc=4 UNSUPPORTED. musl src/conf/sysconf.c:55 _SC_AIO_MAX=-1, glibc sysdeps/posix/sysconf.c:230-235 -1 (no AIO_MAX). The broken EAGAIN logic is never reached on either Linux libc; phase-2 mutation stands

testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/interfaces/fork/1-1.c (openposix: conformance/interfaces/fork/1-1)

  • Category: WRONG (secondary: FRAGILE)
  • Confidence: high (phase 1: medium)
  • Claim under test: fork() creates a new process that runs concurrently.
  • Problem: sem_open(SEM_NAME, O_CREAT, O_RDWR, 0) passes O_RDWR (2) as the permission mode, so the semaphore is created with mode 0002 & ~umask (0 with umask 022). Parent and child each call sem_open() after fork(). Whichever creates the semaphore succeeds, but the other one’s open(O_RDWR) of the existing object fails with EACCES unless it is root (CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE). As non-root: if the parent wins, the child exits UNRESOLVED without posting, and the parent’s sem_timedwait() times out and reports FAILED “The new process does not execute”. If the child wins, the parent reports UNRESOLVED. The “try executing as root” hint papers over the bug. The same O_RDWR-as-mode pattern is in fork/14-1.c and fork/21-1.c. Separately, the >= 2 s total-duration check on CLOCK_REALTIME for two concurrent sleep(1) calls can false-FAIL under load or clock steps.
  • Evidence: fork/1-1.c:77-80, 103-110, 135-142; sem_open(3): “oflag … mode specifies the permissions to be placed on the new semaphore”.
  • Suggested action: Create the semaphore before fork() with mode 0600 (S_IRUSR|S_IWUSR), or use an unnamed pshared semaphore in shared memory. Measure duration with CLOCK_MONOTONIC.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN,REPEAT,STRESS,VIRT. Root: PASS 14/14 (HPE 1+5+5 stress, VIRT 3). As nobody (setpriv –reuid=65534): run1 ‘Failed to open the semaphore (try executing as root)’ EACCES + parent ‘FAILED: The new process does not execute’ rc=1; runs 2-3 both sides EACCES rc=2 (stale mode-0 /semfork1_1 left by run1, removed by next root run’s sem_unlink)

testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/interfaces/fork/6-1.c (openposix: conformance/interfaces/fork/6-1)

testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/interfaces/mmap/21-1.c (openposix: conformance/interfaces/mmap/21-1)

  • Category: WRONG
  • Confidence: high
  • Claim under test: mmap() fails with EINVAL when flags is invalid (neither MAP_PRIVATE nor MAP_SHARED is set).
  • Problem: flags = ~0 sets MAP_SHARED and MAP_PRIVATE together, plus MAP_ANONYMOUS, MAP_HUGETLB and an invalid MAP_HUGE size encoding. On Linux, ksys_mmap_pgoff() takes the anonymous+MAP_HUGETLB branch, hstate_sizelog(63) returns NULL, and EINVAL comes back before the mapping-type validation in do_mmap() runs and before fd is even looked at. The claimed condition (no type flag) is never exercised; the test passes because of an unrelated hugetlb check.
  • Evidence: mmap/21-1.c:37 (int flag = ~0), :54; kernel mm/mmap.c:588-604 (MAP_ANONYMOUS / MAP_HUGETLB -> hstate_sizelog -> -EINVAL).
  • Suggested action: use flags = 0 (neither MAP_SHARED nor MAP_PRIVATE, no other bits) on the regular file fd to test the stated condition.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN,MUTATION. HPE as-is PASS. Probe mmap(len 1024, RW, flags, fd): ~0 with valid fd, fd=-1 and fd=9999 all EINVAL (fd never examined -> hugetlb sizelog EINVAL in ksys_mmap_pgoff); 0&MAP_HUGETLB -> EACCES; flags=0 (the claimed condition) -> EINVAL. Stated condition not what is tested

testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/interfaces/mmap/27-1.c (openposix: conformance/interfaces/mmap/27-1)

  • Category: WRONG
  • Confidence: high
  • Claim under test: MAP_PRIVATE and MAP_FIXED “should either fail with ENOTSUP or SUCCEED”.
  • Problem: the errno checks are inverted in both sub-cases. “if (errno != ENOTSUP) printf(not supported) else { err++; }” counts a failure only when errno IS ENOTSUP, the outcome POSIX allows, and silently accepts every other errno. A conforming ENOTSUP implementation would FAIL, and a broken one returning e.g. EINVAL would PASS. Linux makes both calls succeed, so neither branch runs and the test is ineffective there.
  • Evidence: mmap/27-1.c:61-68 and :83-89.
  • Suggested action: swap the branches (count err++ when errno != ENOTSUP). Also note the MAP_FIXED sub-case munmaps len rather than len/2 (harmless).
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN,MUTATION. HPE: as-is PASS (both mmaps succeed on Linux, neither errno branch runs). Mutation: #define mmap wrapper forcing MAP_PRIVATE/MAP_FIXED calls to fail: errno=ENOTSUP (POSIX-allowed) -> rc=1 ‘MAP_PRIVATE failed with: Operation not supported’ FAIL; errno=EINVAL (non-conforming) -> rc=0 ‘MAP_PRIVATE is not supported … Test PASSED’. Branches inverted.

testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/interfaces/mmap/9-1.c (runtest: openposix: conformance/interfaces/mmap/9-1)

  • Category: WRONG
  • Confidence: high (phase 1: medium)
  • Claim under test: mmap() with MAP_FIXED and an addr that is not page aligned fails with EINVAL.
  • Problem: The second mmap passes flags = MAP_FIXED alone, with neither MAP_SHARED nor MAP_PRIVATE. That is an invalid flags value by itself and also gives EINVAL (POSIX: “The value of flags is invalid (neither MAP_PRIVATE nor MAP_SHARED is set)”; Linux do_mmap switch default -> -EINVAL). So the test passes whether or not the misaligned-addr check works. On current Linux the alignment check in __get_unmapped_area runs before the MAP_TYPE switch, so the test does reach the intended path today, but only by accident of check order. The result of the first mmap is also not checked against MAP_FAILED.
  • Evidence: 9-1.c:79 mmap(illegal_addr, size, PROT_READ | PROT_WRITE, MAP_FIXED, fd, 0); mm/mmap.c:874 offset_in_page(addr) -> -EINVAL comes before mm/mmap.c:443/491 MAP_TYPE switch default -> -EINVAL.
  • Suggested action: Use MAP_FIXED | MAP_SHARED (or MAP_PRIVATE) so the misaligned addr is the only error. Check the first mmap result.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN,MUTATION. HPE as-is PASS. Mutation illegal_addr=pa (page-aligned, legal) with flags MAP_FIXED alone -> still ‘Test PASSED’ rc=0 (EINVAL comes from missing MAP_SHARED/PRIVATE). Control: MAP_FIXED|MAP_SHARED + misaligned -> PASS; MAP_FIXED|MAP_SHARED + aligned -> FAIL. Test passes even when addr is legal: vacuous.

testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/interfaces/mq_notify/2-1.c (runtest: openposix: conformance/interfaces/mq_notify/2-1)

  • Category: WRONG
  • Confidence: high
  • Claim under test: Only one process can be registered for notification; a second registration from another process fails.
  • Problem: The assertion is checked in the child, which returns PTS_FAIL (1) or PTS_PASS (0). The parent does wait(&status); return status;, so it returns the raw wait status. A child exit code of 1 becomes status 0x100, and return 0x100 from test_main -> main -> exit(256) gives exit code 0 (only the low 8 bits are kept). So the child’s FAIL (and UNRESOLVED, 0x200) is reported as PASS, and the test can never fail unless the child is killed by a signal.
  • Evidence: 2-1.c:82-84 wait(&status); mqclean(...); return status;; lib/common.c:12 return test_main(argc, argv);
  • Suggested action: Return WIFEXITED(status) ? WEXITSTATUS(status) : PTS_UNRESOLVED.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN,MUTATION. HPE as-is PASS. Mutation: parent calls mq_notify(mqdes, NULL) before fork so the child’s registration succeeds -> child prints ‘Test FAILED’ and returns PTS_FAIL, parent returns raw wait status 256 -> process exit code 0 (PASS). Child failure is masked.

testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/interfaces/mq_notify/9-1.c (runtest: openposix: conformance/interfaces/mq_notify/9-1)

  • Category: WRONG
  • Confidence: high
  • Claim under test: mq_notify fails with EBUSY if another process is already registered.
  • Problem: Same status bug as 2-1: the EBUSY check runs in the child, and the parent returns the raw wait() status. Child PTS_FAIL (1) -> status 256 -> exit(256) -> exit code 0 = PASS. A missing EBUSY, or a wrong errno, is never reported.
  • Evidence: 9-1.c:87-89 wait(&status); mqclean(...); return status;; lib/common.c:12.
  • Suggested action: Return WEXITSTATUS(status) when WIFEXITED, else PTS_UNRESOLVED.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN,MUTATION. HPE as-is PASS. Mutation: parent calls mq_notify(mqdes, NULL) before fork so the child’s registration succeeds -> child prints ‘Test FAILED’ and returns PTS_FAIL, parent returns raw wait status 256 -> process exit code 0 (PASS). Child failure is masked.

testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/interfaces/mq_receive/13-1.c (runtest: openposix: conformance/interfaces/mq_receive/13-1)

  • Category: WRONG (phase 1: FRAGILE) (secondary: WRONG)
  • Confidence: high (phase 1: medium)
  • Claim under test: mq_receive fails with EINTR when interrupted by a signal.
  • Problem: mq_open() is called with attr.mq_maxmsg = 40. Without CAP_SYS_RESOURCE (non-root run, rootless container), or if fs.mqueue.msg_max is lowered, Linux rejects maxmsg > msg_max (default 10) with EINVAL. The test only sets unresolved = 1 and keeps going with mqdes == (mqd_t)-1. The call under test then fails with EBADF, which sets failure = 1, and failure is reported before unresolved, so a correct kernel gets FAIL instead of UNRESOLVED. The synchronisation is also sleep-based: the child does sleep(2) then kill(getppid(), SIGABRT), assuming the parent is already blocked in mq_receive with the handler installed. If the parent is not yet in mq_receive, the handler runs early and mq_receive blocks forever (timeout). The failure message says “errno != EINVAL” but EINTR is checked.
  • Evidence: testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/interfaces/mq_receive/13-1.c:51-72; ipc/mqueue.c:351-358 (maxmsg > ipc_ns->mq_msg_max -> -EINVAL unless capable(CAP_SYS_RESOURCE)); mq_open(3) ERRORS: “In a process that is unprivileged … attr->mq_maxmsg must be less than or equal to the msg_max limit”.
  • Suggested action: Return PTS_UNRESOLVED right after a failed mq_open, and use mq_maxmsg <= 10 (the assertion does not need 40 slots).
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): REVISED via RUN,MUTATION,REPEAT,STRESS,VIRT. HPE root PASS; nobody -> rc=2 UNRESOLVED (not FAIL): errno is read after wait(NULL), which the child’s SIGABRT interrupts with EINTR. Mutant mq_receive((mqd_t)-1,…) (EBADF) -> Test PASSED 3/3: EINTR check is vacuous. Parent delayed 2.5s before mq_receive -> hang rc=124. As-is 13/13 VIRT (plain/stress/SCHED_IDLE) PASS.
  • Verification conclusion: The errno check runs after wait(NULL). The child’s SIGABRT interrupts that wait() with EINTR whenever mq_receive returned early, so any fast failure of mq_receive passes. That is also why the unprivileged run gives UNRESOLVED, not the FAIL phase 1 predicted. The sleep(2) synchronisation can hang (mutant L) but did not misfire in 13 loaded runs. Fix: save errno right after mq_receive (before wait), keep the maxmsg <= 10 / early-UNRESOLVED fix and the signal-sync fix.

testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/interfaces/mq_send/7-1.c (runtest: openposix: conformance/interfaces/mq_send/7-1)

  • Category: WRONG
  • Confidence: high (phase 1: low)
  • Claim under test: With O_NONBLOCK on a full queue, mq_send returns an error and the message is not queued.
  • Problem: The “not queued” check is strcmp(msgptr, msgrcd) == 0, but msgrcd is an uninitialised stack buffer filled by mq_receive with exactly the message bytes and no NUL terminator. If the kernel wrongly queued the highest-priority “message 10”, strcmp would read past the received bytes into garbage and most likely report “different”, so the bug would go undetected. The EAGAIN errno check is sound.
  • Evidence: 7-1.c:42 (msgrcd uninitialised), 7-1.c:72-79.
  • Suggested action: Compare using the length returned by mq_receive (memcmp plus a length check), or zero-initialise msgrcd.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN,MUTATION. HPE as-is PASS. Mutation emulating the bug (after EAGAIN: drain one msg, mq_send the rejected ‘message 10’ at top prio) -> still Test PASSED 5/5: strcmp on non-NUL-terminated msgrcd misses it. Same mutant with msgrcd zero-initialised -> ‘Error: Received message that caused EAGAIN’ FAIL 5/5.

testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/interfaces/mq_timedsend/7-1.c (openposix: conformance/interfaces/mq_timedsend/7-1)

  • Category: WRONG
  • Confidence: low (phase 1: medium)
  • Claim under test: with O_NONBLOCK on a full queue, mq_timedsend fails with EAGAIN and the message is not queued.
  • Problem: The EAGAIN half works. The “not queued” half receives into char msgrcd[BUFFER], which is uninitialized, then calls strcmp(msgptr, msgrcd). mq_receive() returns a byte count and does not NUL-terminate. If the rejected highest-priority message had been queued, msgrcd would hold “message 5” followed by stack garbage, and strcmp would usually report a mismatch. So the check cannot reliably detect the failure it exists for.
  • Evidence: 7-1.c: if ((strcmp(msgptr, msgrcd) == 0) && (maxreached != 0)); mq_receive(3): “returns the number of bytes in the received message”.
  • Suggested action: Use the length that mq_receive returns: compare with memcmp/strncmp on that length, or NUL-terminate msgrcd[ret].
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): REVISED via RUN,MUTATION. HPE as-is PASS. Same mutant as mq_send/7-1 (rejected ‘message 5’ queued at top prio): detected, ‘Error: Received message that caused EAGAIN’ FAIL 5/5 even without zero-init (stack byte after msg happens to be NUL in this build); zero-init variant FAIL 5/5. Flaw is real UB but harmless on this build; mq_send/7-1 twin misses it 5/5.
  • Verification conclusion: The strcmp-on-unterminated-buffer flaw is real (undefined behaviour), but with this build’s stack layout the byte after “message 5” happens to be NUL, so the check does detect the bug. Its near-twin mq_send/7-1 misses it 5/5. Keep as a low-confidence WRONG (works by luck, compiler/stack dependent); same fix.

testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/interfaces/nanosleep/2-1.c (openposix: conformance/interfaces/nanosleep/2-1)

  • Category: WRONG
  • Confidence: high
  • Claim under test: nanosleep() sleeps at least rqtp for a range of intervals (1 ns .. 999999900 ns).
  • Problem: clock_gettime(&tsbefore) runs once before the loop and is never refreshed. Each iteration therefore compares the cumulative time since the start of the loop with the current interval. Earlier sleeps are added in, so a nanosleep that returned early would often go unnoticed. Once the total passes 1 s (after the 750 ms entry, about 1.56 s total), the slepts >= 1 branch makes the 999999900 ns check always pass.
  • Evidence: 2-1.c: clock_gettime(test_clock, &tsbefore) before for (i = 0; ...); inside the loop only tsafter is updated; if (slepts >= 1 || sleptns > sleepnsec[i]).
  • Suggested action: Move the tsbefore clock_gettime into the loop, directly before each nanosleep.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN,MUTATION. HPE as-is PASS. Mutation: 750ms interval sleeps 0 and 999999900ns interval sleeps 200ms -> rc=0 ‘PASS slept 0s 811831527ns >= 750000000’, ‘PASS slept 1s 11965884ns >= 999999900’, All tests PASSED: cumulative tsbefore hides early returns.

testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/interfaces/pthread_atfork/1-1.c (openposix: conformance/interfaces/pthread_atfork/1-1)

  • Category: WRONG
  • Confidence: high
  • Claim under test: the prepare, parent and child fork handlers are all called (“3. Verify that all three fork handlers were called”).
  • Problem: The child-handler check is a copy-paste of the parent check: if (parent_val == 1) { if (parent_val == 1) {...} else "child handler not called" }. child_val is never read, so the “child handler not called” branch cannot run. Reading child_val in the parent would not help either, because the child handler runs only in the child process, and the child calls pthread_exit(0) without reporting anything. The child-handler part of the assertion is not verified at all.
  • Evidence: pthread_atfork/1-1.c, nested if (parent_val == 1) twice in the result block; the child branch is pthread_exit(0);.
  • Suggested action: In the child, exit(child_val == HANDLER_CALLED ? 0 : 1), and in the parent check WEXITSTATUS from waitpid(). 1-2.c already does this correctly, so 1-1 could also be dropped.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN,MUTATION,GIT. HPE: 1-1 PASS as-is; mutated pthread_atfork(prepare,parent,NULL) (no child handler registered) still ‘Test PASSED’ rc=0 -> child-handler check vacuous (second ‘if (parent_val == 1)’ is a copy-paste, present since the 1.2 import).

testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/interfaces/pthread_join/6-3.c (openposix: conformance/interfaces/pthread_join/6-3)

  • Category: WRONG
  • Confidence: high
  • Claim under test: pthread_join() never returns EINTR when signals hit the joining thread.
  • Problem: main() starts the two signal-sender threads and then sets do_it1 = 0 straight away (lines 236-238), before the sleep(1) measurement window (line 240). Each sender passes sem_wait() once (the semaphore starts at 1), sends at most one kill() and leaves its loop. If do_it1 is already 0 when a sender starts, it sends nothing. For the rest of the second the worker joins threads with at most 2 signals ever sent, so the EINTR path is barely exercised and the “N signals were sent” output shows <=2. The sibling tests (pthread_kill/8-1.c:272-278, pthread_mutex_trylock/4-3.c:364-369) sleep first and then clear the flag.

  • Suggested action: Move the do_it1 = 0 loop after sleep(1), as in pthread_kill/8-1.c. Keep do_it2 = 0 after the senders are joined, or with them. Also make the flags volatile or atomic.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN,MUTATION,REPEAT,VIRT. HPE as-is 4 runs: PASS with ‘3’,‘0’,‘2’,‘0 signals were sent meanwhile’ (~22-25k joins). Mutated to sleep(1) before clearing do_it1 (as pthread_kill/8-1): PASS with 107530 and 133009 signals. VIRT 3/3 PASS. The EINTR claim is effectively untested as shipped.
  • Verification (phase 3, glibc vs musl build and libc sources): UNCHANGED via MUSL,BULK,RUN,SRC. HPE glibc: PASS; musl: UNTESTED ‘File pthread_join/../testfrmw/threads_scenarii.c cannot’. representative rerun of pthread_create/1-5 rc=5. musl PTHREAD_STACK_MIN=2048 (limits.h:67) trips testfrmw/threads_scenarii.c:217-219, already NEW UNDEF by m04; test body never runs. Existing WRONG finding untouched.

testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/interfaces/pthread_rwlock_rdlock/2-1.c (openposix: conformance/interfaces/pthread_rwlock_rdlock/2-1)

  • Category: WRONG (secondary: UNDOC)
  • Confidence: high
  • Claim under test: with SCHED_FIFO threads, a reader does not get the lock while a higher-priority writer is blocked on it (Thread Execution Scheduling option).
  • Problem: (1) set_priority() treats pthread_setschedparam(...) == -1 as failure, but pthread_setschedparam() returns a positive error number (e.g. EPERM when not root), so a failed switch to SCHED_FIFO is silently ignored and the test runs with SCHED_OTHER threads, i.e. not under the condition it claims to test. (2) Since commit 7a7cbb791aa3 the rwlock is created with glibc’s non-portable PTHREAD_RWLOCK_PREFER_WRITER_NONRECURSIVE_NP kind, so the reader blocks because of writer preference whatever the priorities are; the test checks a glibc extension, not POSIX priority behaviour (glibc’s default rwlock does not implement the POSIX TPS rule, sourceware bug 13701). (3) The extension is guarded by #ifdef __GNUC__ (compiler), not __GLIBC__, so it breaks the build on non-glibc libcs such as musl, which lack pthread_rwlockattr_setkind_np.
  • Evidence: 2-1.c:63-73 (== -1 check), 149-152 (setkind_np under GNUC); man pthread_setschedparam(3) RETURN VALUE: “On success, these functions return 0; on error, they return a nonzero error number.”; git show 7a7cbb791aa3.
  • Suggested action: check != 0 and return PTS_UNTESTED/UNRESOLVED when SCHED_FIFO cannot be set; guard with GLIBC; document that the test verifies glibc writer-preference rather than priority ordering (or drop it as glibc is non-conforming).
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN,MUTATION,GIT. VIRT as uid 65534 (RLIMIT_RTPRIO 0; setschedparam/1-1 gets rc=1 EPERM there): Test PASSED with no ‘Can’t set policy’ -> EPERM ignored, runs SCHED_OTHER. VIRT root mutant without setkind_np(PREFER_WRITER_NONRECURSIVE_NP): ‘Test FAILED: rd_thread did not block’ rc=1 -> outcome decided by the glibc kind (git 7a7cbb791aa3, glibc bz13701), not priorities. musl build not tried
  • Verification (phase 3, glibc vs musl build and libc sources): CONFIRMED via MUSL,RUN,BUILD,MUTATION,SRC. HPE glibc: PASS. musl: not built, openposix-build.log:3792,3799 ‘undeclared function pthread_rwlockattr_setkind_np’/‘PTHREAD_RWLOCK_PREFER_WRITER_NONRECURSIVE_NP’ (2-1.c:150 #ifdef GNUC, true for clang). Copy guarded by GLIBC, musl as root: ‘Test FAILED: rd_thread did not block’ (musl tryrdlock.c:8-11 ignores waiting writers)

  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN,READ. diff vs 2-1.c: only reader priority min+1 (equal) and messages; same set_priority() ‘== -1’ check and GNUC-guarded setkind_np. VIRT as uid 65534: Test PASSED rc=0 with no ‘Can’t set policy’ message although pthread_setschedparam returns EPERM for that user; same verdict as 2-1 (writer preference, not priority, makes it pass)
  • Verification (phase 3, glibc vs musl build and libc sources): CONFIRMED via MUSL,RUN,BUILD,MUTATION,SRC. HPE glibc: PASS. musl: not built, openposix-build.log:3804,3811 (setkind_np under #ifdef GNUC). Copy guarded by GLIBC, musl as root: ‘Test FAILED: rd_thread did not block on read lock, when … an equal priority writer is waiting’ -> outcome is the libc rwlock policy, not priorities

testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/interfaces/pthread_rwlock_rdlock/2-3.c (openposix: conformance/interfaces/pthread_rwlock_rdlock/2-3)

  • Category: WRONG (secondary: WEAK)
  • Confidence: high
  • Claim under test: a reader with higher SCHED_FIFO priority than the blocked writer acquires the read lock.
  • Problem: Same broken set_priority() error check (== -1), so without CAP_SYS_NICE the threads stay SCHED_OTHER and the test still runs. The default glibc rwlock prefers readers and lets a new reader in whenever readers hold the lock, regardless of priority, so the test passes whether or not the priority rule is implemented. It cannot detect a violation of the claimed rule.
  • Evidence: 2-3.c:63-73, 153 (default attr), 203-215; man pthread_setschedparam(3) RETURN VALUE.
  • Suggested action: fix the error check (return UNTESTED when SCHED_FIFO cannot be set); accept that on glibc this only verifies reader preference, or drop.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN,MUTATION. VIRT as uid 65534: Test PASSED (SCHED_FIFO silently not set). VIRT root mutant swapping priorities (blocked writer min+1 > reader min, so POSIX TPS says the reader shall NOT get the lock): still ‘Test PASSED’ rc=0, reader acquired -> glibc default reader preference passes regardless of priority; the test cannot detect a violation
  • Verification (phase 3, glibc vs musl build and libc sources): CONFIRMED via MUSL,RUN,MUTATION,SRC. HPE glibc PASS; musl PASS as root and as uid 65534 (no ‘Can’t set policy’ despite EPERM). musl mutant with priorities swapped (blocked writer min+1 > reader min, TPS says reader must block): ‘Test PASSED’ -> musl, like glibc, admits readers whenever not write-locked (src/thread/pthread_rwlock_tryrdlock.c:8-11)

testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/interfaces/pthread_rwlock_unlock/3-1.c (openposix: conformance/interfaces/pthread_rwlock_unlock/3-1)

  • Category: WRONG (secondary: UNDOC)
  • Confidence: high
  • Claim under test: with SCHED_FIFO waiters, the lock is granted in priority order, writers before readers at equal priority.
  • Problem: set_priority() checks pthread_setschedparam(...) == -1, which never happens (it returns an error number), so without CAP_SYS_NICE the threads stay SCHED_OTHER. The test then asserts the POSIX TPS ordering, which only applies to SCHED_FIFO/RR/SPORADIC waiters. In addition, glibc’s default rwlock is reader-preferring and ignores priorities (sourceware bug 13701, the same non-conformance worked around in rdlock/2-1 with setkind_np), so after the write unlock the reader gets the lock before writer1. Built and run locally as non-root on this system (glibc, Linux 7.2): “Test fail: writer did not get write lock, when test_main release the lock”, exit 1, with no “Can’t set policy” message.
  • Evidence: 3-1.c:63-73 (== -1), 195-196, 299-312; man pthread_setschedparam(3) RETURN VALUE: “on error, they return a nonzero error number”; man pthread_rwlockattr_setkind_np(3): default is PTHREAD_RWLOCK_PREFER_READER_NP.
  • Suggested action: fix the error check and return UNTESTED when SCHED_FIFO cannot be set; on glibc either use PTHREAD_RWLOCK_PREFER_WRITER_NONRECURSIVE_NP (as rdlock/2-1 does) or mark it a known glibc non-conformance.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN. HPE as root (SCHED_FIFO set OK): rc=1 ‘reader: acquired read lock / Test fail: writer did not get write lock, when test_main release the lock’; VIRT as uid 65534 (EPERM from setschedparam, no ‘Can’t set policy’ message): same FAIL. Fails on every glibc system because the default rwlock is reader-preferring (bz13701), whatever the priority; the == -1 check additionally hides missing privileges
  • Verification (phase 3, glibc vs musl build and libc sources): CONFIRMED via MUSL,RUN,REPEAT,SRC. HPE glibc root: FAIL ‘writer did not get write lock’. musl root: PASS 1/9, FAIL 8/9 ‘reader: acquired read lock / Test fail’; musl uid 65534: FAIL, no ‘Can’t set policy’. musl unlock wakes all waiters (pthread_rwlock_unlock.c:14-15), readers ignore waiting writers (tryrdlock.c:8-11): no Linux libc does TPS rwlock order

testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/interfaces/pthread_spin_unlock/3-1.c (openposix: conformance/interfaces/pthread_spin_unlock/3-1)

  • Category: WRONG (secondary: UNDEF)
  • Confidence: high
  • Claim under test: pthread_spin_unlock() “may fail” with EPERM when the caller does not hold the lock, and the header says the test “will always PASS”.
  • Problem: Main checks if (rc != 0) { ...; return PTS_FAIL; } right after the unlock, so an implementation that does report EPERM fails the test. The later if (rc == EPERM) branch is unreachable. On glibc the unlock simply stores 0 and returns 0, so the test PASSes without testing anything. POSIX.1-2024 also made the scenario undefined: “The results are undefined if the lock is not held by the calling thread.” EPERM appears only as a RATIONALE recommendation.
  • Evidence: pthread_spin_unlock/3-1.c:97-100 vs :112; https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9799919799/functions/pthread_spin_unlock.html DESCRIPTION.
  • Suggested action: Drop the test (UB per POSIX.1-2024). At minimum, remove the early return PTS_FAIL.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN,MUTATION,READ. HPE: PASS as-is (glibc unlock returns 0, ‘Did not return EPERM’); VIRT: mutant rc = EPERM (an implementation that reports EPERM) -> ‘main: Error at pthread_spin_unlock()’ rc=1 FAIL, so the EPERM PASS branch is unreachable; POSIX 2024 DESCRIPTION ‘results are undefined if the lock is not held’; Issue 7 removed EPERM
  • Verification (phase 3, glibc vs musl build and libc sources): CONFIRMED via MUSL,RUN,SRC. HPE glibc and musl: rc=0 ‘got return code :0 … Did not return EPERM’. musl src/thread/pthread_spin_unlock.c:5-6 ‘a_store(s, 0); return 0;’, glibc nptl/pthread_spin_unlock.c:29-30 likewise -> no Linux libc reports EPERM; the EPERM PASS branch is unreachable anyway (phase-2 mutant)

testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/interfaces/raise/1-2.c (openposix: conformance/interfaces/raise/1-2)

  • Category: WRONG
  • Confidence: high (phase 1: medium)
  • Claim under test: raise() in a forked child delivers the signal to the child, so the child’s handler runs and calls exit(0).
  • Problem: The parent decides with if (!WEXITSTATUS(i)) and never checks WIFEXITED. If the child is killed by a signal (for example the raised SIGABRT taking its default action, or a crash), WEXITSTATUS() of a signal-terminated status is 0. That failure is reported as PASS. The header also says the child “returns 1”, but the handler calls exit(0).
  • Evidence: raise/1-2.c:91.
  • Suggested action: Require WIFEXITED(i) && WEXITSTATUS(i) == 0.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN,MUTATION. HPE: PASS as-is; VIRT: mutant child uses SIG_DFL for SIGABRT so raise() kills the child (core dump, no handler) -> parent prints ‘Child exited normally / Test PASSED’ rc=0, because WEXITSTATUS() of a signal-terminated status is 0 and WIFEXITED is not checked

testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/interfaces/sched_getscheduler/7-1.c (openposix: conformance/interfaces/sched_getscheduler/7-1)

  • Category: WRONG
  • Confidence: high
  • Claim under test: sched_getscheduler(1) fails with EPERM for a non-root caller.
  • Problem: Linux performs no permission check in sched_getscheduler, so the call succeeds and returns pid 1’s policy. The test treats only result == 0 (SCHED_OTHER) as “succeeded -> UNTESTED”. Any other successful return falls into if (errno != EPERM) ... return PTS_FAIL, for example pid 1 running SCHED_BATCH/IDLE/RR in a container, or with SCHED_RESET_ON_FORK or’ed in (kernel line 1011). The test then FAILs a correct kernel with “errno is not EPERM: Success”. An LSM denial (EACCES) also FAILs, although POSIX makes the permission conditions implementation-defined.
  • Evidence: sched_getscheduler/7-1.c:74-80; /usr/src/linux/kernel/sched/syscalls.c:995-1015 (only an LSM hook, no uid check).
  • Suggested action: Treat any result != -1 as UNTESTED/UNSUPPORTED. Better, drop the test, since Linux never returns EPERM here (sched_getparam/6-1.c is the same idea).
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN,CONTAINER,READ. HPE/VIRT host (pid 1 SCHED_OTHER): rc=5 UNTESTED ‘has successed’. VIRT pid namespace with pid 1 non-OTHER: ‘ltprun unshare -pf –mount-proc chrt -b 0 ./7-1’ rc=1 FAIL and ‘chrt -r 1’ -> ‘errno is not EPERM: Success’ rc=1 FAIL -> a correct kernel fails; Linux never returns EPERM (kernel/sched/syscalls.c: LSM hook only)
  • Verification (phase 3, glibc vs musl build and libc sources): UNCHANGED via MUSL,BULK,RUN,SRC. HPE glibc: UNTESTED; musl: FAILED ‘errno is not EPERM: Function not implemented’. representative rerun of sched_getparam/3-1. musl sched/sched_{get,set}{param,scheduler}.c:7 return ENOSYS by design; musl declares no PS option (sysconf.c:41 =-1, no _POSIX_PRIORITY_SCHEDULING). Test right; no PS gate (suite-wide). Existing WRONG finding not reached.

testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/interfaces/sched_setparam/2-1.c (openposix: conformance/interfaces/sched_setparam/2-1)

  • Category: WRONG
  • Confidence: high (phase 1: medium)
  • Claim under test: Higher numeric priority means higher priority under SCHED_FIFO. The father at max priority and a child at min priority each run a counting loop, and the counters are compared.
  • Problem: The busy loops for (i = 0; i < N; i++) count++; use a plain global count. With the suite’s -O2 (open_posix_testsuite/include/mk/config.mk:5), gcc folds each loop into one addl $N, count; compiling this file with gcc -O2 -S shows addl $200000000, count(%rip) and addl $20000000, count(%rip). So no CPU time is ever measured and the ACCEPTABLE_RATIO logic is dead code. On the usual single-CPU (affinity) path, PASS comes only from child_count == 0: the child never ran before SIGTERM. If the child does run, it finishes the folded loop at once, falls out of child_process(), prints “This code should not be executed” and exits. The father’s scanf then hits EOF (returns -1, not 0), and child_count is read uninitialized (line 85 declaration, lines 172-185).
  • Evidence: sched_setparam/2-1.c:66, :158 (loops), :172 (while (scanf(...) == 0)), :185; generated assembly (gcc -O2 -S output, lines 490 and 642).
  • Suggested action: Make count volatile, or replace the counting with a deterministic check. For example, the father spins at max priority on one CPU and the low-priority child writes a shared flag, which must stay unset until the father lowers its priority. Initialize child_count and handle a scanf EOF as UNRESOLVED.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN,MUTATION,BUILD. HPE gcc -O2 -S: ‘addl $200000000, count(%rip)’ / ‘addl $20000000, count(%rip)’ (loops folded). VIRT debug mutant: child_count=0 every run (child never runs before SIGTERM). Mutant with father demoted to min prio (child preempts it): ‘This code should not be executed.’, scanf=-1, child_count=1 (uninitialised) -> Test PASSED 3/3
  • Verification (phase 3, glibc vs musl build and libc sources): UNCHANGED via MUSL,BULK,RUN,SRC. HPE glibc: PASS; musl: UNRESOLVED ‘An error occurs when calling sched_setscheduler(): Func’. representative rerun of sched_getparam/3-1. musl sched/sched_{get,set}{param,scheduler}.c:7 return ENOSYS by design; musl declares no PS option (sysconf.c:41 =-1, no _POSIX_PRIORITY_SCHEDULING). Test right; no PS gate (suite-wide). Existing WRONG finding not reached.

testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/interfaces/sched_setparam/20-1.c

  • Category: WRONG
  • Confidence: high
  • Found in phase 3 verification (not flagged by the phase-1 reading).
  • Verdict: NEW (WRONG, high)
  • Method: MUSL, BULK, RUN, SRC
  • Ran:
bulk: the saved whole-suite open_posix logs of the glibc and musl runs
ssh HPE "LTPRUN_TIMEOUT=60 ltprun-{glibc,musl} /root/ltp-{glibc,musl}/testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/interfaces/sched_setparam/sched_setparam_20-1.run-test"
  • Observed:
glibc: UNSUPPORTED Process contention scope threads are not supported.
musl:  PASS
  • Conclusion: Error path reports PASS: pthread_exit() from the main thread ends the process with status 0. Any sched_getparam() failure turns into PTS_PASS (seen on musl). Fix: return PTS_UNRESOLVED instead of pthread_exit((void )-1) (same line in all six copies). Evidence: HPE glibc: UNSUPPORTED; musl: PASS. Rerun: glibc rc=4, musl rc=0 vacuous PASS. musl sched_getparam() ENOSYS -> test_main error path :37-40 calls pthread_exit((void )-1) on the main thread -> process exit status 0 = PTS_PASS (rerun: rc=0 with “An error occurs …”). glibc passes :37 and skips at setscope ENOTSUP (nptl/pthread_attr_setscope.c:36-37); musl would too (:8-9)
  • Verification (phase 3, glibc vs musl build and libc sources): NEW via MUSL,BULK,RUN,SRC. HPE glibc: UNSUPPORTED; musl: PASS. Rerun: glibc rc=4, musl rc=0 vacuous PASS. musl sched_getparam() ENOSYS -> test_main error path :37-40 calls pthread_exit((void *)-1) on the main thread -> process exit status 0 = PTS_PASS (rerun: rc=0 with “An error occurs …”). glibc passes :37 and skips at setscope ENOTSUP (nptl/pthread_attr_setscope.c:36-37); musl would too (:8-9)

testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/interfaces/sem_init/1-1.c (openposix: conformance/interfaces/sem_init/1-1)

  • Category: WRONG

The test also calls sem_getvalue on the semaphore before checking whether sem_init succeeded. The condition should be sts == -1 -> UNRESOLVED followed by val != 1 -> FAIL.

testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/interfaces/sem_init/3-1.c (openposix: conformance/interfaces/sem_init/3-1)

  • Category: WRONG

HPE: TEST PASS as-is (both sems pshared=0, threads only); mutant with all four sem_wait/sem_post calls in producer/consumer deleted still ‘TEST PASS’ rc=0 on VIRT -> neither pshared nor semaphore behaviour is checked; pthread_exit() in test_main makes rc 0

testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/interfaces/sem_init/6-1.c (openposix: conformance/interfaces/sem_init/6-1)

  • Category: WRONG
  • Confidence: high
  • Claim under test: sem_init fails with EINVAL when value exceeds SEM_VALUE_MAX.
  • Problem: On glibc and musl, SEM_VALUE_MAX is 2147483647 == INT_MAX, so if (SEM_VALUE_MAX >= INT_MAX) is always true on Linux. The test then prints “Test skipped” and returns PTS_PASS, so it never exercises anything and is still reported as a pass. The non-skipped path also reads errno without checking that sem_init returned -1. sem_init takes an unsigned value, so the check can be made with (unsigned)SEM_VALUE_MAX + 1. glibc’s __new_sem_init rejects value > SEM_VALUE_MAX with EINVAL.
  • Evidence: testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/interfaces/sem_init/6-1.c:28-44; /usr/include/bits/local_lim.h:99 “#define SEM_VALUE_MAX (2147483647)”; POSIX sem_init ERRORS: “[EINVAL] The value argument exceeds {SEM_VALUE_MAX}.”
  • Suggested action: Use an unsigned value of SEM_VALUE_MAX + 1u, require a -1 return with EINVAL, and return PTS_UNSUPPORTED (not PASS) when the value cannot be represented.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN,BUILD. HPE+VIRT: prints ‘Test skipped’ rc=0 (PTS_PASS) - SEM_VALUE_MAX==INT_MAX==2147483647 on glibc 2.43; small program on VIRT: sem_init(&s,0,(unsigned)SEM_VALUE_MAX+1u) = -1 EINVAL, so the assertion is testable and the test reports PASS without testing it
  • Verification (phase 3, glibc vs musl build and libc sources): CONFIRMED via MUSL,RUN,SRC. HPE glibc and musl: ‘Test skipped’ rc=0 (PTS_PASS). musl include/limits.h:69 SEM_VALUE_MAX 0x7fffffff == INT_MAX, as glibc local_lim.h:99. musl sem_init.c:7 compares the unsigned value: musl-clang probe sem_init(&s,0,(unsigned)SEM_VALUE_MAX+1u) = -1 errno=22 -> testable on both, never tested

testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/interfaces/sem_open/2-2.c (openposix: conformance/interfaces/sem_open/2-2)

  • Category: WRONG
  • Confidence: high (phase 1: medium)
  • Claim under test: sem_open with O_CREAT|O_EXCL creates a semaphore that does not exist yet.
  • Problem: If sem_open fails, the test reports UNRESOLVED, not FAIL. The only FAIL path is errno == EEXIST checked after a successful sem_open, but errno’s value after success is unspecified (and glibc’s sem_open makes several internal syscalls). So the claimed behavior can never produce FAIL, and the errno check is meaningless.
  • Evidence: testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/interfaces/sem_open/2-2.c:34-49; POSIX errno: “The value of errno should only be examined when it is indicated to be valid by a function’s return value.”
  • Suggested action: FAIL when sem_open returns SEM_FAILED and remove the errno test (or drop it as a duplicate of 1-1).
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN,MUTATION. HPE: TEST PASSED as-is; VIRT: mutant dropping O_CREAT (sem_open does not create the semaphore) -> ‘sem_open: No such file or directory’ rc=2 UNRESOLVED, not FAIL; the only FAIL path tests errno after a successful call -> the claimed behaviour can never yield FAIL
  • Verification (phase 3, glibc vs musl build and libc sources): CONFIRMED via MUSL,RUN,SRC. HPE glibc and musl: ‘TEST PASSED’ rc=0. musl sem_open changes errno on success paths: src/thread/sem_open.c:79 access() leaves ENOENT, and :118-121 hits EEXIST on a /dev/shm/tmp- collision then retries and succeeds -> errno==EEXIST after success is possible, giving a spurious FAIL; check meaningless

testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/interfaces/sem_open/5-1.c (openposix: conformance/interfaces/sem_open/5-1)

  • Category: WRONG
  • Confidence: high
  • Claim under test: sem_open fails with EINVAL when value > SEM_VALUE_MAX.
  • Problem: int counter = SEM_VALUE_MAX; if (counter >= INT_MAX) return PTS_PASS; SEM_VALUE_MAX == INT_MAX on glibc and musl, so the test silently returns PASS without testing anything. sem_open’s value argument is unsigned int, and glibc’s sem_open rejects value > SEM_VALUE_MAX with EINVAL, so the case can be tested.

  • Verification (phase 3, glibc vs musl build and libc sources): CONFIRMED via MUSL,RUN,SRC. testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/interfaces/sem_unlink/4-1.c (openposix: conformance/interfaces/sem_unlink/4-1)

  • Category: WRONG
  • Confidence: high

It passes mainly because glibc maps any invalid name to ENOENT. 4-2.c tests the assertion correctly.

  • Verification (phase 3, glibc vs musl build and libc sources): CONFIRMED via MUSL,RUN,SRC. HPE glibc: TEST PASSED rc 0; musl: ‘TEST FAILED: semaphore does exist’ rc 1. glibc sysdeps/pthread/sem_unlink.c:31-34 maps every bad name to ENOENT; musl src/mman/shm_open.c:13-20 gives EINVAL (embedded ‘/’, empty) or ENAMETOOLONG. Probe: ‘/a/b/c’ glibc ENOENT, musl EINVAL. Uninitialised name passes only by glibc’s mapping

testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/interfaces/sem_unlink/5-1.c (openposix: conformance/interfaces/sem_unlink/5-1)

  • Category: WRONG (phase 1: WEAK)
  • Confidence: high
  • Claim under test: sem_unlink returns -1/ENAMETOOLONG for names longer than PATH_MAX or with a component longer than NAME_MAX.
  • Problem: sem_unlink is called only if sem_open() with the over-long name succeeds. glibc’s sem_open rejects such names (__shm_get_name -> ENAMETOOLONG), so the test always takes the “Creation of the semaphore failed” path and PASSes without calling sem_unlink. The assertion is never exercised. The NAME_MAX case also builds a component of exactly NAME_MAX characters, which is not “greater than NAME_MAX”.
  • Evidence: testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/interfaces/sem_unlink/5-1.c:131-155, 177-186
  • Suggested action: Call sem_unlink() directly on an over-long name (NAME_MAX+1 component) and require -1/ENAMETOOLONG. Note that POSIX may list ENAMETOOLONG only as a “may fail” error, so ENOENT might also need to be accepted.
  • Verification (phase 3, glibc vs musl build and libc sources): REVISED via MUSL,RUN,SRC. HPE glibc: ‘Test passed’ (both sem_open fail ENAMETOOLONG, sem_unlink never called); musl: FAILED ‘did not return ENAMETOOLONG’ rc 1: ‘/’+255 chars is a legal name, musl sem_open succeeds, sem_unlink returns 0. glibc rejects only via ‘sem.’ prefix (posix/shm-directory.c:55-61). glibc sem_unlink(NAME_MAX+1) = ENOENT, musl = ENAMETOOLONG
  • Verification conclusion: The phase-1 note about the “exactly NAME_MAX” component is the decisive bug. “/”+255 chars is a legal name. musl creates it, unlinks it successfully, and the test FAILs. glibc passes only because it prepends “sem.” (posix/shm-directory.c:55-61, buffer sizeof(SHMDIR)+NAME_MAX), so a 255-character name overflows. On glibc the sem_unlink path is never reached; on musl the test is wrong. - Corrected action: call sem_unlink() directly on a name with a NAME_MAX+1 component, without a prior sem_open. Accept -1 with ENAMETOOLONG or ENOENT: ENAMETOOLONG is “may fail” in POSIX.1-2024, and glibc returns ENOENT (sem_unlink.c:31-34).

testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/interfaces/sem_unlink/7-1.c (openposix: conformance/interfaces/sem_unlink/7-1)

  • Category: WRONG

HPE: ‘Test passed’ as-is; VIRT: mutant with the main thread’s sem_post() after sem_unlink removed still ‘Test passed’ rc=0 in 1.0 s (pthread_join returned) -> the thread was never blocked: sem created with value 1 so its sem_wait succeeded immediately; 9-1.c uses value 0

testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/interfaces/sigaction/12-1.c (openposix: conformance/interfaces/sigaction/12-1)

  • Category: WRONG (secondary: WEAK)
  • Confidence: high
  • Claim under test: assertion #12, with SA_ONSTACK and an alternate stack set by sigaltstack(), the SIGABRT handler runs on the alternate stack.
  • Problem: The handler calls sigaltstack(NULL, &ss) and compares only ss_sp/ss_size, which the kernel fills from task state (t->sas_ss_sp/sas_ss_size) no matter which stack the handler is running on; only ss_flags & SS_ONSTACK depends on the current stack pointer. So the check cannot fail even if SA_ONSTACK handling is broken. There is also no check that the handler ran at all: if SIGABRT is not caught, the test still prints PASSED (unless the default action kills it).
  • Evidence: 12-1.c handler (ss_sp/ss_size compare) and unconditional PASS at end of test_main; /usr/src/linux/kernel/signal.c:4464-4468 (do_sigaltstack fills oss->ss_sp/ss_size from task, ss_flags = sas_ss_flags(sp)).
  • Suggested action: In the handler check (oss.ss_flags & SS_ONSTACK) or that the address of a local lies within [alt_ss.ss_sp, +ss_size); set a flag in the handler and FAIL if it was not called.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN,MUTATION. HPE: ‘Caught SIGABRT / Test PASSED’ as-is; VIRT: mutant with act.sa_flags = 0 (no SA_ONSTACK, handler runs on the normal stack) still ‘Caught SIGABRT / Test PASSED’ rc=0 -> the ss_sp/ss_size comparison cannot detect a handler that is not on the alternate stack

testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/interfaces/sigaction/17-1.c (openposix: conformance/interfaces/sigaction/17-1)

  • Category: WRONG (secondary: FRAGILE)
  • Confidence: high
  • Claim under test: assertion #17, with SA_RESTART clear, select() interrupted by a caught SIGABRT fails with EINTR.
  • Problem: The parent judges the child with WEXITSTATUS(s) == PTS_PASS without checking WIFEXITED. If the child is terminated by SIGABRT (handler not installed or not caught, or the signal arrives before the child’s sigaction() because sync is a 1 s select() sleep), the wait status has a zero exit-code byte, WEXITSTATUS() is 0 == PTS_PASS and the test reports PASSED. The opposite side of the same race (signal arrives after sigaction() but before select()) makes the child exit PTS_FAIL on a correct system. If the default action is ignore/stop, a missing handler hangs instead. fork() failure is not checked, so pid == -1 leads to kill(-1, SIGABRT). On Linux select() always returns EINTR after a handler (signal(7): never restarted), so the test cannot tell SA_RESTART set from clear anyway.
  • Evidence: 17-1.c:41 (fork unchecked), 78-84 (1 s sleep, WEXITSTATUS only); signal(7) “File descriptor multiplexing interfaces: … select(2) … never restarted … regardless of the use of SA_RESTART”.
  • Suggested action: Check WIFEXITED(s) && WEXITSTATUS(s) == PTS_PASS; sync with a pipe written by the child after sigaction() (or block the signal and use pselect); handle fork() < 0; consider read() on an empty pipe, which does depend on SA_RESTART.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN,MUTATION,STRESS,READ. HPE: 17-1 (SIGABRT) as-is PASSED rc=0; mutant sa_flags=SA_RESTART -> “Test PASSED” rc=0 (select never restarted on Linux, SA_RESTART not tested); mutant without sigaction() in child: child killed by SIGABRT, WEXITSTATUS=0 -> “Test PASSED” rc=0. Identical to 17-1 modulo signal (diff after s/SIG/MYSIG/: 0 lines).

testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/interfaces/sigaction/22-1.c (openposix: conformance/interfaces/sigaction/22-1)

  • Category: WRONG (secondary: -)
  • Confidence: high (phase 1: medium)
  • Claim under test: with SA_NODEFER, SIGABRT is not blocked while its handler runs, so raising it inside the handler re-enters the handler.
  • Problem: The child installs the handler and raises SIGABRT. On success it exit(0)s from the nested handler; otherwise it returns PTS_FAIL. The parent then checks only ‘if (!WEXITSTATUS(s))’ and never checks WIFEXITED(s). If the child is killed by a signal, the exit-status bits of the wait status are 0, so WEXITSTATUS() is 0 and the test reports PASS. That happens when the handler is not invoked and SIGABRT’s default action (terminate/core) kills the child, or when the child crashes. A real kernel bug therefore turns into a false PASS. A child UNRESOLVED (exit 2) is also reported as FAIL.
  • Evidence: 22-1.c:88-94 (‘if (wait(&s) == -1) … if (!WEXITSTATUS(s)) { PASSED }’). POSIX wait(): WEXITSTATUS is meaningful only ‘If the value of WIFEXITED(stat_val) is non-zero’.
  • Suggested action: change the check to ‘if (WIFEXITED(s) && WEXITSTATUS(s) == 0)’ and map other outcomes to FAIL/UNRESOLVED, in templates/template_22-1.in and all generated 22-*.c files.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN,MUTATION,STRESS,READ. HPE: 22-1 (SIGABRT) as-is PASSED rc=0; mutant with child sigaction() skipped (handler never runs, child killed by SIGABRT) -> “Test PASSED” rc=0: WEXITSTATUS without WIFEXITED gives false PASS. Control on 22-1: sa_flags=0 (no SA_NODEFER) -> Test FAILED rc=1, so only the not-exited path is blind. diff vs 22-1 modulo signal: 0 lines.

  • Confidence: high (phase 1: medium)
  • Claim under test: with SA_NODEFER, SIGTRAP is not blocked while its handler runs (re-entry check).
  • Problem: Same as 22-1.c. The parent checks ‘!WEXITSTATUS(s)’ without WIFEXITED(s), so a child killed by SIGTRAP’s default terminating action (handler never ran) or by a crash is reported as PASS.
  • Evidence: 22-22.c parent branch ‘if (!WEXITSTATUS(s))’ (same lines as 22-1.c:88-94); POSIX wait(): WEXITSTATUS is meaningful only when WIFEXITED is non-zero.
  • Suggested action: require WIFEXITED(s) && WEXITSTATUS(s) == 0 (fix the template and regenerate).
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN,MUTATION,READ. HPE: 22-22 (SIGTRAP) as-is PASSED rc=0; mutant with child sigaction() skipped (handler never runs, child killed by SIGTRAP) -> “Test PASSED” rc=0: WEXITSTATUS without WIFEXITED gives false PASS. Control on 22-1: sa_flags=0 (no SA_NODEFER) -> Test FAILED rc=1, so only the not-exited path is blind. diff vs 22-1 modulo signal: 0 lines.

testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/interfaces/sigpause/2-1.c (openposix: conformance/interfaces/sigpause/2-1)

  • Category: WRONG (secondary: OBSOLETE, FRAGILE)
  • Confidence: high
  • Claim under test: sigpause() restores the original mask (SIGABRT held) before returning, so a later raise(SIGABRT) stays pending.
  • Problem: (1) The FAIL outcome is unreachable. The header says “If it is not, set the variable return_value to 1”, but the thread only sets return_value = 0 on success. If the mask is not restored, return_value keeps its initial 2 and main returns PTS_UNRESOLVED, so a real conformance failure is never reported as FAIL. (2) If sigpause() does not return -1/EINTR, the thread returns early (line 65) without resetting sem. Main then spins forever in while (sem == INTHREAD) sleep(1); and the result is HUNG instead of UNRESOLVED. (3) sleep(1) synchronisation has the same race as 1-1: if the thread has not run sigaction() yet, the process aborts. sem, handler_called and return_value are plain ints shared between threads. sigpause was also removed in POSIX.1-2024.
  • Evidence: sigpause/2-1.c:17 (comment) vs 61-79 (no return_value = 1), 64-65 (no sem = INMAIN), 98-100, 108-113.
  • Suggested action: drop with the sigpause group; if kept, set return_value = 1 in an else branch at line 76, set sem = INMAIN on all exits (or pthread_join), and install the handler before creating the thread.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN,MUTATION,REPEAT,STRESS,VIRT. HPE as-is PASS; 0 failures in 5 plain + 5 stress runs on HPE and 3 plain + 5 stress runs on VIRT (1 CPU). Mutant ‘sigrelse(SIGTOTEST)’ after sigpause (mask NOT restored): handler called twice, exit rc 2 UNRESOLVED, never FAIL. Mutant forcing sigpause result to 0: thread returns without sem=INMAIN, main spins until killed (timeout 20 s, rc 137) = HUNG. Both defects confirmed.

testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/interfaces/sigqueue/7-1.c (openposix: conformance/interfaces/sigqueue/7-1)

  • Category: WRONG
  • Confidence: high
  • Claim under test: when several RT signals are pending, the lowest-numbered one is delivered first.
  • Problem: the handler compares last_signal >= signo but never assigns last_signal, so it stays 0. Since signo >= SIGRTMIN > 0, test_failed can never be set and the test always PASSes, whatever the delivery order. The printed order is never checked.
  • Evidence: sigqueue/7-1.c:29,36-38 (no last_signal = signo;).
  • Suggested action: add last_signal = signo; in the handler after the comparison, and make last_signal volatile sig_atomic_t.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN,MUTATION,GIT. HPE: as-is PASS (34..64). Mutant unblocking with sigrelse() from SIGRTMAX down (delivery order 64,63..34) still rc 0 PASS. Same mutant plus ‘last_signal = signo;’ -> rc 1 ‘Test FAILED: A pending signal was delivered…’; fixed test on in-order kernel PASS. last_signal never assigned since 2003 import (c911fa64e3ec).

testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/interfaces/sigsuspend/1-1.c (openposix: conformance/interfaces/sigsuspend/1-1)

  • Category: WRONG (secondary: FRAGILE)
  • Confidence: high (phase 1: medium)
  • Claim under test: sigsuspend() temporarily replaces the mask (SIGUSR2 stays pending while suspended) and suspends until SIGUSR1 arrives.
  • Problem: (1) After kill(pid, SIGUSR2) the parent checks SIGUSR2_called == 1 and FAILs if so. That variable is the parent’s own copy, which is never written in the parent, so this check is dead code. (2) The real conformance failure (SIGUSR2 not blocked by the temporary mask, so its handler runs before SIGUSR1) makes the child exit(1), and the parent reports exit status 1 as PTS_UNRESOLVED. A broken mask replacement is never reported as FAIL. (3) Synchronisation is a fixed sleep(3). If the child has not installed its handlers in time, SIGUSR2 kills it and the test reports FAIL (“Did not exit normally”).
  • Evidence: sigsuspend/1-1.c:44-62 (handler exit codes), 113-122 (dead parent check), 141-145 (exit 1 -> UNRESOLVED).
  • Suggested action: drop the dead parent check, map child exit 1 to PTS_FAIL, and synchronise with a pipe (child writes just before sigsuspend; the signals stay pending anyway because the mask already blocks them).
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN,MUTATION,READ. HPE as-is PASS. Mutation removing SIGUSR2 from the sigsuspend temp mask (the exact conformance bug) -> child exit 1 -> ‘Test UNRESOLVED’ rc=2, never FAIL. Mutation sleep(4) before child sigaction (slow child) -> ‘Test FAILED: Did not exit normally’ rc=1. Parent check of SIGUSR2_called reads its own never-written copy (dead).

testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/interfaces/timer_settime/3-3.c (runtest: openposix: conformance/interfaces/timer_settime/3-3)

  • Category: WRONG
  • Confidence: high (phase 1: medium)
  • Claim under test: setting it_value = 0 disarms “a currently armed and blocked timer”.
  • Problem: The timer is a one-shot 10ms timer (it_interval 0) and the test sleeps 1s before disarming, so the timer has already expired and is no longer armed; only its signal is pending. The handler is installed and the pending signal is (or is not) delivered during sigprocmask(SIG_UNBLOCK) before the final nanosleep starts, so nanosleep is never interrupted either way. The test passes whether or not timer_settime() with zero it_value disarms anything.
  • Evidence: 3-3.c:67-79 (10ms one-shot, sleep 1s), 98-107 (disarm), 110-126 (unblock then nanosleep).
  • Suggested action: use a periodic timer (e.g. it_value 10ms, it_interval 100ms) so it is still armed when disarmed, then verify no further signal arrives after the pending one is consumed (sigtimedwait), or drop as covered by 3-2.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN,MUTATION,READ. HPE as-is PASS. Mutation deleting the disarming timer_settime(it_value=0) call still PASS (‘OK to be in once’ printed at unblock, then nanosleep not interrupted). The 10 ms one-shot timer has expired before the disarm; kernel timer_settime only bumps it_signal_seq so the stale signal is dropped. The check is vacuous.

testcases/open_posix_testsuite/functional/mqueues/send_rev_1.c (openposix: functional/mqueues/send_rev_1)

  • Category: WRONG (secondary: WEAK)
  • Confidence: high
  • Claim under test: two processes can read/write the same message queue at the same time.
  • Problem: The child sets ret_code=PTS_UNRESOLVED on mq_receive failure and exit()s with it, but the parent does (void)wait(NULL) and returns its own ret_code, so a receive failure in the child is never reported. The received payloads are only printed, never compared with what was sent.
  • Evidence: send_rev_1.c child branch exit(ret_code); parent (void)wait(NULL); ... return ret_code;
  • Suggested action: wait(&status) and fold the child status in; strcmp received vs sent messages.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN,MUTATION. HPE as-is PASS. Mutant with child mq_receive buffer size 1 (EMSGSIZE): child prints ‘mq_receive doesn’t return success’ and exits PTS_UNRESOLVED, parent still rc=0 PASS (wait(NULL) discards the status). Received payloads are only printed, never compared with what was sent.
