Not libc: musl build uses clang -O2, which deletes stress_child’s malloc+memset loop (objdump: 4019a0 jmp 4019a0; child RSS 476 kB), so no memcg pressure. clang -O2 + glibc headers gives the same ‘jmp’ loop. Same reproducer at -O0: drops under both libcs

testcases/kernel/syscalls/mount_setattr/mount_setattr01.c (runtest: syscalls/mount_setattr01)

  • Category: FRAGILE
  • Confidence: low (phase 1: medium)
  • Claim under test: open_tree() + mount_setattr() and open_tree_attr() apply mount attributes.
  • Problem: The open_tree_attr() variant is always built because the LTP syscall tables define __NR_open_tree_attr. When libc provides open_tree_attr() (configure checks HAVE_OPEN_TREE_ATTR; glibc >= 2.42), LTP’s tst_syscall wrapper is not used, so ENOSYS on a kernel older than 6.15 is not turned into TCONF. TST_EXP_FD then reports TFAIL for every tcase. There is no min_kver or ENOSYS check for that variant, although the description itself says open_tree_attr was added in v6.15.
  • Evidence: mount_setattr01.c:59-61, 112-119; include/lapi/fsmount.h:108-114 (fallback only #ifndef HAVE_OPEN_TREE_ATTR); configure.ac:141.
  • Suggested action: in setup, probe open_tree_attr for the variant and TCONF on ENOSYS (or always call through tst_syscall).
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): REVISED via RUN,MUTATION,VIRT. Fedora 44 glibc 2.43 has no open_tree_attr (nm libc; config.h HAVE_OPEN_TREE_ATTR undef), so phase-1 ‘glibc >= 2.42’ is wrong. Under seccomp ENOSYS for open_tree_attr: shipped build -> ‘TCONF: syscall(467) not supported’ (OK). Mutant emulating a libc wrapper (HAVE_OPEN_TREE_ATTR + syscall()) -> 6x ‘TFAIL open_tree_attr(…) failed: ENOSYS’. Latent until libc ships it.
  • Verification conclusion: The mechanism is real. Once libc provides open_tree_attr(), a pre-6.15 kernel turns into 6 TFAILs instead of TCONF. But phase 1’s “glibc >= 2.42” is wrong: even glibc 2.43 (Fedora 44) does not export it, so no shipping configuration hits this today. Lowered to low, latent. Action unchanged: probe open_tree_attr in setup and TCONF on ENOSYS, or always call it through tst_syscall.
  • Verification (phase 3, glibc vs musl build and libc sources): CONFIRMED via MUSL,RUN,SRC,BUILD. HPE glibc and musl: all TPASS. HAVE_OPEN_TREE_ATTR undef in both builds (config.h:354): glibc-2.43 source has only __NR_open_tree_attr in arch-syscall.h, no wrapper/abilist; musl-1.2.5 has nothing. Latent until a libc ships the wrapper; low stays

testcases/kernel/syscalls/mremap/mremap06.c (runtest: syscalls/mremap06)

  • Problem: setup() calls fallocate() only to size the file. A failure is TCONF only on NFS and TBROK on any other filesystem without fallocate support (e.g. ext4 without extents, vfat, some FUSE). That gives a false TBROK when TMPDIR lives on such a filesystem. Nothing in the reproducer needs preallocated blocks.

testcases/kernel/syscalls/msync/msync03.c (runtest: syscalls/msync03)

  • Category: FRAGILE (secondary: DOCS)
  • Confidence: high (phase 1: medium)
  • Claim under test: msync() fails with EINVAL when “addr3 is outside the address space of the process”.
  • Problem: addr3 is set to the RLIMIT_DATA hard limit. EINVAL comes only from the alignment check, and only because rlim_max is normally RLIM_INFINITY (all ones, not page aligned). That makes the subcase a duplicate of the addr2 (addr1+1) case. If the hard RLIMIT_DATA is finite and page aligned (e.g. ulimit -Hd 1048576), start is aligned and unmapped, the kernel returns ENOMEM, and the test fails on a correct kernel. msync(2) has no “outside address space -> EINVAL” condition.
  • Evidence: msync03.c (setup: addr3 = (char *)rl.rlim_max;, test_cases {&addr3, MS_SYNC, EINVAL}); mm/msync.c:45-46 (EINVAL only for offset_in_page), mm/msync.c:49-53 and the vma walk (ENOMEM for unmapped).
  • Suggested action: drop the addr3 subcase (addr2 already covers misalignment), or replace it with a high unaligned address constant and fix the comment.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN,VIRT. VIRT as-is: 6 TPASS (addr3 case EINVAL only via unaligned RLIM_INFINITY). With ‘ulimit -d 1048576’ (finite, page-aligned hard limit 1 GiB): ‘msync03 5 TFAIL: msync failed unexpectedly; expected: 22 - Invalid argument: TEST_ERRNO=ENOMEM(12)’ on a correct kernel. msync(2) has no ‘outside address space -> EINVAL’.

testcases/kernel/syscalls/munlockall/munlockall01.c (runtest: syscalls/munlockall01)

  • Category: FRAGILE
  • Confidence: low
  • Claim under test: munlockall() unlocks all memory locked by mlockall().

As an unprivileged user, mlockall(MCL_CURRENT) fails with ENOMEM whenever the process’s total_vm exceeds RLIMIT_MEMLOCK, and the test reports TBROK. The kernel default RLIMIT_MEMLOCK was 64 KiB before 5.16 (and still is on some distros/containers), which is far below the size of any LTP test process. Root runs are unaffected.

  • Suggested action: add .needs_root = 1, or report TCONF on ENOMEM/EPERM, or set .ulimit = {RLIMIT_MEMLOCK, RLIM_INFINITY} when privileged.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN,VIRT. VIRT as root: 2 TPASS. As nobody (setpriv, TMPDIR=/tmp) with ‘ulimit -l 64’: ‘munlockall01.c:25: TBROK: Could not lock memory using mlockall(): ENOMEM (12)’. As nobody with Fedora’s default 8192 KiB: 2 TPASS. Only bites unprivileged runs with a small RLIMIT_MEMLOCK (old 64 KiB default), so keep low.

testcases/kernel/syscalls/name_to_handle_at/name_to_handle_at01.c (runtest: syscalls/name_to_handle_at01)

  • Category: FRAGILE (secondary: WEAK)
  • Confidence: high (phase 1: medium)
  • Claim under test: name_to_handle_at() + open_by_handle_at() round trip for many dfd/flag combinations, and EOVERFLOW for a zero-sized handle.
  • Problem: (1) The test assumes the TMPDIR filesystem can encode decodable handles. On a filesystem without export ops, or with encode-only ops (e.g. overlayfs mounted without nfs_export=on, the usual container /tmp), name_to_handle_at() returns EOPNOTSUPP. allocate_file_handle() then reports TFAIL (“should fail with EOVERFLOW”) and returns NULL, and every subcase TFAILs with EFAULT. EOPNOTSUPP is a documented outcome (“The filesystem does not support decoding of a pathname to a file handle”) and should be TCONF. (2) The opened file is checked only with st_size == 0. Both TEST_FILE and foo_file are empty, so open_by_handle_at() returning the wrong inode would still pass.
  • Evidence: name_to_handle_at01.c:74, 96-102; include/lapi/name_to_handle_at.h allocate_file_handle(); fs/fhandle.c:32-33 (EOPNOTSUPP when !exportfs_can_encode_fh); include/linux/exportfs.h:366 (requires fh_to_dentry); fs/overlayfs/super.c:1506-1509 and fs/overlayfs/export.c:866-868 (fid ops have only encode_fh); name_to_handle_at(2) ERRORS EOPNOTSUPP.
  • Suggested action: in setup, probe with name_to_handle_at() and TCONF on EOPNOTSUPP (or use .needs_device/.all_filesystems with a known-good fs). fstat the target in setup and compare st_dev/st_ino with the fstat of the reopened fd.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN,VIRT. VIRT as-is (btrfs): 27 TPASS. TMPDIR on a plain overlayfs mount (default opts, no nfs_export, as in containers): ‘name_to_handle_at.h:47: TFAIL: name_to_handle_at() should fail with EOVERFLOW: EOPNOTSUPP (95)’ + 27x ‘TFAIL name_to_handle_at() failed (N): EOPNOTSUPP’ = 28 TFAIL on a correct kernel.

testcases/kernel/syscalls/nanosleep/nanosleep02.c (runtest: syscalls/nanosleep02)

  • Category: FRAGILE
  • Confidence: medium (phase 1: high)
  • Claim under test: nanosleep() interrupted by a signal handler returns -1/EINTR and writes a correct remaining time.
  • Problem: The parent synchronises with sleep(1) and then sends SIGINT. If the child has not yet entered nanosleep() after 1 s (loaded or slow system), the handler runs first and nanosleep() then sleeps the full 5 s and returns 0, giving TFAIL “nanosleep was not interrupted”. The child also records tst_timer_start before the syscall, so the expected remaining time includes any scheduling delay (mitigated by the 250 ms margin).
  • Evidence: nanosleep02.c:85-87 (sleep(1); SAFE_KILL(cpid, SIGINT);); nanosleep02.c:38 (5 s request).
  • Suggested action: replace sleep(1) with TST_PROCESS_STATE_WAIT(cpid, ‘S’, 0) (as msgrcv05 does), optionally followed by a short fixed delay so the remaining-time check still measures something.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): REVISED via RUN,REPEAT,STRESS,VIRT,MUTATION. Not reproduced: HPE ltprepeat 5 pass=5, ltprepeat 5 stress pass=5; VIRT (1 CPU) 3/3 plain + 3/3 stress pass. Mechanism shown by mutant delaying the child 1.1 s before nanosleep(): ‘TFAIL: nanosleep was not interrupted, returned 0, expected -1’. Real window (child not in nanosleep within 1 s of fork) is narrow; lowered to medium.
  • Verification conclusion: The sleep(1) handshake fails exactly as described when the child enters nanosleep() more than 1 s after fork. That did not happen in 16 runs, even with stress-ng on a 1-CPU guest. The race is real but narrow, so confidence is lowered to medium. Fix unchanged: TST_PROCESS_STATE_WAIT(cpid, ‘S’, 0) before kill().

testcases/kernel/syscalls/open_by_handle_at/open_by_handle_at02.c (runtest: syscalls/open_by_handle_at02)

  • Category: FRAGILE
  • Confidence: high (phase 1: medium)
  • Claim under test: “stale-dfd”: open_by_handle_at(0, valid_handle, O_RDWR) fails with ESTALE.
  • Problem: fd 0 is whatever stdin the harness gives the test. If stdin is closed, get_path_anchor() returns EBADF -> TFAIL. If stdin is a file on the same filesystem as the tmpdir, the handle decodes and the call succeeds -> TFAIL. ESTALE only results when stdin happens to be on a different fs (pipefs/devpts have no export ops -> ESTALE). The kernel behavior is correct in all cases; the expectation depends on the environment.
  • Evidence: open_by_handle_at02.c:34 ({“stale-dfd”, 0, &valid_fhp, O_RDWR, 0, ESTALE}); /usr/src/linux/fs/fhandle.c:169-196 (get_path_anchor uses the fd’s mount), 265-284 (decode failure -> -ESTALE).
  • Suggested action: use an fd opened on a known different filesystem (e.g. open(“/proc”, O_RDONLY) or a pipe) as the mount fd instead of fd 0.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN,VIRT. HPE as-is 7 TPASS (stdin from ssh). VIRT: ‘sh -c “exec open_by_handle_at02 <&-”’ -> ‘TFAIL: stale-dfd: … should fail with ESTALE: EBADF’; stdin = file in /var/tmp/ltp (same btrfs as tmpdir) -> ‘TFAIL: stale-dfd: open_by_handle_at() passed unexpectedly’; stdin=/proc/version -> TPASS ESTALE

testcases/kernel/syscalls/openat/openat02.c (runtest: syscalls/openat02)

  • Category: FRAGILE
  • Confidence: high
  • Claim under test: openat() with O_APPEND opens the file in append mode (plus CLOEXEC/LARGEFILE/NOATIME/NOFOLLOW/TRUNC subtests).
  • Problem: testfunc_append writes 7 bytes and PASSes only if the resulting offset is > 7, i.e. it relies on TEST_FILE being non-empty beforehand. testfunc_trunc (last tcase) truncates TEST_FILE to 0, and setup() does not run again between iterations, so with -i 2 (or more) the second append run writes into an empty file, gets offset 7 and reports TFAIL on a correct kernel. The check also cannot distinguish O_APPEND from a plain write to an empty file.
  • Evidence: openat02.c:78-93 (offset > sizeof(STR)-1), 218-236 (O_TRUNC subtest), 246-250 (setup writes “test file” once).
  • Suggested action: fstat before the write and require offset == old_size + 7 (and write data at offset 0 first via a separate fd so append is observable), or recreate TEST_FILE content at the start of testfunc_append.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN,REPEAT,VIRT. HPE+VIRT: openat02 as-is all TPASS (all fs); VIRT: ‘ltprun openat02 -i 2’ -> 2nd iteration on ext2 ‘openat02.c:94: TFAIL: test O_APPEND for openat failed’ (file truncated to 0 by the O_TRUNC subtest of iteration 1); correct kernel

testcases/kernel/syscalls/perf_event_open/perf_event_open03.c (runtest: syscalls/perf_event_open03, cve/cve-2020-25704)

  • Category: FRAGILE
  • Confidence: low (phase 1: medium)
  • Claim under test: CVE-2020-25704: PERF_EVENT_IOC_SET_FILTER does not leak memory (fix 7bdb157cdebb).
  • Problem: The leak is inferred from the system-wide /proc/meminfo SUnreclaim value: TFAIL if it grows by > 100 MiB total over the run or by > 20 MiB in more than 5 of the 10 sample windows. Any unrelated unreclaimable slab growth on the machine during the ~5 min run (other workloads, dentry/inode growth in non-reclaimable caches, network buffers) produces TFAIL on a fixed kernel; the test itself prints that SUnreclaim “can also grow due to unrelated reasons”. Thresholds are close to the expected leak size (~100 MB), so it is noisy in both directions.
  • Evidence: perf_event_open03.c:86-122.
  • Suggested action: measure per-cache growth (e.g. kmalloc-* in /proc/slabinfo for the leaked object size) or compare against a control loop without the ioctl, or downgrade to TWARN with kmemleak suggestion.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): REVISED via RUN,READ,VIRT. Cannot run: ‘TCONF: intel_pt is not available’ on VIRT (as-is and under ltpstress); HPE (Haswell) has no intel_pt PMU either. Noise baseline: SUnreclaim on busy HPE (other verifiers running) sampled 10x30 s: max window +6.1 MB, net +2.4 MB in 5 min; VIRT ~0 -> far below the 20 MB/100 MB thresholds; false FAIL plausible only under unusual slab churn
  • Verification conclusion: The test could not be run (it needs intel_pt, which neither host has). The heuristic is as described: system-wide SUnreclaim with 20 MB/100 MB thresholds. On a busy machine, background unreclaimable-slab churn was about 100x below those thresholds, so a false FAIL needs unusual slab growth during the run. Kept as FRAGILE, confidence lowered to low. The suggested per-cache measurement or kmemleak is still the better design.

testcases/kernel/syscalls/ptrace/ptrace11.c (runtest: syscalls/ptrace11)

  • Category: FRAGILE
  • Confidence: medium (phase 1: low)
  • Claim under test: root can PTRACE_ATTACH to init (PID 1) since 2.6.26.
  • Problem: the result depends on environment policy that the test does not detect. Yama kernel.yama.ptrace_scope=3 (no attach at all), SELinux/AppArmor policy forbidding ptrace of the init domain, or a container without CAP_SYS_PTRACE all give EPERM on a correct kernel, which is reported as TFAIL. In those cases the following SAFE_WAITPID(1) also hits TBROK (ECHILD). The test also briefly SIGSTOPs the real system init.
  • Evidence: ptrace11.c:23-36; ptrace(2) EPERM: “the process may not be traced … Yama”; Documentation/admin-guide/LSM/Yama.rst (ptrace_scope 3)
  • Suggested action: TCONF when /proc/sys/kernel/yama/ptrace_scope is 3. Treat EPERM with CAP_SYS_PTRACE missing as TCONF. Optionally use a PID namespace so that “init” is a test-owned process.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN,VIRT. HPE+VIRT as-is TPASS (yama ptrace_scope=0, SELinux enforcing did not block). VIRT: ‘capsh –drop=cap_sys_ptrace – -c ptrace11’ -> ‘TFAIL: ptrace() returns -1, failed unexpectedly: EPERM’ + ‘TBROK: waitpid(1,(nil),0) failed: ECHILD’. Yama scope 3 not tried (irreversible until reboot)

testcases/kernel/syscalls/readahead/readahead02.c (runtest: syscalls/readahead02)

  • Category: FRAGILE
  • Confidence: high (phase 1: medium)
  • Claim under test: readahead()/POSIX_FADV_WILLNEED, on a plain file and on overlayfs, fills the page cache so that the next mmap read does less I/O.
  • Problem: The verdict depends on memory pressure and on how fast the device is: it needs /proc/self/io read_bytes to drop (read_bytes_ra < read_bytes) and cached_ra > testfile_size/2, waiting on readahead with usleep(5ms) polling of mincore() and a retry count derived from an assumed 5MB/s device. readahead is advisory: readahead(2) says it “initiates readahead”. The kernel may cap it at the bdi read_ahead_kb limit or drop pages under memory pressure. “using less cache than expected” is reported as TWARN, which counts as a failure. The git log has a run of timing/cache fixes (613cba44e65e, 5aa4a4f3f05c, 76ec564da212, 6563b849943f).
  • Evidence: readahead02.c:220-240 (usleep polling loop), :343-372 (pass/fail on I/O and cache amounts); mm/readahead.c ksys_readahead -> vfs_fadvise(WILLNEED) is best-effort.
  • Suggested action: Keep the hard assertion to “readahead returns 0 and file offset unchanged”. Make the I/O/cache checks TINFO/TCONF unless the margin is large, or retry a few times before failing. Do not emit TWARN for “less cache than expected”.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN,REPEAT,STRESS,VIRT. No failure in normal runs: HPE ltprepeat 5 pass=5, 5 stress pass=5; VIRT 3 pass=3, 3 stress pass=3. Under memory pressure (VIRT ‘systemd-run –scope -p MemoryMax=40M readahead02’): 3x ‘TFAIL: readahead failed to save any I/O’ (read 0.9-1.8 GB for a 64 MB file) while the cache check correctly says TCONF ‘Page cache … too small’ -> I/O check lacks the same guard

testcases/kernel/syscalls/rt_sigprocmask/rt_sigprocmask01.c (runtest: syscalls/rt_sigprocmask01)

  • Category: FRAGILE (phase 1: WRONG)
  • Confidence: high (phase 1: medium)
  • Claim under test: SIG_BLOCK keeps TEST_SIG pending (handler not run), SIG_UNBLOCK delivers it.
  • Problem: sig_count is a file-scope counter that is never reset. With -i 2 (or more), the second iteration blocks the signal, sends it, and then finds sig_count != 0 left over from the first iteration, so it reports “rt_sigprocmask() failed to change the process’s signal mask” via tst_brkm(TFAIL). The test only works for a single iteration. Separately, TST_TOTAL = 8 and the inner testno loop are meaningless: the loop always breaks after the first pass. The test duplicates sigprocmask01 coverage.
  • Evidence: rt_sigprocmask01.c:54 (static counter), :120-123 (checked before reset), :148-152 (break after first pass); no sig_count = 0 anywhere.
  • Suggested action: reset sig_count = 0 at the start of each iteration (or convert to the new API with .test_all), drop the fake TST_TOTAL loop.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): REVISED via RUN,REPEAT,VIRT. VIRT as-is TPASS; ‘ltprun rt_sigprocmask01 -i 2’ -> iteration 2: ‘TFAIL: rt_sigprocmask01.c:121: rt_sigprocmask() failed to change the process’s signal mask: errno=SUCCESS(0)’, rc=1: sig_count left over from iteration 1. Mechanism confirmed; it is a false FAIL with -i>1 (FRAGILE, like openat02), not a vacuous check
  • Verification conclusion: The mechanism is confirmed: sig_count is never reset, so iteration 2 fails on a correct kernel. A single iteration does verify block/unblock correctly, so this is a false FAIL under -i, i.e. FRAGILE (as with openat02), not a broken check. Action unchanged: reset sig_count per iteration and drop the fake TST_TOTAL loop (or convert to the new API).
  • Verification (phase 3, glibc vs musl build and libc sources): NEW (second finding, secondary category UNDEF/high; primary kept) via MUSL,BULK,RUN,SRC. Secondary to FRAGILE/high (unaffected). HPE glibc: PASS; musl: ‘timeout: the monitored command dumped core (rc 139, no TPASS)’ 2/2. lapi/rt_sigaction.h:65-83 sig_initial() takes restore_rt from oact.sa_restorer of libc sigaction(); glibc copies it back (x86_64/libc_sigaction.c:29), musl does not (src/signal/sigaction.c:56-58): probe shows 0xa5a5.. garbage -> handler return jumps there
  • Verification conclusion: New finding in include/lapi/rt_sigaction.h (shared by rt_sigaction01/02/03, rt_sigprocmask01, rt_sigsuspend01 via safe_rt_signal.h): on x86_64 the SA_RESTORER address is scraped from libc’s struct sigaction, which only glibc fills in. Under musl it is uninitialised stack, so every test that actually delivers a signal crashes (02/03 only test error paths and pass). Action: provide LTP’s own rt_sigreturn trampoline on x86_64 (as already done for arc/sparc) instead of relying on glibc filling oact.sa_restorer.

testcases/kernel/syscalls/semget/semget02.c (runtest: syscalls/semget02)

  • Category: FRAGILE
  • Confidence: high (phase 1: low)
  • Claim under test: semget() fails with EINVAL when nsems > SEMMSL.
  • Problem: Uses the compile-time constant SEMMSL (32000, include/lapi/sem.h:28) rather than the runtime limit from /proc/sys/kernel/sem. kernel.sem SEMMSL is an admin tunable with no upper bound in proc_ipc_sem_dointvec(), so on a system tuned above 32000 semget(.., 32001, IPC_CREAT|IPC_EXCL) can succeed or fail with ENOSPC (SEMMNS), giving a false TFAIL.
  • Evidence: semget02.c:47; /usr/src/linux/ipc/ipc_sysctl.c:51-70 (no SEMMSL bound); semget(2): “EINVAL nsems is less than 0 or greater than the limit on the number of semaphores per semaphore set (SEMMSL)”.
  • Suggested action: read SEMMSL from /proc/sys/kernel/sem in setup (as semget05 does for SEMMNI).
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN,VIRT. VIRT as-is 6 TPASS with kernel.sem SEMMSL=32000. With ‘sysctl kernel.sem=“64000 1024000000 500 32000”’ (restored afterwards): ‘semget02.c:53: TFAIL: semget(…, 32001, 1536) succeeded’ -> compile-time SEMMSL gives a false FAIL on a tuned correct system

testcases/kernel/syscalls/shmget/shmget02.c (runtest: syscalls/shmget02)

  • Category: FRAGILE
  • Confidence: medium (phase 1: low)
  • Claim under test: shmget(SHM_HUGETLB) by a privileged caller fails with ENOMEM when no hugepages are available.
  • Problem: The test sets nr_hugepages=0 via .hugepages = {TST_NO_HUGEPAGES} (lib/tst_hugepage.c only writes nr_hugepages), but does not touch /proc/sys/vm/nr_overcommit_hugepages. If an admin has configured surplus hugepages, hugetlb_reserve_pages() can succeed and shmget() succeeds, producing TFAIL on a correct kernel.
  • Evidence: shmget02.c:59,144; fs/hugetlbfs/inode.c:1537-1540 (ENOMEM only when hugetlb_reserve_pages() fails); lib/tst_hugepage.c:44-47.
  • Suggested action: also save/restore nr_overcommit_hugepages to 0 (or TCONF if non-zero).
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN. HPE: shmget02 8/8 TPASS as-is; with vm.nr_overcommit_hugepages=4 (restored to 0 after) the SHM_HUGETLB ENOMEM case gives ‘TFAIL: shmget(…,2048,2560) succeeded’ -> surplus hugepages not neutralised by TST_NO_HUGEPAGES

testcases/kernel/syscalls/sockioctl/sockioctl01.c (runtest: syscalls/sockioctl01)

  • Category: FRAGILE
  • Confidence: medium (phase 1: low)
  • Claim under test: SIOCGIFFLAGS succeeds on a valid interface (among several ioctl() error cases).
  • Problem: setup3() does SIOCGIFCONF and blindly copies the first ifreq from the buffer without checking ifc.ifc_len > 0. SIOCGIFCONF lists only interfaces with an IPv4 address. In a network namespace or container where no interface (not even lo) has an IPv4 address, the copied ifreq is all zeros, so SIOCGIFFLAGS fails with ENODEV and the “SIOCGIFFLAGS” case reports TFAIL on a correct kernel.
  • Evidence: sockioctl01.c:103-106,222-227; net/core/dev_ioctl.c (SIOCGIFCONF enumerates only devices with protocol addresses).
  • Suggested action: TCONF (or fall back to “lo”) when ifc.ifc_len == 0.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN. HPE: as-is 8/8 TPASS. ‘unshare -n sockioctl01’ (new netns, lo down, no IPv4 address): ‘TFAIL sockioctl01.c:136: SIOCGIFFLAGS ; returned -1 (expected 0), errno 19’ (ENODEV, zeroed ifreq). Same netns after ‘ip link set lo up’: 8/8 TPASS

testcases/kernel/syscalls/statmount/statmount02.c (runtest: syscalls/statmount02)

  • Category: FRAGILE
  • Confidence: medium
  • Claim under test: statmount(STATMOUNT_SB_BASIC) reports dev, magic and sb_flags of a read-only mount, on all filesystems.
  • Problem: The test requires sb_flags == MS_RDONLY exactly. The kernel reports s_flags & (SB_RDONLY|SB_SYNCHRONOUS|SB_DIRSYNC|SB_LAZYTIME), and f2fs turns on lazytime by default (set_opt(sbi, LAZYTIME) -> sb->s_flags |= SB_LAZYTIME). With .all_filesystems, the f2fs run should see MS_RDONLY|MS_LAZYTIME and fail on a correct kernel. Any fs that defaults to lazytime/sync/dirsync has the same problem.
  • Evidence: statmount02.c:45; fs/namespace.c:5472; fs/f2fs/super.c:2627 and 5201-5202
  • Suggested action: Check sb_flags & MS_RDONLY, mask out SB_LAZYTIME, or compare against the flags reported by statfs()/mountinfo.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): REVISED via RUN. HPE: default all_filesystems run TPASS on ext2/3/4,xfs,vfat,exfat,ntfs,ntfs3,tmpfs (sb_flags==1); f2fs is NOT in lib/tst_supported_fs_types.c whitelist so never runs by default. LTP_SINGLE_FS_TYPE=f2fs statmount02: ‘TFAIL: st_mount->sb_flags (33554433) != MS_RDONLY (1)’ (RDONLY|LAZYTIME) on a correct kernel
  • Verification conclusion: The mechanism is real: on f2fs the exact sb_flags == MS_RDONLY comparison fails on a correct kernel. But f2fs is not in LTP’s all_filesystems whitelist (lib/tst_supported_fs_types.c), so a default run never hits it. It fails only when f2fs is selected with LTP_SINGLE_FS_TYPE/LTP_FORCE_SINGLE_FS_TYPE, or once f2fs (or another lazytime-by-default fs) is whitelisted. Corrected finding: “fails on f2fs (MS_RDONLY|MS_LAZYTIME) when f2fs is tested”. The action is the same: check sb_flags & MS_RDONLY or mask SB_LAZYTIME.

testcases/kernel/syscalls/statx/statx08.c (runtest: syscalls/statx08)

  • Category: FRAGILE (secondary: UNDOC)
  • Confidence: high (phase 1: medium)
  • Claim under test: Attribute bits set with FS_IOC_SETFLAGS are reported in stx_attributes, on all filesystems.
  • Problem: setup() treats every bit in stx_attributes_mask as settable through FS_IOC_SETFLAGS and calls tst_brk(TBROK) if SETFLAGS fails. statx(2) only says the mask lists attributes the filesystem supports reporting. Kernel ntfs3 (an all_filesystems target since LTP split ntfs3 out) advertises STATX_ATTR_COMPRESSED, but ntfs_fileattr_set() returns -EOPNOTSUPP for any flag other than IMMUTABLE/APPEND/NODUMP, so the test should TBROK on ntfs3. Separately, ntfs3 sets STATX_ATTR_NODUMP without adding it to the mask (a kernel inconsistency that makes the test skip the NODUMP check).
  • Evidence: statx08.c:104-115, 132-147; fs/ntfs3/file.c:147-148 and 293-294; lib/tst_supported_fs_types.c:23-35 (ntfs3 in whitelist)
  • Suggested action: Set each flag separately and TCONF the flags that SETFLAGS rejects with EOPNOTSUPP/EINVAL, or skip ntfs3 (adding “ntfs” to skip_filesystems now covers ntfs3 as well).
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN. HPE (ntfs3 module present): statx08 TPASS on ext2/3/4,xfs,btrfs; TCONF on vfat,exfat,ntfs(fuse); on ntfs3: ‘TCONF: filesystem doesn’t support FS_NODUMP_FL’ then ‘TBROK: ioctl(4, FS_IOC_SETFLAGS, 52): EOPNOTSUPP (95)’, rc=2, tmpfs never reached

testcases/kernel/syscalls/sync_file_range/sync_file_range01.c (runtest: syscalls/sync_file_range01)

  • Category: FRAGILE
  • Confidence: high
  • Claim under test: sync_file_range() error conditions EBADF/ESPIPE/EINVAL.
  • Problem: The test calls tst_syscall(__NR_sync_file_range, fd, off_t, off_t, flags) directly instead of the arch-aware sync_file_range() wrapper in include/lapi/sync_file_range.h (which sync_file_range02 uses). powerpc/powerpc64 and arm32 only have sync_file_range2 (LTP’s powerpc.in, powerpc64.in and arm.in define only sync_file_range2), so the test TCONFs there even though setup’s check_sync_file_range() found the call working. On 32-bit ABIs that need split/aligned 64-bit arguments (s390 31-bit, mips o32), passing off_t through variadic syscall() does not match the kernel ABI, so the offset/nbytes the kernel sees are not the ones the test intends.
  • Evidence: sync_file_range01.c:139-142; include/lapi/sync_file_range.h:19-49; include/lapi/syscalls/{powerpc,powerpc64,arm}.in
  • Suggested action: Call the lapi/glibc sync_file_range() (or reuse its per-arch logic) instead of the raw syscall.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN,GIT,READ. HPE x86_64: 5/5 TPASS. include/lapi/syscalls/{powerpc,powerpc64}.in define only sync_file_range2, arm.in only arm_sync_file_range/sync_file_range2, so __NR_sync_file_range is invalid there and tst_syscall() TBROKs/TCONFs with ENOSYS. git: b694c81a8b72 (2021 new-API conversion) replaced the arch-aware sync_file_range() wrapper call with raw tst_syscall(__NR_sync_file_range)
  • Verification (phase 3, glibc vs musl build and libc sources): CONFIRMED via MUSL,RUN,SRC. HPE glibc 5/5, musl 5/5 TPASS (x86_64). Both libcs’ wrappers carry the per-arch logic the raw tst_syscall(__NR_sync_file_range) skips: musl src/linux/sync_file_range.c:8-16 uses SYS_sync_file_range2 when defined and __SYSCALL_LL_O/E arg splitting; glibc linux/sync_file_range.c:25-31 sync_file_range2 + __ALIGNMENT_ARG SYSCALL_LL64

testcases/kernel/syscalls/timerfd/timerfd01.c (runtest: syscalls/timerfd01)

  • Category: FRAGILE
  • Confidence: low (phase 1: medium)
  • Claim under test: A periodic (50 ms) absolute timerfd delivers the right number of expirations.
  • Problem: tnow is sampled before timerfd_settime(). The timer expires at tnow+50, +100, +150, +200 ms. After usleep(160000) plus a timerfd_gettime() call, the test requires exactly 3 ticks (ticks != exp_ticks -> TFAIL). If the process is delayed more than about 40 ms in total (usleep oversleep on a loaded host/VM, preemption, CPU throttling), the read returns 4 ticks and the test fails on a correct kernel.
  • Evidence: timerfd01.c:115-132 (settime at tnow+50ms, interval 50ms; usleep(160000); waittmr(tfd, 3)); 85-90 exact comparison
  • Suggested action: Accept ticks >= 3 and bound it by the elapsed time measured around the read (expected = floor((t_read - t_first)/50ms) + 1), or block in read() without the sleep and check ticks == 1 per period.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): REVISED via REPEAT,STRESS,VIRT,MUTATION. Not reproduced: HPE 5x’-i 20’ plain, 3x’-i 100’ plain, 5x’-i 20’ under stress-ng; VIRT (1 CPU) 3x’-i 20’ plain + 3x under stress: all pass. Work copy with usleep(160000+45000) emulating a 45 ms oversleep: ‘TFAIL: got 4 tick(s) expected 3’ -> mechanism real, but it needs a >40 ms stall
  • Verification conclusion: The window is real: any stall over ~40 ms between settime and read gives 4 ticks. But neither CPU/io/vm stress on 24 CPUs nor a 1-CPU VM produced one. Keep the finding at low: it needs a heavily overcommitted VM (steal) or RT-priority contention. The action is unchanged (accept >= 3 or compute the expected ticks from the elapsed time).

testcases/kernel/syscalls/ustat/ustat01.c (runtest: syscalls/ustat01)

  • Category: FRAGILE
  • Confidence: high
  • Claim under test: ustat(2) succeeds for the device of the root filesystem; Btrfs is skipped because ustat() is known to return EINVAL there.
  • Problem: The Btrfs exclusion is done with .skip_filesystems, which (without .all_filesystems) checks tst_fs_type("."), i.e. the filesystem of the current working directory. The test has no .needs_tmpdir, so “.” is wherever the runner started it, while the device under test is stat("/").st_dev. On a host whose “/” is a Btrfs subvolume (Fedora default) and whose cwd is on another fs (or vice versa), the skip does not trigger and ustat() returns EINVAL (st_dev of a Btrfs subvolume is an anonymous dev, not sb->s_dev), producing a false FAIL; conversely it may TCONF needlessly.
  • Evidence: ustat01.c:39-49; lib/tst_test.c:1643-1653 (tst_fs_type(".")); linux fs/statfs.c:235-240 (user_get_super(dev) -> -EINVAL when no sb has that s_dev).
  • Suggested action: stat “.” (or a needs_tmpdir file) instead of “/”, or explicitly check tst_fs_type("/") against Btrfs in setup and TCONF.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN,VIRT. HPE (/ is btrfs): run from cwd /var/tmp/ltp (btrfs) -> ‘TCONF: btrfs is not supported by the test’; same binary from cwd /dev/shm (tmpfs) -> ‘ustat01.c:29: TFAIL: ustat(2) failed: EINVAL (22)’. Skip checks cwd fs, test uses stat(“/”).st_dev. VIRT from btrfs cwd: TCONF

testcases/kernel/syscalls/ustat/ustat02.c (runtest: syscalls/ustat02)

  • Category: FRAGILE
  • Confidence: high
  • Claim under test: ustat(2) returns EINVAL for an invalid dev and EFAULT for a bad buffer.
  • Problem: Same skip mismatch as ustat01: the Btrfs skip checks the cwd filesystem but the EFAULT case uses stat("/").st_dev. On a Btrfs root, vfs_ustat() fails with EINVAL before copy_to_user() is reached, so the EFAULT subcase fails with EINVAL on a correct kernel.
  • Evidence: ustat02.c:33,55-57,64-67; linux fs/statfs.c:247-262 (EINVAL returned before copy_to_user()); lib/tst_test.c:1643-1653.
  • Suggested action: use the st_dev of “.” / the tmpdir, or check the fs type of “/” in setup.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN,VIRT. HPE (/ is btrfs): from cwd btrfs -> TCONF; from cwd /dev/shm (tmpfs) -> ‘TPASS: ustat(2) expected failure: EINVAL’ then ‘ustat02.c:45: TFAIL: ustat(2) failed to produce expected error; 14, errno: EFAULT: EINVAL (22)’ (EINVAL returned before copy_to_user)

testcases/kernel/syscalls/waitid/waitid10.c (runtest: syscalls/waitid10)

  • Category: FRAGILE
  • Confidence: medium (phase 1: low)
  • Claim under test: waitid() reports a child terminated by SIGFPE (si_status SIGFPE, si_code CLD_DUMPED when a core is produced, CLD_KILLED otherwise).
  • Problem: setup() predicts whether a core dump will happen only from RLIMIT_CORE and the first character of core_pattern. The kernel sets the “dumped” bit (-> CLD_DUMPED) only when the dump is actually started successfully. A non-zero RLIMIT_CORE smaller than binfmt->min_coredump (ELF_EXEC_PAGESIZE; setup keeps any non-zero rlim_cur as is), a core_pattern pointing to a non-existent/unwritable directory (e.g. non-root run with an absolute core_pattern), or a pipe helper that cannot be spawned all give CLD_KILLED while the test expects CLD_DUMPED: a false FAIL on a correct kernel. (A truncated dump still counts as dumped: binfmt_elf sets has_dumped before writing.)
  • Evidence: waitid10.c:39-42,45-67; linux fs/coredump.c:553-560 (0x80 only if core_dumped), fs/coredump.c:886 (limit < min_coredump -> no dump), fs/binfmt_elf.c:2019-2023.
  • Suggested action: raise rlim_cur to at least the page size / rlim_max unconditionally (as waitpid01 does), and accept either CLD_DUMPED or CLD_KILLED when core_pattern is not a plain relative name, or verify the core file exists in tmpdir.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN,VIRT,READ. HPE (core_pattern |systemd-coredump): as-is, ulimit -c 1 (=1024 B) and hard limit 0 all TPASS CLD_DUMPED (pipes ignore RLIMIT_CORE). ‘prlimit –core=1:unlimited waitid10’ -> ‘TFAIL: infop->si_code (2) != CLD_DUMPED (3)’ (fs/coredump.c: limit==1 aborts pipe dumps); –core=4096 TPASS. VIRT as-is TPASS

testcases/kernel/sysfs/class/hwmon/sys_hwmon01.c (runtest: sysfs/sys_hwmon01)

  • Category: FRAGILE
  • Confidence: high
  • Claim under test: every present hwmon tempN/fanN/inN/currN/powerN input, pwmN and update_interval holds a value in a plausible range.
  • Problem: The *_SILENT asserts only skip when the file does not exist. If the file exists but read() fails, file_scanf() fails and range_check()/bool_check() report TFAIL “does not contain a number”. The hwmon ABI documents exactly that for disabled sensors (“When disabled the sensor read will return -ENODATA” for inY/fanY/tempY/currY/powerY_enable), and real drivers do it for valid hardware states: drivetemp returns -ENODATA when the drive reports no valid SCT temperature, ina3221 for a disabled channel, plus I/O errors (-EIO/-ETIMEDOUT/-EAGAIN) from I2C/EC/BMC-backed sensors. Any of these gives a false TFAIL on a correct kernel.
  • Evidence: test lines 61-119; lib/tst_sysfs_assert.c range_check()/bool_check() (TFAIL when file_scanf fails); Documentation/ABI/testing/sysfs-class-hwmon:155-159, 291-295, 591-595, 692-696, 887-892; drivers/hwmon/drivetemp.c:267-279; drivers/hwmon/ina3221.c:287-289, 344-346.
  • Suggested action: treat a read error (especially ENODATA, also EIO/EAGAIN/ETIMEDOUT) on hwmon attributes as TCONF/TINFO, not TFAIL, e.g. with a “read-tolerant” variant of the silent asserts, or check tempN_enable etc. first.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN,VIRT,MUTATION. HPE: as-is 27/27 TPASS (coretemp, i350bb, power_meter); VIRT TCONF no hwmon. Read error simulated in a private mount ns by bind-mounting /sys/class/net/lo/speed (read -> EINVAL) over hwmon2/temp1_input: ‘TINFO: The FILE … ended prematurely’ + ‘TFAIL: /sys/class/hwmon/hwmon2/temp1_input does not contain a number’ -> any -ENODATA/-EIO attribute read is a TFAIL

testcases/kernel/sysfs/class/net/sys_net04.c (runtest: sysfs/sys_net04)

  • Category: FRAGILE
  • Confidence: medium
  • Claim under test: TUN operstate follows fd attach/detach (“down” after close, “up” after reopen).
  • Problem: operstate is applied by linkwatch. For a TUN device (no ndo_get_iflink, so iflink == ifindex) the carrier-off event is non-urgent, and linkwatch_schedule_work() delays it until linkwatch_nextevent, which can be up to HZ (1 s) after the previous linkwatch run. setup() and the s0 check have just caused such a run. TST_RETRY_FUNC(…, 1) polls for about 1.05 s in total (exponential usleep up to 2^20 us), so the margin is about 50 ms plus workqueue latency. On a loaded or slow VM the retry can expire and check_state() reports TFAIL. sys_net02 (veth) is not affected because veth events are urgent (iflink != ifindex).
  • Evidence: test lines 164-166; /usr/src/linux/net/core/link_watch.c linkwatch_urgent_event() and linkwatch_schedule_work() (“delay = linkwatch_nextevent - jiffies”, capped at HZ), linkwatch_nextevent = jiffies + HZ; include/tst_common.h:45-66 TST_RETRY_FUNC.
  • Suggested action: use TST_RETRY_FN_EXP_BACKOFF(…, 3) or similar (more than 1 s plus margin) for the operstate wait in sys_net_common.h users.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via REPEAT,STRESS,VIRT,RUN. No TFAIL: HPE 5 plain + 2x’-i 10’ + 5 under stress, VIRT 3 plain + 3 under stress all pass. But a helper that closes a persistent TUN fd and polls operstate every 1 ms measured ‘down after’ 1021-1024 ms in 8/10 cycles (943 and 72 ms in the others), against TST_RETRY_FUNC’s ~1.048 s exp-backoff budget: about 25 ms margin, as described

testcases/kernel/sysfs/class/rtc/sys_rtc01.c (runtest: sysfs/sys_rtc01)

  • Category: FRAGILE
  • Confidence: high (phase 1: medium)
  • Claim under test: the primary RTC’s since_epoch is close to time(2), within 10 s plus 200 ppm of uptime (x10 in a VM).
  • Problem: since_epoch is the raw RTC value interpreted as UTC (rtc_tm_to_time64 of the hardware time). On systems that keep the RTC in local time (dual-boot with Windows, hwclock --localtime, timedatectl set-local-rtc 1, all supported by util-linux and systemd), since_epoch differs from system time by the UTC offset (often 3600 s or more). The test then TFAILs on a correct kernel. The comment only waves away “booted with an RTC that is fairly off”, which is a different case. Embedded boards with a battery-less RTC that NTP later corrects hit the same problem when hctosys=1.
  • Evidence: test lines 87-104, 191-211; /usr/src/linux/drivers/rtc/sysfs.c since_epoch_show() (rtc_read_time + rtc_tm_to_time64, no timezone handling).
  • Suggested action: downgrade the system-time comparison to TINFO/TCONF when the diff is a whole number of 15-minute timezone units, or check /etc/adjtime for LOCAL, or drop the system-time check and keep the internal date/time vs since_epoch consistency check.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN,VIRT. VIRT: as-is 4/4 TPASS (diff 0s). RTC set 1 h off UTC with hwclock –set –utc –noadjfile (what a local-time RTC in a UTC-1 zone looks like): date/time vs since_epoch still TPASS, but ‘TFAIL: rtc0: since_epoch (1791969903), system time (1791973503), diff 3600s > slack 110s’. RTC restored (hwclock –systohc), rerun TPASS

testcases/kernel/sysfs/devices/system/node/sys_node01.c (runtest: sysfs/sys_node01)

  • Category: FRAGILE
  • Confidence: high
  • Claim under test: for each online node, MemUsed == MemTotal - MemFree in nodeN/meminfo.
  • Problem: The kernel computes all three values from one si_meminfo_node() snapshot, so a single read of the file is self-consistent. The test calls SAFE_FILE_LINES_SCANF() three times (lines 61-63), i.e. it opens and reads the file three times. MemFree (NR_FREE_PAGES) changes continuously on any running system (page cache, the LTP harness itself, kswapd, other tests), so “used” from the third read rarely equals “total - free” from the second, and the test TFAILs on a correct kernel.
  • Evidence: test lines 43-75; /usr/src/linux/drivers/base/node.c:451-460 node_read_meminfo() (single si_meminfo_node(&i, nid), MemUsed = totalram - freeram).
  • Suggested action: read nodeN/meminfo once (read the file into a buffer and sscanf all three keys from it) before comparing.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via REPEAT,STRESS,VIRT. VIRT ltpstress ‘sys_node01 -i 50’ x3: 1 run failed with 3 TFAILs, e.g. ‘node0: MemUsed (1703176) != MemTotal (3712024) - MemFree (2010872)’ (off by 24 kB: the three separate reads saw different MemFree). HPE: 5 plain, 3 x ‘-i 200’ plain, 5 under stress all pass; VIRT 3 plain pass

testcases/kernel/sysfs/power/sys_power01.c (runtest: sysfs/sys_power01)

  • Category: FRAGILE
  • Confidence: high (phase 1: medium)
  • Claim under test: /sys/power/wakeup_count is non-negative (plus format checks of other /sys/power files).
  • Problem: Reading wakeup_count is a blocking operation by design. pm_get_wakeup_count(…, true) sleeps until no wakeup event is in progress and only returns early on a signal. On systems with a wakeup source held for a long time (an Android-style /sys/power/wake_lock, a device driver keeping a wakeup source active, laptops with chatty wakeup devices), the read blocks until the LTP timeout kills the test (TBROK), and the hang has nothing to do with the property being checked.
  • Evidence: test line 190; /usr/src/linux/kernel/power/main.c wakeup_count_show(); drivers/base/power/wakeup.c pm_get_wakeup_count(); Documentation/ABI/testing/sysfs-power:174-178 (“Reading from it … blocks if some wakeup events are being processed at the time the file is read from”).
  • Suggested action: read wakeup_count from a child with alarm()/timeout, or check /sys/class/wakeup/*/active_count deltas instead; at minimum add a comment and a short .timeout with a TCONF on timeout.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN,VIRT. VIRT: sys_power01 9/9 TPASS as-is. With an EPOLLWAKEUP wakeup source held active by a helper (eventfd ready, never harvested): ‘timeout 5 cat /sys/power/wakeup_count’ rc=124, sys_power01 reaches line 60 then ‘Test timeouted, sending SIGKILL!’ TBROK (rc=2); after release the read returns 9 at once

testcases/kernel/thermal/thermal_interrupt_events.c (runtest: thermal/thermal_interrupt_events)

  • Category: FRAGILE
  • Confidence: high (phase 1: medium)
  • Claim under test: lowering x86_pkg_temp trip_point_1_temp to just above the current temperature and loading the CPU raises “Thermal event interrupts” in /proc/interrupts.
  • Problem: The kernel feature is only exercised if the workload raises the package temperature by more than TEMP_INCREMENT (5 C) within the run windows (10 s, then 9 s, …). After every unsuccessful window, set_trippoint() moves the threshold to the new current temperature + 5 C, so slow warming never catches up. Whether the temperature rises that fast depends on cooling, TDP/power limits, fan curves, and how hot the package already is (an idle-hot package near PL limits barely moves). On such hardware the test TFAILs (“No thermal interrupt increase detected” or “temperature did not rise as expected”) with no kernel defect. It also needs about 400 s per zone plus a fixed 300 s sleep() cooldown between zones.
  • Evidence: test lines 22-26, 120-136, 138-150, 152-186, 231-236.
  • Suggested action: set the threshold relative to the temperature reached under load (or a smaller increment), and report TCONF instead of TFAIL when the temperature never crosses temp_high, since then the interrupt path was not exercised.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN. HPE (Xeon, 1 x86_pkg_temp zone, exclusive run): ‘thermal_interrupt_events -D’: zone at 43 C, 10 load windows (24 busy children, 10 s..1 s) never raised it (43,42,40,40,39,38,39,39,38,38 C), trip point moved to temp+5 C each round -> ‘TFAIL: No thermal interrupt increase detected’; TRM count 0 before and after

testcases/kernel/tracing/dynamic_debug/dynamic_debug01.sh (runtest: tracing/dynamic_debug01)

  • Category: FRAGILE (secondary: WRONG)
  • Confidence: high (phase 1: medium)
  • Claim under test: toggling dynamic debug flags on every func/file/line/module does not cause kernel issues, detected by searching dmesg.
  • Problem: (1) The dmesg check greps case-sensitively for the bare substrings “fault” and “warn” (line 113). These match ordinary text such as “default” or “warning” in any message. While the test runs it enables +p on every pr_debug site in the kernel, one function/file/line/module at a time, so whatever debug output those sites print (plus unrelated messages from the rest of the system) ends up in dmesg.new, and a correct kernel can get TFAIL “Issues found in dmesg!”. (2) New messages are separated from old ones by deleting the first wc -l dmesg.old lines (line 110). If the debug flood wraps the printk ring buffer, the cut lands in the wrong place, so new messages can be dropped (missed issues) or old ones re-included (false failures).
  • Evidence: test lines 78-83, 93-117.
  • Suggested action: use dmesg -c/a timestamp or --since boundary (or a shell-loader (tst_run_shell) test with .taint_check) and match real oops markers (e.g. “BUG:”, “WARNING:”, “Oops”, “general protection fault”) rather than “fault”/“warn”.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN. HPE exclusive: as-is TPASS twice (run takes ~4 s). Same run with one benign line ‘ltp-v09: using default settings’ written to /dev/kmsg 1 s in: ‘dynamic_debug01 1 TFAIL: Issues found in dmesg!’ (bare ‘fault’ substring matches ‘default’). Ring-buffer wrap part not reproduced (little pr_debug output here)

testcases/kernel/watchqueue/wqueue02.c (runtest: watchqueue/wqueue02)

  • Category: FRAGILE
  • Confidence: high (phase 1: low)
  • Claim under test: KEYCTL_UNLINK produces NOTIFY_KEY_UNLINKED on the watched session keyring.
  • Problem: The callback reports TFAIL for every notification in the read buffer that is not NOTIFY_KEY_UNLINKED, including WATCH_TYPE_META ones (wqueue_key_event() returns 0 for non-key types). Unlinking drops the key’s last reference, so key_put() schedules key_gc_work, and key_gc_unused_keys() calls remove_watch_list(key->watchers, …), which posts WATCH_META_REMOVAL_NOTIFICATION for the watch the test placed on the key. If the GC worker runs before the test’s single read() (e.g. the per-CPU kworker preempts the task on syscall return), both notes arrive in one buffer and the test reports TPASS + TFAIL on a correct kernel. The same mechanism affects wqueue05 (invalidate, which triggers immediate GC) and wqueue06 (clear).
  • Evidence: wqueue02.c:16-23, 33-34; common.h:28-38, 123-161; /usr/src/linux/security/keys/key.c:647-667 key_put(); security/keys/gc.c:148 remove_watch_list(); include/linux/watch_queue.h:111-117; kernel/watch_queue.c:560-569.
  • Suggested action: ignore WATCH_TYPE_META in the key-event callbacks (as wqueue08/09 already filter by type) and require that at least one matching note was seen, instead of failing on each non-matching note.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN,REPEAT,STRESS,VIRT. VIRT (1 CPU) under stress-ng: 15/100 TFAIL; each failing run reads NOTIFY[000] ty=1 sy=03 (UNLINKED, TPASS) plus NOTIFY[010] ty=000000 sy=00 (WATCH_META_REMOVAL) -> ‘TFAIL: keyctl unlink has not been recognized’; unstressed VIRT 0/130, HPE 0/50

testcases/kernel/watchqueue/wqueue05.c (runtest: watchqueue/wqueue05)

  • Category: FRAGILE
  • Confidence: high (phase 1: low)
  • Claim under test: KEYCTL_INVALIDATE produces NOTIFY_KEY_INVALIDATED.
  • Problem: Same as wqueue02. key_invalidate() schedules GC right away (key_schedule_gc_links()), the GC unlinks the invalidated key and frees it, and remove_watch_list() posts a META removal note. If it lands in the same read(), the callback TFAILs on it.

  • Suggested action: as for wqueue02.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN,REPEAT,STRESS,VIRT. VIRT under stress-ng: 38/100 TFAIL, failing runs read INVALIDATED (sy=06, TPASS) plus META removal note ty=0 sy=0 -> ‘TFAIL: keyctl invalidate has not been recognized’; unstressed VIRT 1/30 + 0/100, HPE 0/50

testcases/kernel/watchqueue/wqueue06.c (runtest: watchqueue/wqueue06)

testcases/lib/run_tests.sh (runtest: none; make test-shell-loader, CI .github/workflows/ci-docker-build.yml:194)

testcases/network/busy_poll/busy_poll01.sh (runtest: net.features/busy_poll01, busy_poll01_ipv6)

  • Category: FRAGILE
  • Confidence: high (phase 1: medium)
  • Claim under test: enabling net.core.busy_read/busy_poll=50 lowers netstress round-trip time.
  • Problem: The only assertion is tst_netload_compare res_0 res_50 1, i.e. busy polling must make the run at least 1% faster than without it. That is a performance claim, not a functional one. Busy polling only does anything when the socket has a NAPI id from a NAPI-capable driver. On the default LTP netns/veth setup, packets go through the backlog path with no NAPI id, so the setting has no effect and the result is noise around 0%. Single-run timing noise can also land below 1% on real NICs. A FAIL can only be avoided by setting LTP_NET_FEATURES_IGNORE_PERFORMANCE_FAILURE=1.
  • Evidence: busy_poll01.sh:39-45; testcases/lib/tst_net.sh:919-930 (TFAIL when res < threshold_low); busy_poll_lib.sh:21-25 (driver capability checked only for kernels < 4.5).
  • Suggested action: Turn the comparison into TINFO, or require a NAPI-capable device (check SO_INCOMING_NAPI_ID != 0) and TCONF otherwise. Also consider averaging more runs.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): REVISED via RUN,REPEAT,VIRT. VIRT (1 CPU, netns veth): 3/3 TFAIL ‘performance result is -464%/-436%/-717% < threshold 1%’ (median 253 ms with busy poll vs 44 ms without); HPE (24 CPU): 3/3 TPASS, ‘performance result is 50%’ (27 vs 54 ms) -> not noise around 0% as claimed, but a verdict that depends on CPU count: busy polling starves the peer on 1 CPU and always fails; HPE stress runs not obtained (lock queue)
  • Verification conclusion: The result is not noise around 0%. On the veth/netns setup the verdict depends on the CPU count: on a 1-CPU guest, busy polling starves the peer and the test always fails by a factor of about 5, while on 24 CPUs it gains about 50%. The finding still holds (a performance assertion decides pass/fail) but the mechanism is different. Corrected action: TCONF or TINFO when nproc < 2 (or make the comparison TINFO), keeping the NAPI-id check idea. HPE stress runs were not obtained because the host lock queue was too long.

testcases/network/busy_poll/busy_poll02.sh (runtest: net.features/busy_poll02, busy_poll02_ipv6)

  • Category: FRAGILE
  • Confidence: high (phase 1: medium)
  • Claim under test: setting SO_BUSY_POLL=50 per socket (with net.core.busy_poll) lowers latency.
  • Problem: Same as busy_poll01. The pass/fail verdict needs at least a 1% speedup, which depends on the NIC driver/NAPI and on timing noise.

testcases/network/busy_poll/busy_poll03.sh (runtest: net.features/busy_poll03, busy_poll03_ipv6)

  • Category: FRAGILE (secondary: OBSOLETE)
  • Confidence: high (phase 1: medium)
  • Claim under test: SO_BUSY_POLL lowers latency for UDP and UDP-Lite sockets.
  • Problem: Has the same performance-threshold problem as busy_poll01. In addition, the udp_lite iteration (TST_TEST_DATA) targets UDP-Lite, which was fully removed in v7.1. socket(…, IPPROTO_UDPLITE) now fails, and the test TCONFs through SAFE_SOCKET -> tst_netload.
  • Evidence: busy_poll03.sh:7,36-40; kernel commit 56520b398e5e “ipv4: Retire UDP-Lite.” (v7.1-rc1) plus the IPv6 counterpart; net/ipv4/udplite.c no longer exists in /usr/src/linux.

VIRT (1 CPU): 3/3 TFAIL -580% (udp) < threshold 1%; udp_lite iteration: ‘netstress.c:675: TCONF: socket(10, 2, 136) failed: EPROTONOSUPPORT’ + ‘TCONF: server failed’ on 7.2.10 (UDP-Lite removed, secondary OBSOLETE confirmed); HPE (24 CPU): 3/3 pass (udp TPASS, udp_lite TCONF)
  • Verification conclusion: The udp case has the same CPU-count dependence. The udp_lite iteration TCONFs on 7.2 because UDP-Lite was removed, so the secondary OBSOLETE finding is confirmed. Drop udp_lite or gate it on the kernel version.

testcases/network/multicast/mc_commo/mc_commo.sh (runtest: net.multicast/mc_commo)

  • Category: FRAGILE (secondary: WRONG)
  • Confidence: high
  • Claim under test: UDP datagrams sent to a multicast group from rhost are received on lhost.
  • Problem: Synchronisation is done entirely with sleeps: sleep 5 for mc_recv to start, sleep 10 for mc_send, sleep 100 for data. The pass condition greps mc_recv’s stdout, which goes to a file and is therefore fully buffered. About 100 short lines (< 4 KiB) are only flushed when mc_recv exits, which happens only when the final UDP “quit” datagram arrives. mc_send needs about 99 s (99 x sleep(1)), leaving roughly 10 s of margin. If the “quit” datagram is lost or delayed past the window, the file is empty and the test reports a false TFAIL “NO Datagrams received”. Separately, grep -q "cannot join group" $OUTFILE can never match: mc_recv writes the error to stderr (not redirected), and the text is “can not join group”. The membership check therefore relies only on netstat. GROUP_ADDR is derived from a ps | grep process count, which lands in the 224.0.0.0/24 local-control block.
  • Evidence: mc_commo.sh:51-75; mc_recv.c:83 (perror “can not join group”), :100 (printf without fflush/setvbuf); mc_send.c:97-115.
  • Suggested action: Make mc_recv line-buffered (setvbuf/fflush) and poll the output file for the expected lines with a timeout instead of the fixed sleeps. Fix the join-failure grep (stderr plus correct text). Use a fixed group outside 224.0.0.0/24.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN,VIRT. VIRT: as-is TCONF ‘netstat’ not found (Fedora 44 lacks net-tools). testcases/network/rpc/rpc-tirpc/tests_pack/rpc_suite/tirpc/tirpc_simple_rpc_broadcast/tirpc_rpc_broadcast.c (runtest: net.tirpc_tests/tirpc_rpc_broadcast)

  • Problem: libtirpc implements rpc_broadcast() as an RPCBPROC_CALLIT (and PMAPPROC_CALLIT) indirect call sent to rpcbind on the broadcast address, so it depends on rpcbind remote-call support. rpcbind disabled remote calls by default in 1.2.5. On such builds rpcbind does not forward the call, no reply arrives, and rpc_broadcast returns RPC_TIMEDOUT after ~8s, which is a false FAIL. rpc_test.sh already TCONFs for exactly this rpcbind configuration (commit 9f512c1d82c1), but only for rpc_pmap_rmtcall and tirpc_rpcb_rmtcall, not for the broadcast clients. The test also needs a broadcast-capable interface between lhost and rhost.

  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): REVISED via RUN,MUTATION,REPEAT,VIRT. As-is TFAIL 7/7 HPE, 3/3 VIRT though rpcbind says ‘remote calls: yes’; rpcinfo -m CALLIT counters unchanged. Debug client: ‘RPC: Timed out’, ifa_broadaddr of ltp_ns_veth1 = 10.0.0.1 (own addr; tst_net adds addrs without brd). rpc_test.sh mutant re-adding both addrs with ‘brd +’: TPASS 5/5 HPE, 5/5 HPE stress, 10/10 VIRT (one earlier set of 5 runs on VIRT all failed, unexplained).
  • Verification conclusion: The test is indeed environment-dependent, but the dominant cause on a stock setup is not rpcbind remote calls: tst_net.sh adds the IPv4 test addresses without a broadcast address, glibc then reports the interface address as ifa_broadaddr, and libtirpc “broadcasts” to the client itself, so the test fails deterministically in the default netns setup. Corrected action: add IPv4 addresses with brd + in tst_net.sh (or in rpc_test.sh for broadcast clients), and also add the broadcast clients to the ‘remote calls: no’ TCONF check as phase 1 suggested. The rpc-tirpc suite builds and installs completely and was run through rpc_test.sh with rpcbind running.
  • Verification (phase 3, glibc vs musl build and libc sources): CONFIRMED via RUN,REPEAT,MUTATION,MUSL,SRC. HPE glibc TFAIL 3/3; musl TFAIL 3/3. getifaddrs in ltp_ns: ltp_ns_veth1 broadaddr=10.0.0.1 (own addr) under BOTH libcs: glibc linux/ifaddrs.c:626-637, musl network/getifaddrs.c:175-182 (IFA_LOCAL moves addr into the broadaddr/dstaddr union). brd + mutant rpc_test.sh: musl TPASS 3/3. Cause is tst_net, not glibc

testcases/network/rpc/rpc-tirpc/tests_pack/rpc_suite/tirpc/tirpc_simple_rpc_broadcast_exp/tirpc_rpc_broadcast_exp.c (runtest: net.tirpc_tests/tirpc_rpc_broadcast_exp)

  • Category: FRAGILE
  • Confidence: high (phase 1: medium)
  • Claim under test: rpc_broadcast_exp() with inittime=1ms, waittime=2ms returns RPC_SUCCESS.
  • Problem: (1) The rpcbind CALLIT dependency is the same as for tirpc_rpc_broadcast: no TCONF when rpcbind is built without remote calls. (2) The runtest passes -e “1,2”, i.e. inittime=1 ms and waittime=2 ms. libtirpc polls for 1 ms, rebroadcasts, polls for 2 ms, then gives up (for (msec = inittime; msec <= waittime; msec += msec)). In about 3 ms the broadcast has to reach rpcbind on lhost, be forwarded to tirpc_svc_1, and the reply must come back across the netns/veth or a real link to rhost. On a loaded or virtualised system, or with a real second host, that fails without any kernel or library bug.
  • Evidence: tirpc_rpc_broadcast_exp.c:66-72; runtest/net.tirpc_tests:41 -e "1,2"; libtirpc src/clnt_bcast.c retry loop as quoted above.
  • Suggested action: add to the rmtcall TCONF list; use realistic timeouts (e.g. -e “500,2000”).
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): REVISED via RUN,MUTATION,REPEAT,STRESS,VIRT. As-is ‘-e 1,2’ TFAIL 6/6 HPE, 3/3 VIRT: same missing-broadcast-address cause as tirpc_rpc_broadcast (packet goes to the client’s own 10.0.0.1). With ‘brd +’ fix: TPASS 5/5 HPE plain, 5/5 under stress-ng, 10/10 VIRT -> the 1 ms/2 ms timeout part was not reproduced on netns/veth.
  • Verification conclusion: Fails for the same missing-broadcast-address reason as tirpc_rpc_broadcast. Once that is fixed, the 1 ms/2 ms timing was not a problem on netns/veth even under load (20 passes); the timeout concern remains plausible only for a real two-host setup, so it is a secondary, unproven point. The rpc-tirpc suite builds and installs completely and was run through rpc_test.sh with rpcbind running.
  • Verification (phase 3, glibc vs musl build and libc sources): CONFIRMED via RUN,REPEAT,MUTATION,MUSL,SRC. HPE ‘-e 1,2’: glibc TFAIL 3/3; musl TFAIL 3/3. Same missing-broadcast-address cause as tirpc_rpc_broadcast: ifa_broadaddr = own addr under both libcs (glibc ifaddrs.c:626-637, musl getifaddrs.c:175-182). brd + mutant: musl TPASS 3/3, so the 1ms/2ms timing is no problem under musl either

testcases/network/rpc/rpc-tirpc/tests_pack/rpc_suite/tirpc/tirpc_simple_rpc_reg/tirpc_rpc_reg.c (runtest: net.tirpc_tests/tirpc_rpc_reg)

The stale entry can satisfy that check before the new server has re-registered, so the readiness check can be bypassed. The only assertion is rpc_reg()==0, and the registration is never looked up.
  • Evidence: tirpc_rpc_reg.c:65-68; rpc_test.sh do_test readiness loop and cleanup() (only with SERVER_STARTED); runtest/net.tirpc_tests:38-39 ordering.

  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN,READ. HPE: ‘rpc_test.sh -c tirpc_rpc_reg’ TPASS, afterwards rpcinfo shows stale ‘536875000 1 tcp 50951’ and ‘536875000 1 udp 64237’ (dead process). Next tirpc_rpc_call TPASS and its cleaner removed them; the readiness-bypass race (stale entry satisfies the rpcinfo grep) not reproduced in 1 run; window is server start->re-register.

testcases/network/sctp/sctp01.sh (runtest: net.features/sctp01, sctp01_ipv6)

Throughput depends on NIC/virtio offloads (TSO/GRO for TCP vs SCTP GSO/CRC offload), CPU and load, so it can FAIL on a correct kernel. The thresholds were already widened once to avoid false positives (f6200f64560c), and LTP_NET_FEATURES_IGNORE_PERFORMANCE_FAILURE=1 downgrades to TINFO, but that is opt-in. Beyond the transfer completing, no SCTP functional property is checked.

  • Suggested action: treat netstress success as the functional PASS and report the ratio as TINFO/TWARN only.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN,REPEAT,STRESS,VIRT. HPE idle: ltprepeat 5 sctp01.sh 0/5 pass, -6 0/5 pass; all fail subtest 2 (-A 65000), e.g. TCP 338 ms vs SCTP 1402 ms -> ‘TFAIL: performance result is -314% < threshold -200%’ (range -228..-376%). HPE under stress-ng: 10/10 PASS. VIRT 1 CPU: 5 pass + 1 TWARN, detail runs -159..-161%. Pure perf ratio on a working kernel.

testcases/network/tcp_cc/dctcp01.sh (runtest: net.features dctcp_ipv4_01, dctcp_ipv6_01)

  • Category: FRAGILE
  • Confidence: low (phase 1: medium)
  • Claim under test: DCTCP works with netem loss 0.5% + ECN marking.
  • Problem: pass/fail is a throughput comparison. tcp_cc_test01 passes threshold 10 to tst_netload_compare, so the test needs DCTCP to finish at least 10% faster than cubic. Unlike bbr01/02 (threshold -100, i.e. “not more than 2x slower”), this asks for a performance gain, which depends on link type (veth/netns vs real NIC), CPU load and netem behaviour, not on kernel correctness. The only escape is the LTP_NET_FEATURES_IGNORE_PERFORMANCE_FAILURE env var.
  • Evidence: dctcp01.sh:33 (tcp_cc_test01 dctcp 10); testcases/lib/tst_net.sh:919-929 (res = (base-new)*100/base; TFAIL if res < threshold_low).
  • Suggested action: use a non-positive threshold (e.g. -50, as for bbr) and/or check that ECN was negotiated (ss -i shows “ecn”/“dctcp”) rather than relying on a speedup.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): REVISED via RUN,REPEAT,STRESS,VIRT. HPE (tc from rpm on PATH) plain: 97,97,96,97,95%; ltpstress 3x: 73,78,91%; VIRT 3x: 89,91,89% vs threshold 10%. One plain run TBROK (netstress connect ETIMEDOUT), unrelated to threshold. Gap is structural (netem ‘loss 0.5% ecn’ marks ECT dctcp packets, drops non-ECN cubic ones); not reproduced in 11 runs.
  • Verification conclusion: The 10% speed-up requirement was met by a wide margin everywhere (73-97%). The gap is structural: netem loss 0.5% ecn marks ECN-capable (dctcp) packets instead of dropping them, but drops non-ECN cubic packets, so the threshold effectively checks that ECN works. Not reproduced in 11 runs; keep as low-confidence FRAGILE (an ECN-less path would fail it, which is arguably correct). Note: the hosts lack tc; on stock Fedora 44 without iproute-tc the test TCONFs.

testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/interfaces/clock_settime/8-1.c (openposix: conformance/interfaces/clock_settime/8-1)

  • Category: FRAGILE

Any external step (NTP/chrony, VM time sync) in that window produces a false FAIL. That is exactly the failure class commit 9ecb4a004b18 fixed in sibling tests 4-1, 5-1, 5-2, 7-1, 7-2 by adding pts_mono_time_start()/pts_mono_time_check() with retries; 8-1 (and 1-1, 4-2) were not converted.
  • Evidence: clock_settime/8-1.c:45-112; git show 9ecb4a004b18 (touches only 4-1, 5-1, 5-2, 7-1, 7-2).
  • Suggested action: Apply the same pts_mono interference detection/retry loop to 8-1.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): UNCHANGED via RUN,REPEAT,STRESS,VIRT,GIT. PASS 14/14 (HPE 1+5+5 under stress, VIRT 3); chronyd active on HPE but did not step. External step during the 5 s window not injected (stepping the shared hosts’ clock not allowed). git 9ecb4a004b18 fixed exactly this failure class in 4-1/5-1/5-2/7-1/7-2 only; 8-1 still has no pts_mono check

testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/interfaces/fork/21-1.c (openposix: conformance/interfaces/fork/21-1)

  • Category: FRAGILE
  • Confidence: low
  • Claim under test: the child process has only one thread (the parent’s helper thread does not run in the child).
  • Problem: the thread receives &ctl (parent PID) and compares *arg with getpid() after sem_wait. The parent later reuses the same variable: ctl = waitpid(child, …) (child PID). The child sleeps 1s before exiting, so if the parent’s thread is delayed by more than ~1s after sem_post (heavily loaded system), it reads the child’s PID and calls FAILED(“The thread is executing in the child process”) in the parent - a false failure.
  • Evidence: fork/21-1.c:62-63 (comparison), :76/:87 (ctl = getpid(); pthread_create(…, &ctl)), :116 (ctl = waitpid(…)).
  • Suggested action: pass a separate, never-modified variable holding the parent PID to the thread (or join the thread before reusing ctl).
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN,REPEAT,STRESS,VIRT,MUTATION. Not reproduced naturally: 19/19 PASS (HPE 1+5+5 stress, VIRT 3+5 stress). Mutation sleep(2) in thread after sem_wait (thread runs after parent’s ctl = waitpid()) -> 3/3 ‘FAILED: The thread is executing in the child process’ in the parent: mechanism real, needs >1 s thread delay

testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/interfaces/kill/1-2.c (openposix: conformance/interfaces/kill/1-2)

  • Category: FRAGILE
  • Confidence: medium
  • Claim under test: kill() sends the signal to another process.
  • Problem: the parent synchronises with sleep(1) before kill(pid, SIGUSR1). If the child has not yet run sigaction() (loaded system), SIGUSR1 kills it with the default action; WEXITSTATUS() of a signalled status is 0 and the test reports FAIL. The header comment admits the assumption. (The child also calls sigwait() on an unblocked signal, which POSIX leaves undefined; on Linux either path yields exit 1.)
  • Evidence: kill/1-2.c:59-66 (child installs handler after fork), :84-85 (sleep(1); kill), :95 (WEXITSTATUS without WIFEXITED).
  • Suggested action: block SIGUSR1 before fork (child then sigwait()s on a blocked signal, no race), or use a pipe to signal readiness.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN,REPEAT,STRESS,VIRT,MUTATION. Not reproduced naturally: 19/19 PASS (HPE 1+5+5 stress, VIRT 3+5 stress on 1 CPU). Mutation removing the parent’s sleep(1) -> 20/20 rc=1 ‘Child did not exit normally. Test FAILED’: sleep(1) is the only handshake; fails whenever the child is >1 s late installing the handler

testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/interfaces/kill/2-2.c (openposix: conformance/interfaces/kill/2-2)

  • Category: FRAGILE
  • Confidence: medium (phase 1: low)
  • Claim under test: error checking is performed for the null signal (ESRCH for nonexistent pid, EPERM for unprivileged target).
  • Problem: ESRCH case assumes PID 999999 can never exist; with kernel.pid_max=4194304 (systemd default on 64-bit) such a PID can be live, giving a false FAIL. EPERM case requires root (setuid(1) failing returns UNRESOLVED, contrary to the comment saying it has no effect for normal users).
  • Evidence: kill/2-2.c:40 (kill(999999, 0)), :58-60.
  • Suggested action: obtain a guaranteed-free PID (fork a child, reap it, use that PID, or read /proc/sys/kernel/pid_max and use a value above it).
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN,CONTAINER,REPEAT,VIRT. HPE: pid_max=4194304. In unshare -pf –mount-proc with ns_last_pid=999998, a sleeper got pid 999999 -> ‘kill() did not fail on ESRCH … At least one test FAILED’ rc=1. As nobody: ‘setuid: Operation not permitted’ rc=2 UNRESOLVED. As-is root PASS (HPE 1, VIRT 3/3)

testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/interfaces/killpg/1-2.c (openposix: conformance/interfaces/killpg/1-2)

  • Category: FRAGILE
  • Confidence: medium
  • Claim under test: killpg() sends the signal to the specified process group.
  • Problem: synchronisation is sleep(1). If the child has not yet installed the handler, SIGUSR1 terminates it and WEXITSTATUS()==0 gives FAIL; if it has not yet called setpgrp(), getpgid(child) returns the parent’s group and the signal goes to the parent’s group (any other members, e.g. a harness sharing the group, receive SIGUSR1 whose default action is termination). Also relies on sigignore()/sigpause(), obsolescent in POSIX.1-2008 and no longer in POSIX.1-2024.
  • Evidence: killpg/1-2.c:40-61 (child setup), :67-75 (sigignore; sleep(1); getpgid; killpg); man sigset(3) STANDARDS: “POSIX.1-2008”, HISTORY: “POSIX.1-2008 marks these functions as obsolete”.
  • Suggested action: have the parent setpgid(child, child) itself, block SIGUSR1 before fork and use sigsuspend/sigwait, and synchronise via a pipe; replace sigignore/sigpause with sigaction/sigsuspend.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN,REPEAT,STRESS,VIRT,MUTATION. Not reproduced naturally: 19/19 PASS (HPE 1+5+5 stress, VIRT 3+5 stress). Mutation removing sleep(1) before getpgid/killpg -> 20/20 rc=1 ‘Child did not exit normally. Test FAILED’: synchronisation is sleep(1) only, as the finding says

testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/interfaces/mlock/12-1.c (openposix: conformance/interfaces/mlock/12-1)

  • Confidence: high
  • Claim under test: mlock() fails with EPERM when the caller lacks privilege (CAP_IPC_LOCK) and RLIMIT_MEMLOCK is 0.
  • Problem: RLIMIT_MEMLOCK is set to 0 only inside set_nonroot(), which runs only when getuid() == 0. Run as a normal user, the test keeps the default RLIMIT_MEMLOCK (8 MiB), mlock(ptr, 8) succeeds, and it returns PTS_FAIL (“You have the right to call mlock”). The comment says the test is meant to run under standard user permissions, so this is a false FAIL in the intended setup. If no non-root passwd entry exists it returns UNTESTED, which is fine.
  • Evidence: mlock/12-1.c:54-57 (setrlimit only in set_nonroot), :80-85, :98-100; kernel mm/mlock.c:40-47 can_do_mlock() returns true when rlimit(RLIMIT_MEMLOCK) != 0; include/uapi/linux/resource.h:79 MLOCK_LIMIT (810241024).
  • Suggested action: always call setrlimit(RLIMIT_MEMLOCK, {0,0}) before mlock(), whatever the uid (and return UNTESTED if the process still has CAP_IPC_LOCK).
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN,REPEAT. HPE root: PASS 6/6 (‘Testing with user bin’); as non-root (setpriv –reuid=65534, RLIMIT_MEMLOCK 8192 KiB inherited) -> rc=1 ‘You have the right to call mlock’ (false FAIL in the setup the comment says is intended). VIRT 3/3 PASS as root

testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/interfaces/mmap/11-4.c (openposix: conformance/interfaces/mmap/11-4)

  • Category: FRAGILE
  • Confidence: high (phase 1: medium)
  • Claim under test: modifications to the partial page past EOF are never written out; a later mapping must not see them.
  • Problem: the child writes past EOF in the last page, calls msync and exits; the parent remaps and FAILs if it sees the byte. Linux documents that such data stays in the page cache and later mappings may see it, and that msync() only helps where writeback zeroes the tail. The test skips only when statfs(tmpdir).f_type is TMPFS_MAGIC. On ramfs (no writeback), or on overlayfs whose upper layer is tmpfs (f_type is overlay, the real inode is tmpfs), the post-EOF byte persists and the test reports a false FAIL. It passes on ext4/xfs/overlay-over-xfs (verified locally on overlay).
  • Evidence: mmap/11-4.c:78-81 (tmpfs-only skip), :115-116, :147-150; man mmap(2) BUGS: “On Linux, when you write data to such partial page after the end of the object, the data stays in the page cache even after the file is closed and unmapped … In some cases, this could be fixed by calling msync(2) before the unmap takes place; however, this doesn’t work on tmpfs(5)”.
  • Suggested action: read back with read()/pread() (as 11-6 does) instead of remapping, or detect filesystems without writeback (ramfs, overlay over tmpfs) and return UNTESTED.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN,REPEAT,STRESS,VIRT. HPE TMPDIR=ramfs mount: 2/2 rc=1 ‘Test FAILED: Modification of the partial page at the end of an object is written out’; TMPDIR=tmpfs: rc=5 skip; btrfs: PASS 6/6, VIRT 3/3. False FAIL reproduced on ramfs (only TMPFS_MAGIC is skipped)
  • Verification (phase 3, glibc vs musl build and libc sources): UNCHANGED via MUSL,BULK,RUN. HPE glibc: PASS; musl: UNTESTED ‘From mmap(2) manpage, skip known bug on tmpfs’. Rerun via wrappers (TMPDIR=/var/tmp/ltp, btrfs): glibc PASS, musl PASS. The bulk musl run used a tmpfs tmpdir, which hits the TMPFS_MAGIC skip (11-4.c:78-81). Run artefact; libc plays no role (msync/page cache are kernel)

testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/interfaces/mmap/24-1.c (openposix: conformance/interfaces/mmap/24-1)

  • Category: FRAGILE
  • Confidence: high (phase 1: medium)

The PASS path returns at line 108 without restoring, leaving a system-wide tunable lowered (Fedora, for example, ships 1048576). That can break later tests or workloads on the same machine.

testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/interfaces/mmap/5-1.c (openposix: conformance/interfaces/mmap/5-1)

  • Category: FRAGILE
  • Confidence: high (phase 1: medium)

When the tmpdir is mounted noexec (common hardening for /tmp), Linux returns EPERM for any PROT_EXEC file mapping, and the test FAILs. EPERM is the documented Linux behaviour. SELinux execmod/execmem policies can likewise return EACCES.
  • Evidence: mmap/5-1.c:46-59 (PROT_EXEC cases), :116-119 (only ENOTSUP tolerated); kernel mm/mmap.c:479-481 (path_noexec && VM_EXEC -> -EPERM); man mmap(2) ERRORS: “EPERM The prot argument asks for PROT_EXEC but the mapped area belongs to a file on a filesystem that was mounted no-exec.”
  • Suggested action: tolerate EPERM/EACCES for PROT_EXEC cases (or check statvfs ST_NOEXEC and skip them).
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN. HPE: as-is PASS (TMPDIR=/var/tmp/ltp). TMPDIR on tmpfs mounted noexec -> rc=1, 8 lines ‘Combination of PROT_EXEC … with MAP_SHARED/MAP_PRIVATE has failed: Operation not permitted’; same tmpfs remounted exec -> rc=0 Test PASSED. Correct EPERM is reported as FAIL.

testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/interfaces/mq_notify/5-1.c (runtest: openposix: conformance/interfaces/mq_notify/5-1)

  • Category: FRAGILE
  • Confidence: medium (phase 1: high)
  • Claim under test: When a process is registered for notification and another thread/process is blocked in mq_receive, the arriving message goes to the receiver and no notification is sent.
  • Problem: The parent sleeps 2 s and assumes the child is then blocked in mq_receive. If the child has not reached mq_receive yet (loaded system), the send moves the queue from empty to non-empty with no waiter, the notification is sent correctly, and the test reports FAIL on a correct kernel. The header comment admits the race. Also attr.mq_maxmsg = 40 is above the default msg_max (10), so without CAP_SYS_RESOURCE mq_open fails with EINVAL and the test is UNRESOLVED. In that path mqclean() is also called on (mqd_t)-1.
  • Evidence: 5-1.c:95 sleep(2); /* assume that child with block on mq_receive */; ipc/mqueue.c:356 msg_max check; mq_overview(7) msg_max default 10.
  • Suggested action: Check that the child is blocked (poll /proc//stat for state S / wchan, or similar) before registering and sending. Use mq_maxmsg <= 10.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): REVISED via RUN,REPEAT,STRESS,VIRT,MUTATION. Race not reproduced: as-is 23/23 PASS (HPE 5+5 stress; VIRT 1-CPU 5+5 stress+3 stress+SCHED_IDLE). Mutant child sleep(3) before mq_receive -> rc=1 Test FAILED (consequence real). As nobody: rc=2 ‘mq_open: Invalid argument’ UNRESOLVED (maxmsg 40 > msg_max 10). 2 s window after fork is wide; lowered one step.
  • Verification conclusion: Both mechanisms are real: a late child turns a correct notification into FAIL, and unprivileged runs are UNRESOLVED because of mq_maxmsg=40. But the child only has to call mq_receive within 2 s of fork(), and that never slipped even at SCHED_IDLE under full load on 1 CPU. Keep as FRAGILE, medium.

testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/interfaces/mq_open/2-1.c (runtest: openposix: conformance/interfaces/mq_open/2-1)

  • Category: FRAGILE
  • Confidence: low (phase 1: medium)
  • Claim under test: A name starting with “/” refers to the same queue in another process.
  • Problem: The handshake is sleep(1); kill(pid, SIGUSR1) in the parent, while the child must first install a handler and block SIGUSR1 before sigwait(). If the child has not run sigaction() yet, SIGUSR1 kills it and the test reports FAIL. If it has the handler but has not blocked the signal, the handler consumes it and sigwait() blocks until the harness timeout. Also attr.mq_maxmsg = 40 > default msg_max 10, so without CAP_SYS_RESOURCE the result is UNRESOLVED.
  • Evidence: 2-1.c:67-75 (child sets up signal mask after fork); 2-1.c:128-129 sleep(1); kill(pid, SIGUSR1);
  • Suggested action: Block SIGUSR1 in the parent before fork() (the mask is inherited), or use a pipe for synchronisation. Use mq_maxmsg <= 10.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): REVISED via RUN,REPEAT,STRESS,VIRT,MUTATION. Race not reproduced: as-is 23/23 PASS (HPE 5+5 stress; VIRT 1-CPU 5+5 stress+3 stress+SCHED_IDLE). Mutants of 2-1 (7-2/8-2/9-2: identical handshake): child 1.5 s late before sigaction -> rc=1 FAIL; late between sigaction and sigprocmask -> hang rc=124. As nobody: rc=2 ‘mq_open() did not return success: Invalid argument’ UNRESOLVED.
  • Verification conclusion: Both failure modes are real (FAIL and hang), but the child only needs a few syscalls within 1 s of fork(), and that never slipped in 23 loaded runs. Lowered to low. The maxmsg=40 issue gives UNRESOLVED for unprivileged runs, as phase 1 said. The fix (block SIGUSR1 before fork) is still right.

testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/interfaces/mq_receive/1-1.c (runtest: openposix: conformance/interfaces/mq_receive/1-1)

  • Category: FRAGILE (secondary: WRONG)
  • Confidence: high (phase 1: medium)
  • Claim under test: mq_receive returns the oldest highest-priority message and stores its priority.
  • Problem: mq_open() is called with attr.mq_maxmsg = 40. Without CAP_SYS_RESOURCE (non-root run, rootless container), or if fs.mqueue.msg_max is lowered, Linux rejects maxmsg > msg_max (default 10) with EINVAL. The test only sets unresolved = 1 and keeps going with mqdes == (mqd_t)-1. The call under test then fails with EBADF, which sets failure = 1, and failure is reported before unresolved, so a correct kernel gets FAIL instead of UNRESOLVED.
  • Evidence: testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/interfaces/mq_receive/1-1.c:45-62; ipc/mqueue.c:351-358 (maxmsg > ipc_ns->mq_msg_max -> -EINVAL unless capable(CAP_SYS_RESOURCE)); mq_open(3) ERRORS: “In a process that is unprivileged … attr->mq_maxmsg must be less than or equal to the msg_max limit”.
  • Suggested action: Return PTS_UNRESOLVED right after a failed mq_open, and use mq_maxmsg <= 10 (the assertion does not need 40 slots).
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN. HPE: as root rc=0 PASS. As nobody (setpriv –reuid=nobody –inh-caps=-all; msg_max=10, no CAP_SYS_RESOURCE): mq_open EINVAL, test continues on mqd -1 -> rc=1 ‘FAIL: mq_receive didn’t receive the correct message / FAIL: receive priority 63 != send priority 1 / Test FAILED’ (FAIL, not UNRESOLVED) on a correct kernel.
