testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/interfaces/pthread_detach/2-1.c (openposix: conformance/interfaces/pthread_detach/2-1)

  • Category: WEAK
  • Confidence: high (phase 1: medium)
  • Claim under test: pthread_detach() does not terminate a running thread.
  • Problem: The only check is that pthread_cancel(new_th) does not return ESRCH. Since glibc 2.34, pthread_cancel returns 0 for an already-exited thread (glibc bug 19193), and POSIX does not require ESRCH. So the check could not detect a terminated thread even if detach killed it. pthread_detach/2-2.c tests the same assertion properly (the thread must post a semaphore after detach).
  • Evidence: 2-1.c ret = pthread_cancel(new_th); if (ret == ESRCH) FAIL.
  • Suggested action: drop in favour of 2-2.
  • Verification (phase 3, glibc vs musl build and libc sources): CONFIRMED via MUSL,RUN,SRC. HPE glibc: PASS; musl: PASS. If detach killed the thread, neither libc returns ESRCH: glibc pthread_cancel.c:62-68 returns 0; musl pthread_kill.c:13-14 returns 0 for tid==0, and a detached exited thread unmaps itself so cancel would crash. Check cannot detect termination on either.

testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/interfaces/pthread_equal/2-1.c (openposix: conformance/interfaces/pthread_equal/2-1)

  • Category: WEAK
  • Confidence: high (phase 1: medium)
  • Claim under test: pthread_equal() does not return EINTR while signals are delivered.
  • Problem: pthread_equal() is a pure comparison that returns “non-zero if equal”, not an error code; signals cannot affect it. The check ret = pthread_equal(me, me); ... if (ret == EINTR) FAILED treats a legitimate non-zero “equal” result that happens to be 4 as a failure. glibc returns 1, so it never trips, but the test validates nothing and spends 1 s on a signal storm.
  • Evidence: 2-1.c test(); POSIX pthread_equal: “The pthread_equal() function shall return a non-zero value if t1 and t2 are equal; otherwise, zero shall be returned.”
  • Suggested action: drop.
  • Verification (phase 3, glibc vs musl build and libc sources): CONFIRMED via MUSL,RUN,REPEAT,SRC. HPE glibc: PASS 3/3 (106M comparisons); musl: PASS 3/3 (40M). Both return a==b (musl pthread_equal.c:6; glibc nptl/pthread_equal.c:24 and inline pthread.h:1345-1348), always 1 here, so the EINTR check cannot trigger on either libc.

testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/interfaces/pthread_exit/6-2.c (openposix: conformance/interfaces/pthread_exit/6-2)

  • Category: WEAK
  • Confidence: high (phase 1: medium)
  • Claim under test: pthread_exit() never returns to its caller.
  • Problem: The only check is FAILED("pthread_exit() returned") placed right after pthread_exit(). glibc declares pthread_exit __attribute__((__noreturn__)), so the compiler drops that code and the test cannot fail. For detached scenarios main only waits for a semaphore posted before pthread_exit, so even thread termination is not observed. The behavior is already exercised by 1-2/2-2/3-2/4-1, where the join value proves the thread exited.
  • Evidence: 6-2.c threaded(); /usr/include/pthread.h extern void pthread_exit (void *__retval) __attribute__ ((__noreturn__));.
  • Suggested action: drop as redundant.
  • Verification (phase 3, glibc vs musl build and libc sources): CONFIRMED via MUSL,RUN,SRC. HPE glibc: PASS; musl: rc=5 UNTESTED ‘min stack size is not a multiple of the page size’ (testfrmw/threads_scenarii.c:217-219; musl PTHREAD_STACK_MIN=2048). musl pthread.h:82 ’_Noreturn void pthread_exit’ like glibc noreturn, so the FAILED line is dead code with both libcs.

  • Confidence: medium
  • Claim under test: init fails with ENOMEM when memory is exhausted.
  • Problem: Both 0 and ENOMEM pass, and glibc’s pthread_mutex_init() allocates nothing, so the test only checks that init does not return some other error. Lines 134-143 apply all four settype calls to pma[0], so pma[1..3] stay default and the “different attributes” coverage is just ERRORCHECK, 3 default attrs and NULL.
  • Evidence: 5-1.c:134-145,213-217.
  • Suggested action: Fix the pma[i] indices. Accept that the test is a smoke check, or drop it.
  • Verification (phase 3, glibc vs musl build and libc sources): CONFIRMED via MUSL,RUN,SRC. HPE glibc: PASS; musl: PASS (all ‘succeeds when memory is full’). Neither libc allocates in mutex_init (musl pthread_mutex_init.c:5-7; glibc nptl/pthread_mutex_init.c:89,151), so ENOMEM is unreachable on both; test is a smoke check. pma[0] index bug unaffected by libc.

testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/interfaces/pthread_mutex_lock/3-1.c (openposix: conformance/interfaces/pthread_mutex_lock/3-1)

  • Category: WEAK
  • Confidence: medium
  • Claim under test: pthread_mutex_lock() never returns EINTR.
  • Problem: Only the worker thread ever locks m[0..4] and count_protect, so pthread_mutex_lock() always takes the uncontended userspace fast path and never sleeps in futex(). There is no blocking point for a signal to interrupt, so the EINTR check can never be exercised. The same goes for unlock/init/destroy.
  • Evidence: 3-1.c:204-247 (all mutexes are local to threaded()); sendsig() only sends signals.
  • Suggested action: Have another thread hold each mutex for a while so the worker blocks in lock while signals arrive (as 5-1.c does).

testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/interfaces/pthread_mutex_unlock/2-1.c (openposix: conformance/interfaces/pthread_mutex_unlock/2-1)

  • Category: WEAK
  • Confidence: high
  • Claim under test: when unlocking with waiters, the scheduling policy decides which thread acquires the mutex.
  • Problem: The NOTES say the case “will only demo the scheduling sequence instead of testing it”. The code is a copy of pthread_mutex_lock/1-1.c (a lost-update counter), with a mismatch reported as UNRESOLVED. Nothing about the scheduling policy is checked.
  • Evidence: 2-1.c:13-15,56-62.
  • Suggested action: Drop it (it duplicates pthread_mutex_lock/1-1), or implement a SCHED_FIFO priority-order check with TCONF/UNSUPPORTED when that is not permitted.

testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/interfaces/pthread_mutex_unlock/5-1.c (openposix: conformance/interfaces/pthread_mutex_unlock/5-1)

  • Category: WEAK (secondary: DOCS)
  • Confidence: medium
  • Claim under test: a non-owner unlock of a RECURSIVE mutex returns an error.
  • Problem: If the non-owner unlock succeeds, which is a conformance violation, the test reports UNRESOLVED instead of FAIL (line 86-89). A non-EPERM error is accepted with only a message, under the comment ‘This is a “may” assertion’. POSIX.1-2024 makes EPERM a “shall fail” for RECURSIVE/ERRORCHECK mutexes when the caller does not own them.
  • Evidence: 5-1.c:85-93; pthread_mutex_lock.html ERRORS for pthread_mutex_unlock(): “shall fail if: [EPERM] The mutex type is PTHREAD_MUTEX_ERRORCHECK or PTHREAD_MUTEX_RECURSIVE … and the current thread does not own the mutex.”
  • Suggested action: Use FAILED() when ret == 0 and require ret == EPERM.

testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/interfaces/pthread_rwlock_unlock/1-1.c (openposix: conformance/interfaces/pthread_rwlock_unlock/1-1)

  • Category: WEAK
  • Confidence: medium
  • Claim under test: unlocking one of several read locks leaves the rwlock read-locked; releasing the last one makes it unlocked.
  • Problem: The child sets thread_state = PASSED_RLOCK2 right before calling pthread_rwlock_wrlock(), and main leaves its poll loop as soon as it sees that value, then immediately unlocks. Nothing verifies that the child actually blocked in wrlock while main still held its read lock, which is the “remains in the read locked state” part of the claim. If the implementation wrongly granted the write lock, main may see state 5 and report UNRESOLVED, or see state 4 and PASS.
  • Evidence: 1-1.c:86-89, 135-158.
  • Suggested action: after seeing PASSED_RLOCK2, sleep/poll and require the state to stay PASSED_RLOCK2 (FAIL if EXITING_THREAD) before unlocking, or use pthread_rwlock_trywrlock() from the child and expect EBUSY.

testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/interfaces/sched_getparam/6-1.c (openposix: conformance/interfaces/sched_getparam/6-1)

  • Category: WEAK
  • Confidence: medium

  • Problem: Linux has no permission check for sched_getparam (only an LSM hook), so the call always succeeds and the test always ends UNTESTED. Its own comment admits this. When started as root it also setuid()s permanently to the first passwd entry.
  • Evidence: /usr/src/linux/kernel/sched/syscalls.c:1025-1050.
  • Suggested action: Drop it, or return UNSUPPORTED on Linux.
  • Verification (phase 3, glibc vs musl build and libc sources): UNCHANGED via MUSL,BULK,RUN,SRC. Test right; no PS gate (suite-wide). Existing WEAK finding not reached.

testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/interfaces/sched_setparam/1-1.c (openposix: conformance/interfaces/sched_setparam/1-1)

  • Category: WEAK (secondary: WRONG)
  • Confidence: high
  • Claim under test: sched_setparam() sets the target’s parameters.
  • Problem: The new priority is chosen from the caller’s policy. Under the default SCHED_OTHER, min == max == 0, so new_priority == old_priority == 0 and the PASS condition param.sched_priority == new_priority holds without any change. In the EINVAL fallback, param.sched_priority == new_priority compares the struct the test just wrote, not a value re-read with sched_getparam, so it is tautological.
  • Evidence: sched_setparam/1-1.c new_priority selection and EINVAL branch.
  • Suggested action: Put the child in SCHED_FIFO/RR first (UNRESOLVED without privilege), choose a different priority, and re-read after every set.
  • Verification (phase 3, glibc vs musl build and libc sources): UNCHANGED via MUSL,BULK,RUN,SRC. HPE glibc: PASS; musl: UNRESOLVED ‘An error occurs when calling sched_getparam(): Function’. representative rerun of sched_getparam/3-1. musl sched/sched_{get,set}{param,scheduler}.c:7 return ENOSYS by design; musl declares no PS option (sysconf.c:41 =-1, no _POSIX_PRIORITY_SCHEDULING). Test right; no PS gate (suite-wide). Existing WEAK finding not reached.

testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/interfaces/sem_post/5-1.c (openposix: conformance/interfaces/sem_post/5-1)

  • Category: WEAK
  • Confidence: high
  • Claim under test: sem_post() can be re-entered after being interrupted by a signal (assertion 5).
  • Problem: The test calls sleep(1), then alarm(1), then sem_post immediately. sem_post never blocks, and SIGALRM arrives about one second later, after sem_post has returned (normally after the process has exited). No interruption or re-entry ever happens, so the test only repeats sem_post/1-1 (value 0 -> 1). The sleep(1) only adds runtime. The header admits it is a “best attempt”.
  • Evidence: testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/interfaces/sem_post/5-1.c:55-63
  • Suggested action: Drop it as a duplicate of 1-1. The behavior cannot really be tested with a non-blocking call.

testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/interfaces/sem_wait/3-1.c (openposix: conformance/interfaces/sem_wait/3-1)

  • Category: WEAK
  • Confidence: medium (phase 1: low)
  • Claim under test: the semaphore stays locked until sem_post executes and returns successfully (assertion 3).
  • Problem: A single thread calls sem_wait and then sem_post, and the test checks that the value is 1. Nothing tries to acquire the semaphore while it is locked, so “remains locked until sem_post” is never observed. It is only a value-arithmetic check, already covered by sem_wait/1-1 and sem_post/1-1. Blocking on a locked semaphore is covered by 13-1.
  • Evidence: testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/interfaces/sem_wait/3-1.c:41-60
  • Suggested action: Add a sem_trywait check (expect EAGAIN) between wait and post, or drop it.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN,MUTATION,VIRT. HPE: TEST PASSED as-is; VIRT mutant with both sem_wait() and sem_post() calls replaced by no-ops (‘if (0)’): TEST PASSED rc=0 -> the test only sees the final value 1 and never observes the semaphore being locked between wait and post; add sem_trywait()==EAGAIN in between, or drop

  • Problem: Commit d3df7e05e9f7 (“Replace SIGPOLL with SIGUSR2 wherever possible”) was meant to replace SIGPOLL only (the -19 files). The same commit touched 9 other sigaction “-2.c” files, which are worth checking for the same mistake.
  • Evidence: testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/interfaces/sigaction/1-2.c:40,46 (SIGUSR2); testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/interfaces/sigaction/1-18.c:40,46; git show d3df7e05e9f7
  • Suggested action: Restore SIGALRM in 1-2.c (and audit the other N-2.c files changed by d3df7e05).

testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/interfaces/sigaction/11-1.c (openposix: conformance/interfaces/sigaction/11-1)

  • Category: WEAK
  • Confidence: high
  • Claim under test: assertion #11, SIGCHLD with CLD_CONTINUED when a stopped child is continued.
  • Problem: Both branches print “Test PASSED” and return PTS_PASS (lines 106-127), so the test can never fail; it only logs whether the optional behaviour exists. Uses 1 s select() sleeps for sync. The handler message says “Child has been stopped” for CLD_CONTINUED.
  • Evidence: 11-1.c:106-127; POSIX sigaction SA_NOCLDSTOP: continue notification is “may”.
  • Suggested action: Drop, or return PTS_UNSUPPORTED/PTS_UNTESTED when CLD_CONTINUED is not seen (behaviour is XSI-optional), and PTS_PASS only when it is.

testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/interfaces/sigaction/25-1.c (runtest: openposix: conformance/interfaces/sigaction/25-1)

  • Category: WEAK (secondary: WRONG, DOCS)
  • Confidence: medium
  • Claim under test: assertion 25: the mask on handler entry is the union of the current mask and sa_mask plus the delivered signal (SIGABRT); header says “sa_sigaction signal-catching function”.
  • Problem: sa_mask is empty and nothing else is blocked, so the only thing checked is that SIGABRT itself is blocked inside its handler (re-raise does not re-enter). That is exactly assertion 23 (SA_NODEFER clear), already covered more strictly by 23-1.c, which also verifies the re-raised signal is pending. The union with sa_mask/current mask is never exercised. The parent also tests !WEXITSTATUS(s) without WIFEXITED, so a child terminated by a signal (status low byte != 0, exit byte 0) is reported PASS, and the child’s PTS_UNRESOLVED (2) is reported as FAIL. The header claims sa_sigaction but the code uses sa_handler without SA_SIGINFO.
  • Evidence: testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/interfaces/sigaction/25-1.c:67-69 (sa_handler, sa_flags=0, empty sa_mask), :96 (WEXITSTATUS without WIFEXITED); wait(2): “WEXITSTATUS … should be employed only if WIFEXITED returned true”; POSIX sigaction: “the new signal mask … shall be calculated as the union of the current signal mask and the value of the sa_mask for the signal being delivered”
  • Suggested action: rework into a real assertion-25 test (put another signal in sa_mask and/or pre-block one, then check sigprocmask(0) inside the handler contains both plus SIGABRT), check WIFEXITED in the parent; otherwise drop as duplicate of 23-1.

testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/interfaces/timer_create/speculative/15-1.c (openposix: conformance/interfaces/timer_create/speculative/15-1)

  • Category: WEAK
  • Confidence: high
  • Claim under test: timer_create() fails with EAGAIN when the per-process timer limit or signal queueing resources are exhausted (a POSIX “shall fail”).
  • Problem: everything is under #ifdef TIMER_MAX, and the #else branch returns PTS_PASS. glibc (and musl) do not define TIMER_MAX: /usr/include only has _POSIX_TIMER_MAX and _SC_TIMER_MAX. On Linux the test therefore always reports PASS without creating a single timer. On Linux the limit is enforced via RLIMIT_SIGPENDING (preallocated sigqueue per SIGEV_SIGNAL timer), which the test could use.
  • Evidence: timer_create/speculative/15-1.c:26,52-54; grep -rn TIMER_MAX /usr/include (no TIMER_MAX); POSIX timer_create ERRORS “shall fail if: [EAGAIN] …”.
  • Suggested action: return PTS_UNSUPPORTED/UNTESTED in the #else branch, or lower RLIMIT_SIGPENDING and loop until EAGAIN.
  • Verification (phase 3, glibc vs musl build and libc sources): CONFIRMED via MUSL,RUN,SRC. HPE glibc: rc=0 PASS with no output; musl: rc=0 PASS with no output (#else branch). TIMER_MAX defined in neither: musl include/limits.h has only _POSIX_TIMER_MAX:145 and _SC_TIMER_MAX (unistd.h:322); glibc only _SC_TIMER_MAX (bits/confname.h:144). Both libcs report PASS without creating a timer

testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/interfaces/timer_getoverrun/2-2.c (runtest: openposix: conformance/interfaces/timer_getoverrun/2-2)

  • Category: WEAK
  • Confidence: medium
  • Claim under test: overrun count equals the number of extra expirations (EXPECTEDOVERRUNS=75) with nanosecond interval.

Commit a7f5bda336ba that introduced the clock_getres interval itself notes the test “becomes very similar to the test 2-3”, which does a proper range check.
  • Evidence: 2-2.c:79-82,89,102; git show a7f5bda336ba.
  • Suggested action: drop as duplicate of 2-3, or use a fixed interval (e.g. 1ms rounded up to resolution) and check a two-sided range.

testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/interfaces/timer_settime/2-1.c (runtest: openposix: conformance/interfaces/timer_settime/2-1)

  • Category: WEAK
  • Confidence: medium
  • Claim under test: timer_settime() on an already armed timer resets time-to-expiry to the new it_value.
  • Problem: In every repetition it_interval = it_value + 3 and both grow by 2, so after sigwait the still-armed periodic timer’s remaining time equals new_value + 1s. ACCEPTABLEDELTA is 1s (and elapsed is truncated to whole seconds), so an implementation that ignores the new it_value and keeps the previous reload (or applies new settings only at the next reload) yields delta == 1 and still passes in every iteration. The test only catches an implementation that ignores the call completely (fails at i=2).
  • Evidence: 2-1.c:29-32,71-74,113-128.
  • Suggested action: use an interval much larger than value + tolerance (e.g. interval 30s, values 2..10s) and measure with nanosecond precision.

testcases/realtime/func/pi-tests/sbrk_mutex.c (runtest: realtime profiles/default func/pi-tests sbrk_mutex)

testcases/realtime/func/pi-tests/testpi-1.c (runtest: realtime profiles/default func/pi-tests testpi-1 + parse-testpi1.py)

  • Category: WEAK (secondary: FRAGILE)
  • Confidence: medium
  • Claim under test: a SCHED_OTHER thread holding a PI mutex wanted by RR20/30/40 threads is boosted and preempts the RR40 noise thread.
  • Problem: The verdict comes from parse-testpi1.py: PASS if some “pthread pol 0 pri 0” (SCHED_OTHER loop) line follows a Noise-thread line whose loop count is < 9900. Even without PI the SCHED_OTHER holder gets CPU time on CPU 0 through RT throttling / the fair deadline server (about 5% of each second during the 10s noise run), so it prints its loop-0 line between noise lines and the check passes; it does not distinguish PI from no PI. The binary always exits 0 and run_auto.sh discards the parser’s status (sys.exit(str) exits 1 for both outcomes). All threads are hard-pinned to CPU 0.
  • Evidence: testpi-1.c:95-106, :139-165, :175-208; pi-tests/parse-testpi1.py eval()/main(); pi-tests/run_auto.sh.
  • Suggested action: Compare progress of the SCHED_OTHER holder vs noise quantitatively (e.g. holder must finish before the noise thread), run the nopi variant as a negative control, and use the result in the exit status.

testcases/realtime/func/pi-tests/testpi-4.c (runtest: realtime profiles/default func/pi-tests testpi-4 + parse-testpi1.py)

testcases/realtime/func/pi_perf/pi_perf.c (runtest: realtime profiles/default func/pi_perf “pi_perf -c 200”)

  • Category: WEAK (secondary: DOCS)
  • Confidence: medium
  • Claim under test: with a PI mutex, the high-priority thread’s wait for a lock held by a low-priority thread (with NCPU medium FIFO35 busy threads) is bounded by the low thread’s hold time.
  • Problem: The only checked value is high_get_lock = high_end - low_unlock, i.e. the delay from the low thread’s unlock to the high thread’s acquisition. That is a futex hand-off/wakeup latency and is independent of priority inheritance: without PI (run with -p0) the low FIFO30 holder is simply starved by the FIFO35 busy threads and holds the lock longer, but the unlock->acquire delay stays small and the test still prints PASS. The low hold time (low_dat) that would expose missing boosting is collected but never checked. The “Criteria: High prio lock wait time < (Low prio lock held time + %d us)” text does not match the code, which compares max_pi_delay against pass_criteria (200us) only. Minor: the global stats_record_t rec is written concurrently by the low and high threads.
  • Evidence: pi_perf.c:150-155 (low_hold measured, only stored in low_dat), :188-191 (high_get_lock = high_end - low_unlock), :271-276 (criterion compares max delay to 200us); :81,157-158,196-197 (shared global rec).
  • Suggested action: Check that max(high wait from lock attempt) <= low_work_time + threshold (measure from high_start), or assert low_hold stays close to low_work_time; fix the Criteria text.

testcases/realtime/func/sched_jitter/sched_jitter.c (runtest: realtime profiles/default func/sched_jitter)

  • Category: WEAK (secondary: DOCS)
  • Confidence: medium
  • Claim under test: measure the scheduler overhead of a higher-priority thread repeatedly preempting a worker.
  • Problem: No pass/fail criterion and always exit 0 (profile lists it under “no pass/fail criterium”). The FIFO80 interrupter and FIFO10 worker are not pinned, so on any SMP machine they run on different CPUs and the worker is never preempted by the interrupter; the measured jitter has nothing to do with the claimed switch overhead.
  • Evidence: sched_jitter.c:28-30 (claim), :157-162 (interrupter), :172-180 (no affinity, return 0).
  • Suggested action: Pin both threads to one CPU and add a criterion, or move to a benchmarks area / drop.

testcases/realtime/perf/latency/pthread_cond_many.c (runtest: realtime perf/latency/run_auto.sh)

  • Category: WEAK (secondary: WRONG)

Spinlock “may fail” tests that always PASS and exercise undefined behavior

  • Category: WEAK (secondary: UNDEF)
  • Confidence: high
  • Files:
    • testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/interfaces/pthread_spin_destroy/3-1.c: destroys a lock held by another thread
    • testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/interfaces/pthread_spin_init/2-2.c: uses a PTHREAD_PROCESS_PRIVATE lock from a forked process
    • testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/interfaces/pthread_spin_init/4-1.c: re-initializes an initialized, held lock
    • testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/interfaces/pthread_spin_lock/3-1.c: relocks a lock the caller already holds (escapes via SIGALRM + pthread_exit)
    • testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/interfaces/pthread_spin_lock/3-2.c: locks an uninitialized stack spinlock
    • testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/interfaces/pthread_spin_trylock/4-1.c: trylocks an uninitialized stack spinlock
  • Problem: Each test returns PTS_PASS whatever the result, as their own headers say (“This case will always pass”). In POSIX.1-2024 every one of these scenarios is undefined: “The results are undefined if pthread_spin_destroy() is called when a thread holds the lock”, “…if pthread_spin_init() is called specifying an already initialized spin lock”, “…if the calling thread holds the lock at the time the call is made”, “…if any of these functions is called with an uninitialized spin lock”, and for PRIVATE locks “If threads of differing processes attempt to operate on such a spin lock, the behavior is undefined”. EBUSY/EINVAL/EDEADLK now appear only as RATIONALE recommendations; Issue 7 removed them from ERRORS. The tests verify nothing and can hang or crash on a strict implementation (3-2 relies on alarm()).
  • Evidence: https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9799919799/functions/pthread_spin_destroy.html and …/pthread_spin_lock.html (DESCRIPTION, ERRORS, RATIONALE).
  • Suggested action: Drop the tests.

sched_get_priority_{max,min} 1-1 / 1-2 / 1-4

  • Category: WEAK (secondary: UNDEF)
  • Confidence: medium
  • Files: testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/interfaces/sched_get_priority_max/1-1.c, 1-2.c, 1-4.c; testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/interfaces/sched_get_priority_min/1-1.c, 1-2.c, 1-4.c
  • Claim under test: The function returns the maximum/minimum priority value for SCHED_RR / SCHED_FIFO / SCHED_OTHER.
  • Problem: The tests pass when result != -1 && errno == 0. The value is never checked (POSIX requires at least 32 distinct priorities for FIFO/RR, and max >= min), so they amount to “the call did not fail”. Requiring errno == 0 after a successful call depends on unspecified behavior: POSIX errno says “The setting of errno after a successful call to a function is unspecified unless the description of that function specifies that errno shall not be modified.” testcases/kernel/syscalls/sched_get_priority_{max,min}01.c check the exact Linux values.
  • Evidence: e.g. sched_get_priority_max/1-1.c test_main.
  • Suggested action: Check that max - min >= 31 for FIFO/RR and max >= min generally, and drop the errno == 0 condition.

testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/definitions/time_h/7-{1..5}-buildonly.c, signal_h/5-1-buildonly.c

  • Category: WEAK
  • Confidence: low
  • Claim under test: <time.h> defines clock_t/size_t/time_t/clockid_t/timer_t (time_h 7-x) and <signal.h> defines pid_t (signal_h 5-1) “as described in <sys/types.h>”.
  • Problem: The tests include only <sys/types.h>, so they verify <sys/types.h> rather than the header under test; the assertion.xml paraphrase misread “as described in <sys/types.h>”. The real requirement (the type is visible after including only <time.h>/<signal.h>) is never checked. Minor; no false results.
  • Evidence: time_h/7-1..7-5 and signal_h/5-1 (#include <sys/types.h> only); time.h.html: “The <time.h> header shall define the clock_t, size_t, time_t, types as described in <sys/types.h>.”
  • Suggested action: include <time.h> / <signal.h> instead of <sys/types.h>.

testcases/open_posix_testsuite/functional/semaphores/{sem_conpro,sem_philosopher,sem_readerwriter,sem_sleepingbarber}.c (openposix: functional/semaphores/*)

  • Category: WEAK (secondary: WRONG)
  • Confidence: high
  • Claim under test: classic synchronization problems (producer/consumer, dining philosophers, readers/writers, sleeping barber) work with POSIX semaphores.
  • Problem: These are demos, not tests. Nothing about correctness is checked (consumed data vs produced, two neighbours never eating at once, no reader during a write, etc.); thread failure paths call pthread_exit((void *)1) but main joins with NULL and always returns PTS_PASS. The only way to fail is a hang (timeout). sem_philosopher sleeps ~40 s (20 loops x 2 sleep(1)); sem_sleepingbarber leaves the barber thread blocked forever in sem_wait (30 loops for at most 10 customers) and returns without joining it.
  • Evidence: e.g. sem_conpro.c test_main pthread_join(con, NULL); pthread_join(pro, NULL); ... return PTS_PASS;; sem_philosopher.c philosopher(): sleep(1) twice per LOOP_NUM=20 iteration.
  • Suggested action: add invariant checks (e.g. sequence numbers on consumed data, counters of concurrent readers/writers/eaters asserted under the lock) and propagate thread status, or drop.

OBSOLETE: Targets removed, dead or permanently disabled functionality

The feature, interface, /proc or /sys file, driver or kernel version the test targets no longer exists, or the test is not built or never runs. In the open_posix_testsuite this also covers interfaces that POSIX.1-2024 removed (sighold, sigignore, sigpause, sigrelse, sigset, SIGPOLL, asctime_r, ctime_r, ucontext.h); those tests are still valid against Issue 7, so keeping them is a policy decision. Action: drop.

testcases/commands/tpm-tools/tpmtoken/tpmtoken_import/tpmtoken_import_tests.sh (runtest: tpm_tools/tpmtoken03)

  • Category: OBSOLETE (secondary: WRONG, FRAGILE)
  • Confidence: high (phase 1: medium)
  • Claim under test: tpmtoken_import imports cert/key/combined PEM objects into the TPM PKCS#11 token; wrong-type imports fail.
  • Problem: In addition to the suite-wide issues above, setup runs openssl req ... -sha1 -batch -config ... (lines 78-80) without || RC=$?, so the following if [ $RC -ne 0 ] (line 81) can never trigger; if certificate generation fails (e.g. SHA-1 signatures rejected by a crypto policy), the tests run against missing files and report TFAIL against tpmtoken_import instead of TBROK. Test09/10 “expected failure” cases would then pass trivially because the input files do not exist.
  • Evidence: testcases/commands/tpm-tools/tpmtoken/tpmtoken_import/tpmtoken_import_tests.sh:78-86, :249-278
  • Suggested action: drop with the suite; if kept, capture openssl’s exit status and TBROK on failure.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): REVISED via RUN,CONTAINER,READ,GIT. As-is HPE: TBROK (tool absent). Container w/ tools: openssl fails (cnf never installed, $LTPBIN never set), unchecked RC at :81 is dead code as claimed, but next cat of missing cert/key -> TBROK in setup, so no TFAIL/trivial PASS; suite cannot run anywhere. OBSOLETE high.
  • Verification conclusion: OBSOLETE confirmed, raised to high. The secondary claim is half right: the if [ $RC -ne 0 ] after openssl (:78-81) is dead code, but the next step, cat of the missing cert/key, fails and TBROKs. Tests do not run against missing files and test09/10 cannot pass trivially. New, stronger point: the openssl config is never installed and $LTPBIN is never set, so this test cannot get past setup on any system, TPM 1.2 or not. Corrected action: remove with the suite. The dead RC check is not worth fixing.

testcases/kernel/device-drivers/tbio/tbio_kernel/ltp_tbio.c (runtest: kernel_misc/tbio)

  • Category: OBSOLETE (secondary: WRONG)
  • Confidence: high
  • Claim under test: block I/O layer API (bio_alloc/clone/add_page/split/get_nr_vecs, request submission) through a test block device “tbio”.
  • Problem: the module cannot be compiled against any kernel LTP supports (minimum 4.4). It uses bio->bi_sector (moved into bi_iter in v3.14), blk_make_request(), bio_map_user()/bio_unmap_user(), bio_get_nr_vecs(), bio_clone(), struct bio_pair/bio_pair_release, rq->cmd, blk_init_queue()/blk_fetch_request() (legacy request path, removed in 5.0), alloc_disk() (removed in 5.15), BIO_MAX_PAGES, req->rq_disk, and the media_changed and revalidate_disk fops. None of these exist in /usr/src/linux. module.mk deliberately ignores module build failures (-$(MAKE)), so the user test tbio (runtest kernel_misc:9) silently TCONFs on every system. The code also has its own bugs: test_bio_split() dereferences bio_pairp (NULL when data_len == 0 or bio_map_user fails), tbio_io() ignores send_request()’s result so DO_IO always “passes”, and buf is kmalloc’d and leaked.
  • Evidence: ltp_tbio.c:84,105,152,189,291,342,370,469,513-514,535,541; grep -rw blk_make_request|bio_map_user| bio_get_nr_vecs|blk_init_queue|alloc_disk include/linux block in /usr/src/linux returns nothing; include/mk/module.mk:55-70.
  • Suggested action: drop tbio (kernel module, tbio_user and the runtest entry), or rewrite it from scratch against the blk-mq API if the coverage is wanted.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via BUILD. VIRT 7.2.10 with kernel-devel, WITH_MODULES=yes: ltp_tbio.c fails to compile (implicit blk_make_request, bio_map_user, blk_execute_rq, blk_put_request; struct bio has no bi_sector; request_queue has no bounce_gfp). Log: verify/v00-data/modules-virt-7.2.10.txt

testcases/kernel/fs/doio/datapid.c (runtest: none directly; helper linked into growfiles/doio/iogen)

  • Category: OBSOLETE (secondary: WRONG)

Every caller in growfiles.c treats ret >= 0 as “data mismatch at that offset”, so any growfiles run with -q p or -q o reports a corruption at offset 0 on a correct kernel. None of the current runtest entries pass -q p/-q o (the Linux default is PATTERN_ASCII, growfiles.c:219-223), so nothing fails today. The code is dead Cray support that can still be selected and will then give false FAILs.
  • Evidence: datapid.c:86-175 (#if CRAY … #else return -1;), datapid.c:181-294 (#else ... sprintf(Errmsg, "Not supported on this OS."); return 0;); growfiles.c:701-705 (-q p/-q o accepted), growfiles.c:2166-2169 (gen, return ignored), growfiles.c:2644-2648 + if (ret >= 0) error path, also 2794-2800 and 2883-2888; grep growfiles runtest/* shows no -q usage.
  • Suggested action: Drop datapid.c, and drop PATTERN_PID/PATTERN_OFFSET (-q p/-q o) from growfiles, or reject them with a clear “unsupported” error.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via BUILD. built: yes (datapid.o linked into growfiles, doio/Makefile:36); growfiles is in runtest (fs:gf01..), but default Pattern is PATTERN_ASCII on non-CRAY (growfiles.c:219-223) and no runtest/script passes growfiles -q p or -q o, so datapidgen/chk never run

testcases/kernel/syscalls/fcntl/fcntl16.c (runtest: syscalls/fcntl16, fcntl16_64)

  • Category: OBSOLETE (secondary: WEAK, FRAGILE)
  • Confidence: high
  • Claim under test: Processes blocked in F_SETLKW are woken correctly when the holder changes lock boundaries, on files “without mandatory locking”, “with mandatory locking” and “mandatory locking with NOBLOCK”.
  • Problem: (1) Blocks 2 and 3 create the file with S_ISGID and no group-exec to “enable mandatory locking”. The tmpdir is never mounted with -o mand, and Linux >= 5.15 removed mandatory locking, so these blocks just repeat block 1, adding about 100s of alarm timeouts. (2) Each child sends SIGUSR1/SIGUSR2 to the parent before it calls F_SETLKW (dochild() lines 302-320). The parent then immediately sets parent_c, so in NOBLOCK cases the child often requests the lock after the boundary change and never waits. The “notification on lock change” path is not reliably exercised. (3) WILLBLOCK detection relies on a 10s alarm(); the test is slow (about 150s) and cannot distinguish “still blocked” from “child not yet scheduled”.
  • Evidence: fcntl16.c:302-320 (signal before F_SETLKW), 506-511, 559-581 (alarm-based detection), 662-695 (mandatory-locking blocks); fcntl_locking(2) “This feature is no longer supported at all in Linux 5.15 and above”; fs/namespace.c:2070-2074.
  • Suggested action: drop blocks 2/3. Have each child signal only after it is known to be blocked (e.g. parent polls F_GETLK or uses TST_PROCESS_STATE_WAIT for ‘S’), and replace the 10s alarms with a process-state wait.

testcases/kernel/syscalls/ftruncate/ftruncate04.c (runtest: syscalls/ftruncate04, ftruncate04_64)

  • Category: OBSOLETE
  • Confidence: low
  • Claim under test: ftruncate() fails with EAGAIN inside or before a region held by a mandatory record lock.
  • Problem: Mandatory file locking was removed in Linux 5.15. CONFIG_MANDATORY_FILE_LOCKING no longer exists in fs/Kconfig, and MS_MANDLOCK now only triggers warn_mandlock(). The test always TCONFs (needs_kconfigs) on every current kernel. It still has value only on older LTS kernels (e.g. 5.10) that LTP still lists as supported, hence the low confidence.
  • Evidence: ftruncate04.c:153-174; /usr/src/linux/fs/Kconfig (no MANDATORY_FILE_LOCKING); fs/namespace.c:4258-4259 (warn_mandlock()).
  • Suggested action: Drop once LTP’s minimum kernel is >= 5.15. Until then, set .max_kver or similar so the TCONF reason is explicit.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN,READ. HPE 7.2.9: TCONF ‘Aborting due to unsuitable kernel config’ (CONFIG_MANDATORY_FILE_LOCKING=y missing). /usr/src/linux/fs/Kconfig has no MANDATORY_FILE_LOCKING; MS_MANDLOCK -> warn_mandlock() (fs/namespace.c:4260). TST_MIN_KVER is 4.4, so the test is still live for 4.4-5.14; the needs_kconfigs TCONF already names the reason, .max_kver is cosmetic.

testcases/kernel/syscalls/mmap/mmap11.c (runtest: syscalls/mmap11)

  • Category: OBSOLETE (phase 1: WRONG) (secondary: OBSOLETE)
  • Confidence: high (phase 1: medium)
  • Claim under test: munmap() does not fail with ENOMEM because of sysctl_max_map_count when glibc frees thread stacks (2009 ia64 bug, lkml 2009/10/2/85).
  • Problem: With the default loop count of 1, the test creates only two detached threads and then exits at once while one thread still sleeps. It never raises the map count near vm.max_map_count, which the bug needs, and it never checks munmap() results, so it reports TPASS unconditionally. The bug was fixed in 2009 (659ace584e7a “mmap: don’t return ENOMEM when mapcount is temporarily exceeded in munmap()”) and ia64 is no longer in the kernel. It also has a memory bug: thread is sized by STD_LOOP_COUNT, but with -I (duration) the loop count is unbounded and thread[lc] writes past the allocation.
  • Evidence: mmap11.c:105-124 (malloc(STD_LOOP_COUNT*…), TPASS unconditional); 128-137.
  • Suggested action: drop. Or rewrite so it raises the map count to just below vm.max_map_count and asserts that munmap() which splits a VMA succeeds.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): REVISED via BUILD,GIT,READ,RUN,VIRT. [v00: NEW] built/installed: yes (bin/mmap11); runtest refs: none, only “#mmap11 mmap11 -i 30000” commented out in runtest/syscalls since 575048459994 (2011) “syscalls/mmap11: mask broken test” || [v07: CONFIRMED] VIRT: mmap11 ‘TPASS test completed.’ Source l.105-124: loop (default 1 iteration) creates 2 detached threads that malloc/sleep(1), then TPASS unconditionally; no munmap result is checked and map count never approaches vm.max_map_count; thread[] sized STD_LOOP_COUNT but indexed by lc (overflow with -I). Cannot fail; target bug fixed 2009.
  • Verification (phase 3, glibc vs musl build and libc sources): UNCHANGED via MUSL,RUN. HPE glibc: ‘mmap11 1 TPASS : test completed.’; musl: same. Finding (no munmap check, map count never near max, TPASS unconditional) is test logic; libc choice adds nothing

testcases/network/nfsv4/acl/acl1.c (runtest: none; only testcases/network/nfsv4/acl/runtest script)

  • Category: OBSOLETE (secondary: WRONG, UNDEF)
  • Confidence: high
  • Claim under test: setting a POSIX ACL on a file on an NFSv4 mount gives the expected per-user/group access, and default ACLs are inherited.
  • Problem: The program is built but not referenced by any runtest/ file. Its driver script uses rsh to a hardcoded host “nfsserver” and useradd/groupadd. It uses no LTP result API: it only prints counts and always return 1. Functionally it cannot work on NFSv4: acl_set_file() uses the system.posix_acl_* xattrs, and the Linux NFSv4 client has no POSIX ACL inode ops (only nfs4_acl/dacl/sacl xattrs), so it fails with EOPNOTSUPP. It also has C bugs: K&R report(testnum, expected, result, fail) is called with 3 arguments; strcat(dir, "/testfile") writes past the argv[2] string; testgrp4/5 use result uninitialised when seteuid fails; the test_acl_default() fopen leaks.
  • Evidence: acl1.c:104-122, 135, 288-315, 365; fs/nfs/nfs3proc.c:1059-1072 (get_inode_acl/set_acl only for v3); fs/nfs/nfs4proc.c:10843-10854 (nfs4_xattr_handlers: nfs4_acl, dacl, sacl, label, user, no posix_acl); grep of runtest/ finds no acl1.
  • Suggested action: Drop testcases/network/nfsv4/acl (acl1.c and the python scripts), or rewrite it as an NFSv3 POSIX ACL test or an NFSv4 nfs4_acl test using the nfs_lib.sh infrastructure.

The N-host check is therefore vacuous as well as able to hang. Action unchanged: drop.

testcases/network/stress/dccp/dccp_ipsec.sh (runtest: net_stress.ipsec_dccp/dccp4_ipsec01…, dccp6_ipsec…)

  • Category: OBSOLETE
  • Confidence: high (phase 1: medium)
  • Claim under test: DCCP traffic over IPsec (AH/ESP/IPComp, transport/tunnel).
  • Problem: DCCP was removed from the kernel in v6.16 by commit 2a63dd0edf38 (“net: Retire DCCP socket.”); /usr/src/linux has no net/dccp/. netstress’s modprobe dccp_ipv6 fails and the test TCONFs on every current kernel. It remains meaningful only for kernels < 6.16, which LTP still supports, so dropping is a policy decision.
  • Evidence: dccp_ipsec.sh:18 (-T dccp); netstress.c:961-966; kernel git 2a63dd0edf38; ls /usr/src/linux/net/dccp -> absent.
  • Suggested action: keep for now with a note (or a max-kver guard), drop the whole net_stress.ipsec_dccp runtest once LTP’s minimum kernel passes 6.16.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN,READ. HPE 7.2.9: ‘dccp_ipsec.sh -s 100:500:1000:R1000’ -> netstress.c:966 TCONF ‘Failed to load dccp_ipv6 module’, ‘dccp_ipsec 1 TCONF: server failed’. modprobe -n dccp/dccp_ipv6: ‘Module not found’; no CONFIG_IP_DCCP in /boot/config; /usr/src/linux (7.3-rc7) has no net/dccp. Drop timing is policy (LTP min kernel 4.4).

testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/interfaces/sigpause/1-1.c (openposix: conformance/interfaces/sigpause/1-1)

  • Category: OBSOLETE (secondary: FRAGILE)
  • Confidence: medium
  • Claim under test: sigpause(sig) removes sig from the mask, so a held SIGABRT is delivered while suspended.
  • Problem: sigpause was removed in POSIX.1-2024 (see the group note). Synchronisation also relies on sleep(1): if the new thread has not run sigaction() before main’s pthread_kill(), SIGABRT’s default action kills the whole process. The result is checked by a fixed sleep(1) after the kill. handler_called is a plain int.
  • Evidence: sigpause/1-1.c:41-43,56-65; XRAT B.1.1.
  • Suggested action: drop with the sigpause group; if kept, install the handler in main before pthread_create.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN,REPEAT,STRESS,VIRT,MUTATION,READ. As-is PASS; 0 failures in 5 plain + 5 stress runs on HPE and 3 plain + 5 stress runs on VIRT (1 CPU). Mutant delaying the thread’s sigaction() by sleep(2) -> whole process killed by SIGABRT (rc 134, core) on HPE and VIRT, so the secondary FRAGILE race is real but needs a >1 s scheduling delay. glibc 2.43 still provides sigpause; removed in POSIX.1-2024 (XRAT B.1.1).
  • Verification (phase 3, glibc vs musl build and libc sources): CONFIRMED via MUSL,RUN,REPEAT,SRC,READ. HPE ltprepeat 5: glibc pass=5/5, musl pass=5/5 (‘signal was called|Test PASSED’); FRAGILE sleep(1) race not opened by musl. musl src/signal/sigpause.c:6-8, glibc sysdeps/posix/sigpause.c:36-45. Issue 8 XRAT ‘Removed Functions’ lists all 5; both libcs still ship them: glibc 2.43 exports (deprecated attr since 2.32, NEWS:2624), musl exports with no deprecation (include/signal.h:241-246)

testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/interfaces/sigpause/1-2.c (openposix: conformance/interfaces/sigpause/1-2)

  • Category: OBSOLETE (secondary: FRAGILE)
  • Confidence: medium
  • Claim under test: sigpause() suspends the caller until a signal arrives.

Secondary FRAGILE (fixed sleep(1) before final check) not reproduced, consistent with phase-1 ‘practically safe’. glibc 2.43 still provides sigpause; builds with -Wdeprecated-declarations; removed in POSIX.1-2024 (XRAT B.1.1).
  • Verification (phase 3, glibc vs musl build and libc sources): CONFIRMED via MUSL,RUN,REPEAT,SRC,READ. HPE ltprepeat 5: glibc pass=5/5, musl pass=5/5 (11 s each); secondary FRAGILE not reproduced under either libc. Issue 8 XRAT ‘Removed Functions’ lists all 5; both libcs still ship them: glibc 2.43 exports (deprecated attr since 2.32, NEWS:2624), musl exports with no deprecation (include/signal.h:241-246)

testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/interfaces/sigpause/3-1.c (openposix: conformance/interfaces/sigpause/3-1)

  • Category: OBSOLETE (secondary: FRAGILE)
  • Confidence: medium
  • Claim under test: sigpause() returns -1/EINTR after the handler runs.
  • Problem: sigpause was removed in POSIX.1-2024. SIGABRT is not blocked before sigpause, and main only waits sleep(1) before pthread_kill. If the thread has installed the handler but not yet entered sigpause, the signal is consumed early and sigpause blocks forever (HUNG). If it has not installed the handler yet, the process aborts. A sighold() before sigpause (as in 1-1) would close the race.
  • Evidence: sigpause/3-1.c:42-43,76-84; XRAT B.1.1.
  • Suggested action: drop with the group; if kept, sighold() before sigpause and install the handler before pthread_create.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN,REPEAT,STRESS,VIRT,MUTATION,READ. As-is PASS; 0 failures in 5 plain + 5 stress runs on HPE and 3 plain + 5 stress runs on VIRT (1 CPU). Mutant with sleep(2) between sigaction() and sigpause() (signal arrives before sigpause, SIGABRT not held) -> sigpause never returns, killed by timeout (rc 137) on HPE and VIRT = HUNG, as phase 1 says; window needs a >1 s delay. glibc 2.43 still provides sigpause; removed in POSIX.1-2024.
  • Verification (phase 3, glibc vs musl build and libc sources): CONFIRMED via MUSL,RUN,REPEAT,SRC,READ. HPE ltprepeat 5: glibc pass=5/5, musl pass=5/5 (‘returned -1 and set errno to EINTR’); race needs >1 s delay (phase-2 mutant). Issue 8 XRAT ‘Removed Functions’ lists all 5; both libcs still ship them: glibc 2.43 exports (deprecated attr since 2.32, NEWS:2624), musl exports with no deprecation (include/signal.h:241-246)

testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/interfaces/sigpause/4-1.c (openposix: conformance/interfaces/sigpause/4-1)

  • Category: OBSOLETE
  • Confidence: low (phase 1: medium)
  • Claim under test: sigpause(-1) fails with EINVAL.
  • Problem: the logic is fine for Issue 7, but sigpause was removed in POSIX.1-2024. (The #if 0 && defined(__FreeBSD__) || ... operator precedence is off but has no effect on Linux.)
  • Evidence: sigpause/4-1.c:18,31-48; XRAT B.1.1.
  • Suggested action: see the group action.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN,BUILD,READ. HPE: sigpause_4-1: Test PASSED: sigpause returned -1 and set errno to EINVAL (rc 0). glibc 2.43 still exports all five (deprecated attr, only -Wdeprecated warnings); XRAT B.1.1 lists them removed in Issue 8. The ‘#if 0 && … || defined(NetBSD) || …’ precedence slip only affects Net/OpenBSD; none on Linux. Medium: dropping is policy.
  • Verification (phase 3, glibc vs musl build and libc sources): REVISED via MUSL,RUN,SRC,READ. HPE glibc: ‘sigpause returned -1 and set errno to EINVAL’ rc 0; musl: HANGS, killed by 30 s timeout (rc 124). musl bug: src/signal/sigpause.c:7 ignores sigdelset() failure and sigsuspends; glibc sysdeps/posix/sigpause.c:36 returns -1. Issue 7 says ‘shall fail’ EINVAL. Test still finds libc bugs -> soften drop
  • Verification conclusion: This is a musl bug, not a test bug. musl src/signal/sigpause.c:7 ignores the return value of sigdelset(&mask, -1) and calls sigsuspend() on the current mask, so sigpause(-1) blocks forever. glibc sysdeps/posix/sigpause.c:36 returns -1/EINVAL, which is what Issue 7 requires (“shall fail … illegal signal number”). The interface is still removed in POSIX.1-2024, so OBSOLETE stands. However, this test is the only one in the family that finds a real defect in a shipping libc, so the “drop” action is weaker here: lower to low and suggest “keep while libcs ship sigpause, or drop with the family”. The test has no internal alarm and relies on the harness timeout to survive the hang.

testcases/open_posix_testsuite/stress/threads/pthread_cond_timedwait/stress1.c (openposix: stress/threads/pthread_cond_timedwait/stress1)

  • Category: OBSOLETE (secondary: FRAGILE, UNDEF)
  • Confidence: high
  • Claim under test: pthread_cond_timedwait atomically releases the mutex and blocks. Uses ping-pong between thread A and grandchild B (thread or forked process); a 120 s timeout means a lost signal.
  • Problem: Never built: open_posix stress/threads has no Makefile, so nothing under it is compiled. The test only ends on SIGUSR1, so under t0 it is killed and reported HUNG. In the fork scenarios, the child of the multithreaded process calls pthread_mutex_lock/cond_timedwait/printf (the output() mutex). POSIX allows only async-signal-safe calls after fork() in a multithreaded process, so this is UB. The gchild’s exit status is read into ret and ignored (stress1.c:352). The cleanup “destroy the mutex” actually calls pthread_mutex_init(&mtx, &ma) on an initialized mutex with an already destroyed attr object, which is UB (stress1.c:672).
  • Evidence: stress/Makefile; stress1.c:sighdl/test_main; POSIX fork(): “the child process may only execute async-signal-safe operations until such time as one of the exec functions is called”; pthread_mutex_init: “Attempting to initialize an already initialized mutex results in undefined behavior.”
  • Suggested action: Drop together with stress/threads, or wire up a Makefile, add a self-terminating duration, call pthread_mutex_destroy in cleanup and check the gchild exit status.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via BUILD. LTP configure default WITH_OPEN_POSIX_TESTSUITE=no; clean copy + generate-makefiles: no stress/threads/Makefile is generated, so stress/Makefile (*/Makefile only) never descends; make stress-all builds only mqueues+signals (3 tests); no runtest refs; gcc -c -std=c99 compiles OK

testcases/open_posix_testsuite/stress/threads/pthread_kill/stress.c (openposix: not selected; would be stress/threads/pthread_kill/stress)

  • Category: OBSOLETE (secondary: WRONG, FRAGILE)

  • Problem: Never built, and it fails to compile with glibc headers: static int sync; (stress.c:159) redeclares sync(2) from <unistd.h>. The comment “register the signal handler for this one thread” is wrong because sigaction() is process-wide. The handlers for SIGABRT/SIGBUS/SIGILL are installed inside flood_receiver/sync_rec, which race with the already-created flooder_1/flooder_2/sync_send threads. If a sender runs first, the default action of SIGABRT/SIGBUS/SIGILL terminates the whole process. The sync flag is a plain int written from a handler and polled across sleep(), not volatile sig_atomic_t.
  • Evidence: gcc 16: “stress.c:159:12: error: ‘sync’ redeclared as different kind of symbol”; POSIX sigaction(): the action is per-process; pthread_kill(): “the signal shall be delivered to the specified thread” but the action is process-wide.
  • Suggested action: Drop, or rename the flag to volatile sig_atomic_t, install the handlers in main before creating the senders, and build it.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via BUILD. LTP configure default WITH_OPEN_POSIX_TESTSUITE=no; clean copy + generate-makefiles: no stress/threads/Makefile is generated, so stress/Makefile (*/Makefile only) never descends; make stress-all builds only mqueues+signals (3 tests); no runtest refs; gcc -c -std=c99: FAIL stress.c:159 ‘sync’ redeclared
  • Verification (phase 3, glibc vs musl build and libc sources): CONFIRMED via MUSL,BUILD. HPE suite CFLAGS (-std=c99 -D_XOPEN_SOURCE=700): gcc/glibc FAIL stress.c:159 ‘sync’ redeclared; musl-clang FAIL 3 errors: 159 redefinition of ‘sync’, 163/194 ‘non-object type void (void) is not assignable’. Unbuildable under both libcs

testcases/open_posix_testsuite/stress/threads/pthread_mutex_lock/stress.c (openposix: not selected; would be stress/threads/pthread_mutex_lock/stress)

  • Category: OBSOLETE (secondary: WRONG, UNDEF)

All later *loc accesses read and write the byte past the caller’s char loc (stress.c:228/275/332, itself never initialised), which is a stack out-of-bounds access. The *loc = -120 / *loc = 1 assignments write out of bounds. Because the value is garbage and may be 0, c->ctrl = *loc can store 0 and the “two threads own the mutex” check cannot fire. In addition, SIGUSR1 (the stop request) is process-directed. If it lands on a sigthr thread blocked in sem_wait, sem_wait fails with EINTR (the handler is installed with sa_flags = 0, no SA_RESTART) and the test reports UNRESOLVED “Sem wait failed”.
  • Evidence: stress.c:202-218 control(); signal(7): sem_wait(3) is restarted “if the SA_RESTART flag was used; otherwise the call fails with the error EINTR”; gcc -Wall: “value computed is not used”.
  • Suggested action: Drop; if kept, change to (*loc)++, initialise loc, retry sem_wait on EINTR.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via BUILD. LTP configure default WITH_OPEN_POSIX_TESTSUITE=no; clean copy + generate-makefiles: no stress/threads/Makefile is generated, so stress/Makefile (*/Makefile only) never descends; make stress-all builds only mqueues+signals (3 tests); no runtest refs; gcc -c -std=c99 compiles OK

HPE built under both; SIGUSR1 after 10s: glibc ‘PASSED – 7728 iterations’, musl ‘PASSED – 7368 iterations’. ‘Works with glibc’s int-based once only’ is wrong: musl pthread_once_t is int, INIT 0 (alltypes.h.in:58, pthread.h:61, pthread_once.c:19 states 0-3); reset after join works on both. Only formal POSIX UB remains
  • Verification conclusion: OBSOLETE (never built, runs until SIGUSR1) stands. The secondary claim, “works with glibc’s int-based pthread_once_t only”, is wrong. musl’s pthread_once_t is also an int with PTHREAD_ONCE_INIT 0 (include/alltypes.h.in:58, pthread.h:61). Its state machine (0/1/2/3, src/thread/pthread_once.c:19-36) is reset correctly by assignment once all threads are joined, and glibc behaves the same (sysdeps/nptl/bits/pthreadtypes.h:53). Corrected secondary text: “re-arming by assignment is formally undefined in POSIX, but harmless on glibc and musl.” The action (drop) is unchanged.

Grouped entries (OBSOLETE)

sighold / sigignore / sigpause / sigrelse / sigset directories (shared evidence for the OBSOLETE entries below)

POSIX.1-2024 (Issue 8) removed these XSI functions: https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9799919799/xrat/V4_xsh_chap01.html B.1.1 “Removed Functions in Issue 8” lists sighold, sigignore, sigpause, sigrelse and sigset, and https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9799919799/functions/sighold.html returns 404. sigset(3) HISTORY says “POSIX.1-2008 marks these functions as obsolete”; sigpause(3) says “Obsoleted in POSIX.1-2008”. glibc still provides them, marked deprecated. The tests are judged against Issue 7 text, which still applies to them; where a test also has a logic problem, its own section says so. Suggested action for the whole group: decide once whether open_posix keeps Issue 7-only coverage. If it does not, drop these directories (or move them to a “removed interfaces” area that is not run by default).

testcases/commands/tpm-tools/ (whole suite, runtest/tpm_tools: tpm01-tpm07, tpmtoken01-05)

  • Category: OBSOLETE (secondary: FRAGILE)
  • Confidence: medium
  • Claim under test: TrouSerS tpm-tools (tpm_version, tpm_selftest, tpm_getpubek, tpm_takeownership, tpm_restrictpubek, tpm_changeownerauth, tpm_clear) and the opencryptoki PKCS#11 tpmtoken_* tools work against the TPM.
  • Problem: All 12 scripts (plus 28 expect helpers *_exp0N.sh) target TPM 1.2 userspace (tcsd/TrouSerS, tpm-tools), unchanged since 2005-2009 (git log only shows license/address edits). They test userspace tools, not the kernel (only /dev/tpm0 underneath). None detects a TPM or its version: on systems with no TPM or a TPM 2.0 (practically all current hardware) they TBROK (tool missing) or TFAIL (tcsd cannot talk to a TPM 2.0), never TCONF. The runtest order forms one stateful sequence (getpubek needs an un-owned TPM, takeownership takes ownership with fixed passwords, restrictpubek permanently restricts PUBEK, changeauth chains passwords across subtests, tpmtoken_init test01 fails if the token is already initialized, tpm_clear clears ownership which on TPM 1.2 leaves it disabled until reboot), so it can run once on a freshly cleared TPM 1.2 and cannot be re-run. Each expect helper waits a full 30 s expect timeout in the hang case and the pass/fail is only the tool exit code. They use the legacy apicmds (tst_resm/tst_brk binaries) API.
  • Evidence: runtest/tpm_tools; e.g. testcases/commands/tpm-tools/tpm/tpm_getpubek/tpm_getpubek_tests.sh:46-55 (only which check, TBROK); tpm_restrictpubek_tests_exp01.sh:25 (tpm_restrictpubek -r); tpm_clear_tests_exp01.sh:25; tpmtoken_init_tests_exp01.sh:37-55 (fails if store already initialized).
  • Suggested action: drop runtest/tpm_tools and testcases/commands/tpm-tools/ (kernel TPM coverage is better served by IMA/tpm2 based tests); if kept, add TPM 1.2 presence detection with TCONF and document that it is destructive.

testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/definitions/signal_h/17-1-buildonly.c, 18-1-buildonly.c (openposix: conformance/definitions/signal_h/17-1-buildonly, 18-1-buildonly)

  • Claim under test: “ucontext.h shall define ucontext_t” (17) / “… mcontext_t” (18).
  • Problem: <ucontext.h> (getcontext/makecontext/swapcontext) was removed from POSIX in Issue 7; ucontext_t and mcontext_t are now defined by <signal.h> (CX). Additionally 18-1 is a byte-for-byte copy of 17-1 and never references mcontext_t.
  • Evidence: signal_h/17-1, 18-1 (both #include <ucontext.h> + static ucontext_t dummy;); signal.h.html: “shall define the mcontext_t type through typedef”, “shall define the ucontext_t type as a structure”.
  • Suggested action: switch to #include <signal.h> and make 18-1 use mcontext_t.

testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/definitions/signal_h/{2-3,21-1,22-30..22-35,35-1,36-1,37-1,40-1,44-1,45-1}-buildonly.c (openposix: conformance/definitions/signal_h/*)

  • Category: OBSOLETE
  • Confidence: high (21-1: medium, only the si_band part is affected)
  • Claim under test: <signal.h> defines SIG_HOLD (2-3), siginfo_t.si_band (21-1), POLL_IN/OUT/MSG/ ERR/PRI/HUP (22-30..22-35), and declares sighold (35), sigignore (36), siginterrupt (37), sigpause (40), sigrelse (44), sigset (45).
  • Problem: All of these were obsolescent in POSIX.1-2008 (XSI STREAMS / old signal API) and were removed in POSIX.1-2024 by Austin Group Defect 1330. The current <signal.h> lists neither SIG_HOLD, si_band, the POLL_* codes, nor these functions. The tests still pass on glibc (which keeps them, partly marked deprecated), but they assert requirements that no longer exist; a conforming Issue 8 libc may omit them and get a “compile FAILED”.
  • Evidence: https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9799919799/basedefs/signal.h.html (prototype list has no sighold/sigignore/siginterrupt/sigpause/sigrelse/sigset; only SIG_DFL/SIG_ERR/SIG_IGN; siginfo_t has no si_band; CHANGE HISTORY Issue 8: “Austin Group Defect 1330 is applied, removing obsolescent interfaces.”)
  • Suggested action: drop these buildonly tests (for 21-1 drop only the si_band line).

testcases/open_posix_testsuite/conformance/definitions/time_h/9-1-buildonly.c, 17-1-buildonly.c (openposix: conformance/definitions/time_h/9-1-buildonly, 17-1-buildonly)

  • Category: OBSOLETE

  • Problem: Both functions were obsolescent in POSIX.1-2008 and removed in POSIX.1-2024. glibc still declares them, so the tests pass, but they test a requirement that no longer exists.

  • Suggested action: drop both.

testcases/open_posix_testsuite/stress/threads/{fork/s-c1.c, fork/testfrmw.c, helper.c, pthread_cancel/stress.c, pthread_cancel/testfrmw.c, pthread_cond_init/s-c.c, pthread_cond_init/stress.c, pthread_cond_init/testfrmw.c, pthread_cond_timedwait/s-c.c}

In addition locate-test only picks stress files matching ’[0-9].c’, so stress.c, s-c.c and helper.c never get targets. logfile.stress-all lists only stress/mqueues and stress/signals. Their content would also be a poor fit for LTP: the stress.c samples loop forever until a signal (helper.c is the manual timeout wrapper), and s-c.c FAIL on a statistical latency-growth model, a performance property POSIX does not specify, after forking/creating threads until EAGAIN/ENOMEM. Small bugs too: fork/s-c1.c passes O_RDWR as the sem_open() mode, and its power-law model uses logl() where exp is meant; pthread_cond_init/s-c.c fills time_sav[4..7] incorrectly.

v4l user_space test_VIDIOC_*.c files: common problems

All remaining files in this directory (test_VIDIOC_AUDIO .. test_VIDIOC_EXT_CTRLS) are part of the 2009 “v4l-test” CUnit suite by Marton Nemeth imported into LTP. Common to all of them: - Not built by LTP: v4l/ is not in testcases/kernel/device-drivers/Makefile SUBDIRS, the stand-alone v4l/user_space/Makefile links -lcunit and is unaware of LTP’s build system; there is no runtest entry and no LTP result reporting (CUnit asserts only). git log shows only whitespace/style churn since import. - They encode the pre-3.1 V4L2 convention that an unimplemented ioctl returns EINVAL. Since v3.1 (commit 9190d191b1b8 “[media] v4l2 core: return -ENOTTY if an ioctl doesn’t exist”) the core returns ENOTTY: drivers/media/v4l2-core/v4l2-ioctl.c:3078,3117-3119 (ret = -ENOTTY; if (!is_valid_ioctl(vfd, cmd) ...) goto done;), documented in Documentation/userspace-api/media/gen-errors.rst:60 “ENOTTY The ioctl is not supported by the file descriptor.” Every “not supported” branch (CU_ASSERT_EQUAL(errno_x, EINVAL)) therefore fails on any device that lacks the ioctl (e.g. uvcvideo webcams lack audio, tuner, std and crop ioctls). - The *_NULL subtests require “ioctl not supported => NULL argument gives EINVAL”. The core copies the argument in before dispatch for _IOW/_IOWR ioctls (video_usercopy -> video_get_user, v4l2-ioctl.c:3437-3451, 3302-3304), so NULL yields EFAULT for them, and ENOTTY for _IOR ones; EINVAL is never the result. - Suggested action for all: drop testcases/kernel/device-drivers/v4l (and the usb tree). v4l2-compliance from v4l-utils is the maintained conformance suite and is used upstream with vivid/vimc in CI; if LTP wants V4L2 coverage it should be a new tst_test-based test on vivid. Per-file specifics follow.

DOCS: Inaccurate description, comments or metadata

The test logic is sound but what it says about itself (header comment, docparse block, runtest entry) is wrong or misleading. Action: fix the text only.

69 testcases. Sorted by path; confidence shown in each entry.

testcases/cve/sctphantom.c (runtest: cve/cve-2026-64564)

  • Category: DOCS (secondary: FRAGILE)
  • Confidence: high (phase 1: medium)
  • Claim under test: CVE-2026-64564 SCTP ASCONF DEL-IP UAF; fixed kernel answers the first DEL-IP with SCTP_ERROR_REQ_REFUSED (matches fix 9b2854f86f0b, net/sctp/sm_make_chunk.c sctp_process_asconf_param()).
  • Problem: The docparse says the sysctls exist only while the sctp module is loaded “so the test reports TCONF if it is not (run modprobe sctp first)”. The code instead calls tst_modprobe(“sctp”, NULL) unconditionally in setup, which runs tst_cmd(…, flags 0): any non-zero modprobe exit or a missing modprobe binary is TBROK (lib/tst_cmd.c:104-112), e.g. CONFIG_IP_SCTP=y on a system without /lib/modules/$(uname -r) or without kmod. The doc text is wrong and the environment case gives TBROK instead of TCONF.
  • Evidence: testcases/cve/sctphantom.c:45-49 vs :208; lib/tst_module.c:150-169; lib/tst_cmd.c:65-66,111-112.
  • Suggested action: use .needs_drivers = {"sctp", NULL} (handles built-in and loads modules) or pass TST_CMD_TCONF_ON_MISSING and tolerate failure; fix the doc paragraph accordingly.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): REVISED via RUN,READ. HPE, sctp not loaded: no modprobe in PATH -> tst_cmd returns 255 silently, then ‘tst_sys_conf.c:73: TCONF: Path not found: /proc/sys/net/sctp/addip_enable’. modprobe present but failing (-d empty dir, as without kernel-modules-extra) -> ‘tst_cmd.c:112: TBROK: modprobe exited with a non-zero code 1’ + CVE ‘may be vulnerable’ hints. Doc wrong; missing binary gives TCONF, not TBROK
  • Verification conclusion: The doc paragraph is wrong: setup() modprobes sctp itself (sysctls are saved only after that), so “run modprobe sctp first” is not needed. When modprobe runs and fails (e.g. Fedora without kernel-modules-extra) the result is TBROK with a misleading “may be vulnerable” hint. Phase 1 was wrong on one detail: a missing modprobe binary is silently ignored by tst_cmd() (returns 255) and ends in TCONF from the sysctl save. Suggested fix stands (.needs_drivers sctp, fix the doc). The exploit part was not run (not needed for a DOCS finding).

testcases/kernel/containers/pidns/pidns02.c (runtest: containers/pidns02)

  • Category: DOCS
  • Confidence: high (phase 1: medium)
  • Claim under test: “child session ID must be 1, parent process group ID must be 1”.
  • Problem: The code checks the child’s getsid(0)/getpgid(0) are 0 right after clone (session/pgrp leader lives in the ancestor ns, so pid_vnr() yields 0), then calls setsid() and checks both are 1. It never looks at a “parent process group ID”; the description omits the pre-setsid 0 checks and names the wrong process.
  • Evidence: pidns02.c:9-12 vs 18-25.
  • Suggested action: Reword: “before setsid() the child’s sid and pgid are 0 (not visible in the new ns); after setsid() both are 1”.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN,GIT,READ. HPE: pidns02 TPASS getsid(0)==0, getpgid(0)==0, then after setsid() getsid(0)==1, getpgid(0)==1 (all child-side); doc still says ‘parent process group ID must be 1’ and omits the pre-setsid 0 checks; wording inherited from 2007 version, 3fc912172c32 only fixed a flag name

testcases/kernel/controllers/cgroup_fj/cgroup_fj_function.sh (runtest: controllers/cgroup_fj_function_*)

HPE v2 (memory, cpu): test1 TCONF ‘Controller mounted on cgroup2…’ and test7 prints ‘…/ltp_1/tasks cannot be removed’ although task_list is cgroup.procs. Mutation removing test1’s v2 skip: ‘echo: write error: Device or resource busy … TBROK: echo PID > …/test-N/cgroup.procs failed’ = no-internal-process rule, not mv; comment copied from test2/3 in c35298b8c184

testcases/kernel/fs/fs_bind/bind/fs_bind23.sh (runtest: fs_bind/fs_bind23_sh)

It then mount --moves mnt into a shared tree tmp1 (peer tmp2) and checks that the moved subtree, including the nested abc mount, appears under the peer tmp2/3. It is a move-propagation test, not a “shared child to shared parent” bind. The description was copy-pasted in the original IBM test (which even printed “TEST24”).

HPE: fs_bind23 20 TPASS; key check is ‘mount –move mnt tmp1/3’ + ‘Check propagation tmp1/3/1/abc tmp2/3/1/abc tmp2/3/2/abc’ (move into shared parent). TINFO text identical to fs_bind01; git show 1d1937abbf83:…/bind/test23 already printed ‘TEST24’ + ‘bind: shared child to shared parent.’ -> copy-paste since 2008

HPE: fs_bind24 15 TPASS; body = rshared dir1, bind subdir to dir2, make-rslave/rshared/rslave dir1, then ‘Check propagation dir1/1/2/fs_bind_check/ dir4’ (master->slave). testcases/kernel/fs/fs_bind/cloneNS/fs_bind_cloneNS05.sh (runtest: fs_bind/fs_bind_cloneNS05_sh)

testcases/kernel/io/ltp-aiodio/aiocp.c (runtest: ltp-aiodio.part1 AD001..)

testcases/kernel/mem/hugetlb/hugemmap/hugemmap19.c (runtest: hugetlb/hugemmap19)

  • Category: DOCS
  • Confidence: high
  • Claim under test: Header says truncating at or above 4GB on 32-bit could truncate lower pages (prio_tree misconversion), with linux-git tag 856fc2950555 (“hugetlb: fix prio_tree unit”).
  • Problem: The code tests something else. It is the libhugetlbfs “misaligned_offset” test: map 2 hugepages, mprotect the first, try a MAP_FIXED mapping at a non-hugepage-aligned file offset, expect EINVAL, then check that the original mapping was not clobbered (bad pud/pmd backout). No truncation and no 4GB offset are involved. The in-code comment “First get arena of three hpages size, at file offset 4GB” (line 57) is also wrong: it maps 2 hpages at offset 0. The truncate-above-4GB scenario is actually tested by hugemmap36, which has the same header and tag.
  • Evidence: hugemmap19.c:8-18, 57-58, 82-96, 133-136; hugemmap36.c:8-15, 150-152.
  • Suggested action: Rewrite the description to describe the misaligned-offset MAP_FIXED backout check and remove or replace the 856fc2950555 tag.

No EACCES case exists. shm_id_1, the no-permission segment the header refers to, is created in setup() but never used by any test case (as root, IPC_STAT on it would succeed anyway).

testcases/kernel/mem/mtest06/mmap3.c (runtest: mm/mtest06_3)

  • Category: DOCS
  • Confidence: medium (phase 1: low)
  • Claim under test: threads repeatedly map/write/unmap files of random size “(maximum 1GB)”.
  • Problem: Code uses at most 1000*4096 bytes (~4MB) per file; the header says 1GB in one sentence and “upto 1000 times 4096” in the next. Also the SIGSEGV/SIGBUS handler only stores the signal and returns, so a real fault re-executes the faulting memset forever; the “Unexpected signal caught” TFAIL can never be printed and the failure surfaces only as a test timeout.
  • Evidence: mmap3.c:7-12, :46, :100-103, :123-128.
  • Suggested action: fix the description; make the SIGSEGV/SIGBUS handler report TFAIL and _exit (or longjmp) instead of returning.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN,MUTATION,READ. HPE: mtest06_3 ‘mmap3 -p’ TPASS. Mutation: thread 0 ftruncate(fd,0) before its memset -> SIGBUS, handler returns, fault repeats; no ‘Unexpected signal caught’ TFAIL ever printed, result ‘TBROK: Test killed! (timeout?)’ after the full runtime. Header: ‘(maximum 1GB)’ vs code (1+rand%1000)*4096 <= ~4 MB confirmed by reading

testcases/kernel/sched/cfs-scheduler/starvation.c (runtest: sched/starvation)

  • Category: DOCS (secondary: FRAGILE, UNDEF)
  • Confidence: high
  • Claim under test: a SIGUSR1 storm from a child pinned to the same CPU must not starve the parent (faulty kernels time out).
  • Problem: (1) Option help text is wrong: “-l Number of loops (default 2000000)” but loop = 1000000; “-t Max timeout (default 240s)” but the default is a calibrated value (callibrate()/1000, i.e. the microseconds for 120M empty loops reinterpreted as seconds). (2) The TFAIL criterion is “took longer than the calibrated runtime”, a wall-clock budget derived from an empty-loop calibration; on noisy VMs/steal time it can mis-fire, though the margin is usually large (low confidence). (3) loop is a plain static long decremented in the signal handler and polled by while (loop) sleep(1);; strictly UB per C (needs volatile sig_atomic_t), in practice the call to sleep() forces a reload.
  • Evidence: starvation.c:27, 31-54, 111-112, 120-124, 148-156, 166-167.
  • Suggested action: fix the option help strings (and document how the default runtime is derived); make loop volatile.

testcases/kernel/syscalls/epoll_ctl/epoll_ctl02.c (runtest: syscalls/epoll_ctl02)

  • Category: DOCS

  • Claim under test: epoll_ctl() errnos, including “EINVAL if events is NULL”.

The kernel copies the event with copy_from_user() before any other check and returns -EFAULT. Note also that epoll_ctl(2) does not list EFAULT at all (a man-pages gap), so the test depends on stable kernel behavior rather than on the man page.
  • Evidence: epoll_ctl02.c:15 (header bullet) vs :48 (tcase expects EFAULT); fs/eventpoll.c:2755-2757 SYSCALL_DEFINE4(epoll_ctl): if (ep_op_has_event(op) && copy_from_user(&epds, event, sizeof(struct epoll_event))) return -EFAULT;; epoll_ctl(2) ERRORS has no EFAULT entry.
  • Suggested action: change the bullet to “EFAULT if event is NULL”. Optionally report the missing EFAULT to man-pages.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN,READ. VIRT: 9 TPASS incl. ‘epoll_ctl(…) if events is NULL : EFAULT (14)’, while the docparse bullet (:15) says EINVAL. Kernel epoll_ctl() copy_from_user -> -EFAULT first (fs/eventpoll.c). epoll_ctl(2) ERRORS on Fedora 44 lists no EFAULT (man-pages gap).

testcases/kernel/syscalls/epoll_ctl/epoll_ctl04.c (runtest: syscalls/epoll_ctl04)

VIRT 7.2.10: ‘TPASS: … nesting is 5 : ELOOP (40)’, description still says EINVAL. e84f0689cf7a (2025) added ELOOP to accepted errnos (kernel f2e467a48287, 6.17) without updating the description. epoll_ctl(2) documents ELOOP for nesting depth > 5.

testcases/kernel/syscalls/eventfd/eventfd02.c (runtest: syscalls/eventfd02)

  • Category: DOCS
  • Confidence: high
  • Claim under test: write() to eventfd fails with “EAGAIN when counter is zero on non blocking fd”.

  • Category: DOCS

  • Claim under test: errno list incl. “ENOTDIR – the path contains a directory name which doesn’t exist” and “ENAMETOOLONG – greater than VFS_MAXNAMELEN”.

  • Evidence: execve03.c:14, :49-50, :75; execve(2) ERRORS: “ENOTDIR A component of the path prefix of pathname or of a script or ELF interpreter is not a directory.”

VIRT: 6 TPASS incl. ENOTDIR for ‘/fake/fake’ where fake is a regular file (path-prefix component not a directory, per execve(2)), not ‘directory name which doesn’t exist’ (that is ENOENT). VFS_MAXNAMELEN does not exist anywhere in /usr/src/linux; the 256-char component exceeds NAME_MAX.

The child gets the parent’s fd by fork(), so it shares the open file description, and the test expects the child’s LOCK_UN to SUCCEED (TPASS “File locked by parent unlocked”). This matches flock(2): locks belong to the open file description. Only the first sentence of the description is wrong; the rest of the paragraph matches the code.

Mutated copy with needskeyset=0 for case 02: ‘TFAIL: fsetxattr(2) on symlink passed unexpectedly’ -> EEXIST comes only from the pre-created key + XATTR_CREATE; fd from open(symlink) is the regular file. Description is misleading.

testcases/kernel/syscalls/mknod/mknod03.c (runtest: syscalls/mknod03)

  • Category: DOCS

The S_ISGID check was deliberately removed in fe002060deda (“mknod03: Skip S_ISGID check on files created by non-group members”), but the description was never updated.

testcases/kernel/syscalls/mknod/mknod08.c (runtest: syscalls/mknod08)

testcases/kernel/syscalls/modify_ldt/modify_ldt01.c (runtest: syscalls/modify_ldt01)

  • Category: DOCS (secondary: FRAGILE)
  • Confidence: medium
  • Claim under test: “Fails with EINVAL, when writing (func=1) to an invalid pointer”.
  • Problem: That case is {1, NULL, 0, EINVAL}. write_ldt() returns EINVAL because bytecount (0) != sizeof(struct user_desc), before it reads the pointer. A NULL pointer with the correct bytecount gives EFAULT. So this case checks the same condition as the next one (bytecount sizeof-1), and the description is wrong. Separately, the EFAULT case uses sbrk(0)+0xFFF as the “invalid” address. That address becomes valid if anything grows the heap with brk() after setup (glibc malloc from library or stdio code); tst_get_bad_addr() is the reliable choice. The {0, &buf, sizeof(buf)} case reads into the pointer variable buf, not the guarded buffer, which also looks unintended.
  • Evidence: modify_ldt01.c:13, 33-36, 61; arch/x86/kernel/ldt.c write_ldt(): error = -EINVAL; if (bytecount != sizeof(ldt_info)) goto out; error = -EFAULT; if (copy_from_user(...)).
  • Suggested action: reword it as “invalid bytecount (0)”, or add a real NULL-pointer/correct-size case that expects EFAULT. Use tst_get_bad_addr() for the read EFAULT case.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN,VIRT,READ. VIRT: ‘TCONF: This arch x86_64 is not supported’ (test is #ifdef i386 only, so it runs nowhere in this lab). arch/x86/kernel/ldt.c write_ldt(): ‘error = -EINVAL; if (bytecount != sizeof(ldt_info)) goto out;’ precedes copy_from_user -> {1, NULL, 0} is a bytecount check, not an invalid-pointer check; docs wrong. sbrk(0)+0xFFF EFAULT fragility holds by reading.
  • Verification (phase 3, glibc vs musl build and libc sources): UNCHANGED via MUSL,RUN. HPE glibc and musl: ‘TCONF: This arch x86_64 is not supported for test!’ (i386-only). Kernel write_ldt() ordering argument is libc-independent

testcases/kernel/syscalls/recvfrom/recvfrom01.c (runtest: syscalls/recvfrom01)

That holds because TCP does not report a source address (msg_namelen stays 0 and nothing is copied), but the case name and ENOTSOCK are misleading. Cases 6/7 call MSG_OOB/MSG_ERRQUEUE “invalid flags”, but they are valid flags that fail because there is no urgent data or the error queue is empty. recv01 and recvmsg01 have the same wording.

VIRT as-is 7 TPASS incl. ‘invalid socket buffer successful’: case 3 has retval 0 (src_addr=(void*)-1 on connected TCP succeeds), so its ENOTSOCK and name are unused/misleading; cases 6/7 ‘invalid MSG_OOB/MSG_ERRQUEUE flag’ get EINVAL/EAGAIN from empty urgent data / error queue, not invalid flags

testcases/kernel/syscalls/request_key/request_key02.c (runtest: syscalls/request_key02)

  • Category: DOCS (phase 1: WRONG)
  • Confidence: high (phase 1: medium)
  • Claim under test: request_key() fails with EKEYREVOKED when “a revoked key was found” and EKEYEXPIRED when “an expired key was found” (request_key(2) ERRORS).
  • Problem: For the revoked and expired cases, the test passes the revoked/expired key’s own serial as the dest_keyring argument (request_key("keyring", "ltp2", NULL, key2)). The syscall validates the destination keyring with lookup_user_key(…, KEY_LOOKUP_CREATE, KEY_NEED_WRITE) before any search, and key_validate() returns -EKEYREVOKED / -EKEYEXPIRED for that destination. The errno therefore comes from “invalid destination keyring”, and the documented search-path behaviour is never reached. A kernel whose search returned the wrong errno for a revoked or expired match would still pass.
  • Evidence: request_key02.c verify_request_key() (dest = *tc->id) and setup(); security/keys/keyctl.c:203-212 (dest lookup before key_type_lookup/request_key_and_link); security/keys/permission.c:102-119 (key_validate); request_key(2): “EKEYREVOKED A revoked key was found, but no replacement could be obtained.”
  • Suggested action: Pass dest_keyring 0 (or KEY_SPEC_THREAD_KEYRING) for all cases so the error comes from the search. Optionally keep the revoked-destination case as a separate, correctly described subcase.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): REVISED via RUN,MUTATION,READ,VIRT. VIRT as-is 3 TPASS. Mutant searching nonexistent descriptions with dest=revoked/expired key still gets EKEYREVOKED/EKEYEXPIRED -> errno from dest validation (confirmed). But mutant with dest=0 gets ENOKEY for both: request_key search skips expired keys (SKIP_EXPIRED) and ranks EKEYREVOKED below EAGAIN, so the suggested ‘dest 0’ fix would TFAIL on a correct kernel
  • Verification conclusion: Phase 1 is right that the errno comes from validating the destination keyring (mutant A), not from the search. Its suggested fix is wrong, though: on 7.2 the search path returns ENOKEY. request_key’s search uses KEYRING_SEARCH_SKIP_EXPIRED (request_key.c:593), and search_cred_keyrings_rcu ranks EKEYREVOKED below the EAGAIN from the other keyrings (process_keys.c:433), so request_key then reports ENOKEY. Corrected finding: the subcases really test “dest_keyring is revoked/expired”, which is valid kernel behaviour with a misleading description. Corrected action: rename them as such and keep the dest argument. Do not switch to dest 0. Optionally add a search case expecting ENOKEY.

testcases/kernel/syscalls/socket/socket01.c (runtest: syscalls/socket01)

  • Category: DOCS
  • Confidence: high

  • Problem: max_bytes is not an independent “limit set” value; it is computed on every read from max_ratio and the current global dirty threshold, so it is non-zero whenever max_ratio > 0 (default 100%). The “0 means no limit” wording is wrong; the check itself is harmless (min_ratio <= max_ratio is enforced, so min_bytes <= max_bytes for one threshold value).
  • Evidence: test lines 15-16, 53-59; /usr/src/linux/mm/page-writeback.c:661-671 bdi_get_bytes(), :766-769 bdi_get_max_bytes(); mm/backing-dev.c:393-400 max_bytes_show().
  • Suggested action: reword the description (max_bytes reflects max_ratio scaled by the current dirty threshold); the max_bytes > 0 guard can stay.
