Code raise()s SIGUSR2 and asserts it is pending (l.48-62) before sigwait(), so only the already-pending path is exercised; suspension is covered by sigwait/4-1 (alarm(3) then sigwait). Header text unchanged since 2002 import. Also l.82 message ‘is not pending!’ should read ‘still pending’.

testcases/open_posix_testsuite/functional/timers/timers/twoevtimers.c (openposix: functional/timers/timers/twoevtimers)

  • Category: DOCS (secondary: FRAGILE)
  • Confidence: high (phase 1: medium)
  • Claim under test: header: “two timers in different processes set to expire at the same time”.
  • Problem: The code creates both timers (SIGABRT, SIGALRM) in a single process, so the header is wrong (copied from twoptimers.c). Also sleep(EXPIREDELTA + 1) returns as soon as the first handler runs, so the check relies on the second signal already being pending at that point. On Linux both hrtimers with identical expiry fire in the same interrupt, so this normally holds, but it is not guaranteed. Counters are plain int, not volatile sig_atomic_t.
  • Evidence: twoevtimers.c header comment vs test_main; sleep(EXPIREDELTA + 1); followed by immediate check.
  • Suggested action: fix the description; loop on sleep/sigsuspend until both counters are set or a deadline passes.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): CONFIRMED via RUN,REPEAT,STRESS,VIRT,READ. Header says ‘two timers in different processes’; the code arms SIGABRT+SIGALRM timers in one process. All runs PASS (HPE 11/11 incl. 5 under stress, VIRT 6/6), so the secondary FRAGILE note (sleep returns after the first handler) was not reproduced. An untracked /usr/src/ltp/…/twoevtimers.c~ already holds a reworded header.

Refuted in verification (now OK)

Phase-1 findings that phase 2 or phase 3 showed to be wrong: the test’s check does fail when it should, or the claimed problem does not occur. Kept here for transparency; no action needed.

testcases/kernel/security/smack/smack_set_socket_labels.c (runtest: smack/smack_set_socket_labels)

  • Category: OK (phase 1: WRONG)
  • Confidence: high (phase 1: medium)
  • Claim under test: fsetxattr() of security.SMACK64IPIN/IPOUT on a UDP socket succeeds, unknown SMACK64IPNOT is rejected; TCONF when Smack is not active.
  • Problem: char buf[256] is never initialised and the return value of flistxattr(sock, buf, 256) is ignored (line 82). When Smack is not enabled, vfs_listxattr() on a sockfs inode writes nothing (sockfs has no ->listxattr, only security_inode_listsecurity contributes), so strstr(buf, ...) on line 83 reads stack garbage (UB) and the TCONF/continue decision is random. Even with Smack active, strstr only inspects the first NUL-terminated name in the list, so the check works by accident of ordering.
  • Evidence: test lines 76-84; /usr/src/linux/fs/xattr.c vfs_listxattr() (no i_op->listxattr for sockfs -> only LSM names); the actual assertions (lines 86-103) are correct per security/smack/smack_lsm.c smack_inode_setsecurity() which accepts only SMACK64/SMACK64IPIN/SMACK64IPOUT for sockets.
  • Suggested action: check flistxattr() return value (<=0 -> TCONF) and scan the returned list properly (iterate NUL-separated names up to the returned length); zero the buffer.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): REFUTED via RUN,VIRT,READ. VIRT: flistxattr() on a UDP socket with buf prefilled 0xAA returns 38 ‘[security.selinux] [system.sockprotoname]’: sockfs HAS ->listxattr (net/socket.c:646,693 sockfs_listxattr -> simple_xattr_list -> security_inode_listsecurity), so buf is always filled; Smack lists security.SMACK64 first. TCONF decision is deterministic; test TCONFs as-is.
  • Verification conclusion: Phase 1’s premise is wrong: sockfs does implement ->listxattr (net/socket.c:646 and :693, sockfs_listxattr -> simple_xattr_list -> security_inode_listsecurity, then always appends “system.sockprotoname”), so flistxattr() always fills buf. With Smack active, security.SMACK64 is the first name, and Smack and SELinux are exclusive, so the strstr() TCONF decision is deterministic. The unchecked return value and first-name-only strstr() are hygiene issues, not a test defect. Suggested report text: OK. Optional cleanup: check the flistxattr() return value.

testcases/kernel/syscalls/shmget/shmget05.c (runtest: syscalls/shmget05)

  • Category: OK (phase 1: WRONG)
  • Confidence: high
  • Claim under test: writing N to /proc/sys/kernel/shm_next_id makes the next shmget() return id N and resets shm_next_id to -1.
  • Problem: verify_shmget() removes the segment (SAFE_SHMCTL(shm_id, IPC_RMID), line 40) but leaves shm_id set to the stale id. cleanup() then calls SAFE_SHMCTL(shm_id, IPC_RMID) again (lines 52-53) because shm_id != -1; the kernel returns EINVAL for the removed id, and tst_brk in cleanup is converted to TWARN (lib/tst_test.c:408-418), so the test ends with a warning / non-zero exit on every run on a correct kernel. (Also shm_id is statically 0, not -1, so the guard is wrong even before the first iteration.)
  • Evidence: shmget05.c:26,40,52-53; lib/tst_safe_sysv_ipc.c:197-201; lib/tst_test.c:408-425.
  • Suggested action: set shm_id = -1 after IPC_RMID in verify_shmget() and initialise it to -1.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): REFUTED via RUN,MUTATION,READ. HPE: shmget05 TPASS, warnings 0 (also -i 3). Instrumented cleanup prints shm_id=-1: SAFE_SHMCTL macro sets its id arg to -1 on IPC_RMID (include/tst_safe_sysv_ipc.h:50-53), so no double RMID. Only nit: static 0 init means early tst_brk before shmget would RMID id 0
  • Verification conclusion: Phase 1 missed that SAFE_SHMCTL is a macro that assigns -1 to its shmid argument when cmd == IPC_RMID (include/tst_safe_sysv_ipc.h:50-53), so cleanup never repeats the RMID and no TWARN is produced. The only remaining nit (not worth a finding) is the static 0 initialisation: if SAFE_FILE_PRINTF breaks before the first shmget, cleanup does shmctl(0, IPC_RMID). Entry should be dropped / marked OK.

testcases/kernel/syscalls/shmget/shmget06.c (runtest: syscalls/shmget06)

  • Category: OK (phase 1: WRONG)
  • Confidence: high
  • Claim under test: when shm_next_id names an id already in use, shmget() returns a different id.

  • Evidence: shmget06.c:24,39,55-58; lib/tst_test.c:408-425.
  • Suggested action: set shm_id[1] = -1 after IPC_RMID; initialise both ids to -1.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): REFUTED via RUN,READ. HPE: shmget06 TPASS, warnings 0. Same as shmget05: SAFE_SHMCTL(shm_id[1], IPC_RMID) resets shm_id[1] to -1 (tst_safe_sysv_ipc.h:52), cleanup only removes shm_id[0]. Nit: zero-init ids only matter if setup breaks before shmget
  • Verification conclusion: Same as shmget05 (verified by instrumentation there): SAFE_SHMCTL(shm_id[1], IPC_RMID) resets shm_id[1] to -1, so cleanup only removes shm_id[0]; no TWARN on any run. Only nit: zero-initialised ids would matter only if setup broke before SAFE_SHMGET. Mark OK.

testcases/network/stress/route/route-change-netlink-dst.sh (runtest: net_stress.route route4-change-netlink-dst, route6-change-netlink-dst)

  • Category: OK (phase 1: WRONG)
  • Confidence: high
  • Claim under test: add/delete routes to several destinations via netlink (route-change-netlink binary).
  • Problem: setup builds ROUTE_CHANGE_NETLINK_PARAMS="-d $(tst_iface) -r '$rhost_all'"; route-lib.sh test_netlink runs $cmd $opt without eval, so word splitting passes the single quotes literally: -r "'10.23.4.1,...,10.23.0.1,'". strtok on ‘,’ yields “’10.23.4.1” and “’” which SAFE_GETADDRINFO cannot resolve -> TBROK in setup -> exit 2 -> test_netlink reports TFAIL. With libmnl present the test cannot pass; without libmnl it TCONFs, which likely hid the bug. Present since the test was added (553ca8ea3bc5).
  • Evidence: route-change-netlink-dst.sh:32; route-lib.sh:93,98 ($cmd $opt); route-change-netlink.c:74,123 (SAFE_GETADDRINFO on each item). Verified: opt="-r '1.2.3.4,5.6.7.8,'"; printf '<%s>\n' $opt prints <'1.2.3.4,5.6.7.8,'>; getaddrinfo(“’1.2.3.4”) -> EAI_NONAME.
  • Suggested action: drop the inner single quotes (the list has no spaces), or use eval in test_netlink.
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): REFUTED via RUN,READ. HPE: route-change-netlink-dst.sh and -6 both TPASS (‘routes created and deleted’, 10000 loops) with the literal quotes in argv (-r ‘10.23.4.1,…,’). Reason: strtok delim is TST_TO_STR(IP_ADDR_DELIM) where IP_ADDR_DELIM is ‘,’ -> string “‘,’”, so the quote char is also a delimiter and gets stripped.
  • Verification conclusion: The literal single quotes do reach argv, but route-change-netlink.c splits with strtok(item, TST_TO_STR(IP_ADDR_DELIM)) where #define IP_ADDR_DELIM ','; stringifying the char literal yields the string "','", so ' is itself a delimiter and the quotes are discarded. The test works (by accident). At most a cosmetic note: drop the inner quotes / define the delimiter as a string. No functional finding.

testcases/network/stress/route/route-change-netlink-if.sh (runtest: net_stress.route route4-change-netlink-if, route6-change-netlink-if)

  • Category: OK (phase 1: WRONG)
  • Confidence: high
  • Claim under test: switch route output interface via netlink across several ifaces/gateways.
  • Problem: same quoting bug as -dst: ROUTE_CHANGE_NETLINK_PARAMS="-d '$iface_all' -g '$gw_all' -r $rhost" passes literal quotes; save_iface() calls if_nametoindex(“’ltp_ns_veth…”) -> fails -> tst_brk(TBROK) -> shell reports TFAIL. The test can never pass when built with libmnl.
  • Evidence: route-change-netlink-if.sh:35; route-lib.sh:98; route-change-netlink.c:59-61,122.
  • Suggested action: remove the single quotes (or eval in test_netlink).
  • Verification (phase 2, run on real hosts): REFUTED via RUN,READ. HPE: route-change-netlink-if.sh TPASS as-is (also -gw TPASS). Same reason as -dst: route-change-netlink.c strtok delimiter TST_TO_STR(‘,’) expands to the 3-char string “‘,’” so literal single quotes from -d ‘…’ -g ‘…’ are treated as delimiters.
  • Verification conclusion: Same as -dst: the ' characters around the -d/-g lists are consumed as strtok delimiters (TST_TO_STR(‘,’) == “‘,’”), so if_nametoindex() gets clean names. Test passes on 7.2.
